meta.tagline: Fluência primeiro: do português como ponte ao inglês executivo, em blocos de 5.
meta.particularity: Fluência em primeiro lugar: você começa comunicando e ganha precisão como camada seguinte. O português apoia no início e cede lugar ao inglês de forma gradual. As aulas avançam em ciclos curtos, voltando sempre aos mesmos eixos — comunicação, negociação e o vocabulário técnico do seu projeto — para fixar com naturalidade.

overview: Um programa pensado para você falar inglês com confiança desde a primeira aula. A prioridade é a fluência: cumprimentar, perguntar, abrir uma reunião e se fazer entender — a porta de entrada para o domínio progressivo do idioma. No começo, o português é a ponte que acelera; com o tempo, o inglês assume o protagonismo. Todo o curso vive no seu dia a dia com o cliente, para que cada aula seja útil na mesma hora.
logic: Em entrevista, Fabrício traçou um perfil claro de aprendizagem: blocos curtos e repetitivos com retorno constante a cada eixo. Por isso cada 5 aulas seguem sempre o mesmo padrão: as duas primeiras são de comunicação interpessoal, as duas seguintes de negociação/números/contrato, e a quinta é a aula técnica do data center Google. O ciclo se repete 35 vezes ao longo do curso. Os 7 módulos do programa agrupam essas 35 repetições em fases temáticas — da fundação da comunicação executiva até o fechamento e a expansão de contrato. Até a aula 90 (primeira metade) os objetivos e explicações vêm em português; a partir da aula 91 a transição para o inglês é progressiva.

modules.name: FUNDAÇÃO DA COMUNICAÇÃO EXECUTIVA
modules.objective: Bloco de abertura que estabelece a comunicação executiva imediata — cumprimentar, apresentar-se, dizer números e datas em voz alta, abrir reunião e responder pelo cargo. Endereça a prioridade que Fabrício definiu em entrevista: comunicar-se com confiança em situações reais antes do aprofundamento estrutural. As 20 aulas constroem o vocabulário inicial executivo aplicado ao contexto Google, com apoio do português nas explicações. Bloco dos 5 — 4 repetições completas: duas aulas de interpessoal, duas de negociação/números, uma de técnico.

modules.name: CONHECER & APRESENTAR A RACIONAL AO GOOGLE
modules.objective: Capacitar Fabrício a apresentar a Racional ao Google — equipe, obras já entregues, valores expressivos, ciclo de obra, energia e resfriamento do data center. Endereça o primeiro pilar levantado em entrevista: estabelecer confiança apresentando os pontos fortes da Racional. As 30 aulas combinam português e inglês, com role-play de "first meeting com Google" e pitch curto da empresa em frases seguras.

modules.name: REUNIÕES COM O GOOGLE · CONDUZINDO E PARTICIPANDO
modules.objective: Aplicar o inglês nas reuniões reais com o Google — abertura, condução, pedindo a palavra, passando a palavra, recusa diplomática, quality control, commissioning e handover. Cobre também o small talk antes da reunião (viagem, família, comida, hobbies), peça-chave para construir vínculo com o cliente americano. 30 aulas, com o português ainda apoiando explicações de contexto.

modules.name: NEGOCIAÇÃO COM O GOOGLE — CUSTO, PRAZO, ESCOPO & CONTRATO
modules.objective: Coração do programa — negociação comercial com o Google em torno do data center. Cobre defesa de margem, mudança de escopo (change order), force majeure, contract clauses, BATNA, claims e tréplica. As 40 aulas cruzam a metade do curso (aula 90 marca a transição): o inglês passa a conduzir as aulas, com notas pontuais em português apenas quando agregam contexto. É também o módulo em que data hall, UPS, backup, cooling e segurança entram em profundidade.

modules.name: RELACIONAMENTO DE LONGO PRAZO & CONVERSAS DIFÍCEIS
modules.objective: Linguagem do relacionamento maduro com o Google — reconstrução depois de reunião tensa, conversas difíceis, apology language, multi-cultural meeting, code-switching, phone calls e video meetings. 30 aulas em inglês, com tópicos técnicos avançados (BIM, sustentabilidade, permits, subcontractor management) intercalados nas posições 5 do bloco.

modules.name: FECHAMENTO, ROI & EXPANSÃO DO PROGRAMA GOOGLE
modules.objective: Encerramento do projeto e abertura da próxima frente com o Google — end-of-project conversation, reference & referral, ROI conversation, renewal & expansion, master service agreement, strategic alignment de 3 anos. 25 aulas que consolidam o repertório executivo do Fabrício e preparam o terreno para os capstones.

modules.name: CAPSTONE — APRESENTAÇÕES FINAIS AO GOOGLE
modules.objective: Encerrar o curso com 3 apresentações conduzidas por Fabrício para o Google — espelhando os 3 eixos do bloco dos 5. Cada apresentação é precedida (quando aplicável) por uma aula de briefing e revisão de linguagem. Funcionam como avaliação aplicada e como demonstração concreta de domínio: Fabrício deixa o curso tendo conduzido em inglês os 3 cenários reais do dia a dia que ele descreveu em entrevista.

capstoneDetail.title: Apresentação 1 — Relationship pitch para o Google
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: primeira reunião de relacionamento com um novo interlocutor Google. Fabrício se apresenta, apresenta a Racional em frases curtas e seguras, conduz o small talk de abertura, faz perguntas sobre o projeto e fecha a conversa com agenda dos próximos passos. Foco em comunicação interpessoal — a prioridade número um identificada em entrevista.

capstoneDetail.title: Apresentação 2 — Negociação Google (custo, prazo, escopo)
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: rodada de negociação com o Google em torno de um contrato de data center. Fabrício fala números e prazos em voz alta com fluência, defende a posição da Racional, lida com mudança de escopo (change order) e sustenta tréplica simples na 2ª e 3ª troca da reunião.

capstoneDetail.title: Apresentação 3 — Technical handover do data center Google
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: entrega técnica do data center ao Google. Fabrício conduz a visita final pela obra, descreve em inglês os sistemas-chave (energia, cooling, racks, redundância), apresenta o relatório de qualidade e segurança e formaliza o handover.

lessons.title: Cumprimentos básicos: good morning / good afternoon / hi
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você cumprimenta uma pessoa do Google em qualquer horário do dia — good morning, good afternoon, good evening e o informal hi/hello — abrindo a conversa sem travar.
lessons.overview:
A greeting is the first thing you say in a meeting. It is small, but it is very important. A warm good morning opens the door. The client feels welcome. At Racional, you meet new people every week. Engineers, clients, partners. A simple greeting starts the relationship well.

The client here is Google. Google builds a data center with Racional. The team is from the United States. They say hi and hello a lot. They are friendly and direct. When you greet them in English, you show respect. You also show confidence. This is the goal of this lesson.

Racional is a strong company. More than 50 years of work. More than 620 projects. Big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. Every big project starts with a hello. Today you learn to open the room. Short words. Clear voice. A good start every time.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fixar três frases-âncora simples: "Good morning, everyone." para abrir uma reunião de manhã, "Welcome." para receber o cliente e "Let's start." para começar.

Repita em voz alta. O importante é falar com naturalidade, não acertar tudo. Você só precisa de poucas palavras para abrir bem.
lessons.situation: Você chega cedo na reunião com o time do Google no canteiro do data center. Você cumprimenta todos e abre o encontro.
lessons.context: It is 8 a.m. on site. The Google team arrives. You smile and say: "Good morning, everyone. Welcome." They answer: "Hi! Nice to see you." You say: "It's great to see you. Let's start." The meeting begins well.

vocab.example: It's great to see you today.

vocab.pt: que bom ver você de novo

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o cumprimento ao horário do dia
exercises.explanation: Use cada cumprimento no horário certo. "Welcome" serve para receber o cliente a qualquer hora.

exercises.title: 2. Você abre a reunião das 8h. O que você diz?
exercises.prompt: O time do Google chega de manhã no canteiro. Qual frase abre bem?

options.whyWrong: "Good evening" é para a noite. De manhã, use "good morning".
"Good afternoon" é para a tarde. Às 8h da manhã, use "good morning".

exercises.title: 3. Complete o cumprimento
exercises.prompt: Good ___, everyone. Welcome.
exercises.explanation: "Good morning/afternoon/evening" + "everyone" abre a reunião com o time todo.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua abertura de reunião
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas para abrir uma reunião de manhã com o Google. Use pelo menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: good morning, welcome, let's start).
exercises.modelAnswer: Good morning, everyone. Welcome. It's great to see you. Let's start.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos da aula. Frases curtas bastam.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta a abertura
exercises.targetText: Good morning, everyone. Welcome. Let's start.
exercises.translation: Bom dia, pessoal. Bem-vindos. Vamos começar.
exercises.prompt: Imagine o time do Google na sua frente, de manhã. Diga essa abertura com voz clara e calma.
exercises.explanation: Fale devagar. O objetivo é soar natural e seguro, não rápido.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, abra uma reunião de manhã com o time do Google: cumprimente, dê as boas-vindas e diga que vai começar. Use "good morning", "welcome" e "let's start".
takeaways: I can say good morning, good afternoon, and good evening.
I can say hi and hello to the Google team.
I can welcome the client to a meeting.
I can open a meeting with simple words.

pill.sample: I'm gonna grab a coffee, and then we can talk.

lessons.title: "My name is..." — apresentando-se a alguém do Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você se apresenta a alguém do Google — diz seu nome, seu cargo e onde trabalha — usando "My name is...", "I'm..." e "I work for..." sem travar.
lessons.overview:
After the greeting comes the introduction. You say who you are. "My name is Fabrício. I work for Racional." This is short and clear. The client now knows your name and your company. A good introduction builds trust in seconds.

You are the Contracts Superintendent at Racional. This is a big role. You talk to clients, partners, and your team every day. With Google, you represent the whole company. When you say "I work for Racional", you carry 50 years of work in those words.

Racional builds for top clients — Microsoft, Amazon, and now Google. The Google team meets many people on site. Your name and your role help them remember you. A clear introduction opens the door for the next meeting. Today you learn to say it well.
lessons.intro:
As frases-âncora desta aula são três: "My name is Fabrício.", "I work for Racional." e "I'm responsible for contracts."

Depois de ouvir o nome da outra pessoa, responda com "Nice to meet you.". São poucas palavras, muito repetíveis.
lessons.situation: Você encontra um gerente do Google pela primeira vez no canteiro. Vocês trocam nomes e cargos.
lessons.context: A Google manager comes to you. You say: "Hi. My name is Fabrício. I work for Racional. I'm responsible for contracts." He says: "Nice to meet you. I'm John." You answer: "Nice to meet you, John."

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: My name is Fabrício. I work for Racional.
exercises.explanation: Frase de apresentação simples: nome + empresa. Escreva exatamente o que ouvir.

exercises.title: 2. Coloque as palavras na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: A ordem é: sujeito (I) + verbo (work) + for + empresa. "I work for Racional."

exercises.title: 3. Complete a apresentação
exercises.prompt: My ___ is Fabrício. I work for Racional.
exercises.explanation: "My name is..." é a forma mais comum de dizer seu nome.

exercises.title: 4. O gerente do Google diz o nome dele. Como você responde?
exercises.prompt: Ele diz: "I'm John." Qual a melhor resposta?

options.whyWrong: "Good evening" é um cumprimento de noite, não uma resposta a uma apresentação.
"Let's start" abre uma reunião, mas não responde a uma apresentação. Use "Nice to meet you".

exercises.title: 5. Leia sua apresentação em voz alta
exercises.targetText: My name is Fabrício. I work for Racional. Nice to meet you.
exercises.translation: Meu nome é Fabrício. Trabalho na Racional. Prazer em conhecê-lo.
exercises.prompt: Você encontra um gerente do Google pela primeira vez. Apresente-se com voz calma e clara.
exercises.explanation: Diga seu nome devagar. O cliente precisa ouvir e lembrar.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, apresente-se a um gerente do Google: diga seu nome, sua empresa e seu cargo. Use "My name is...", "I work for..." e "I'm responsible for contracts."
takeaways: I can say my name with "My name is...".
I can say I work for Racional.
I can say nice to meet you.
I can introduce myself to the Google team.

lessons.title: Números de 0 a 10 em voz alta (drill de pronúncia)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz os números de 0 a 10 em inglês em voz alta, com pronúncia clara — a base para falar quantidades, prazos e, mais à frente, valores com o Google.
lessons.overview:
Numbers are everywhere in your day. How many teams? How many days? Numbers from zero to ten are the first step. You use them all the time. To count people on site. To count weeks. To count meetings with the client.

At Racional, numbers tell the story. More than 620 projects. More than 10 million square meters. With Google, you will talk about teams, days, and deliveries. Saying small numbers in clear English helps you sound confident. The client understands you fast.

This lesson is a pronunciation drill. You say the numbers out loud, again and again. Zero, one, two, three. Slow and clear. Soon, numbers come easy. Later, you will use them for dates and for contract talks. The base starts today.
lessons.intro:
O alvo da aula são os números zero a ten. Diga-os em voz alta, em sequência e fora de ordem.

Use também a pergunta-âncora "How many?" e a resposta "We have ___ on site." (Temos ___ no canteiro.)
lessons.situation: No canteiro do Google, alguém pergunta quantas equipes estão trabalhando. Você responde com um número.
lessons.context: A Google engineer asks: "How many teams on site today?" You count and say: "We have six teams on site." She asks: "And how many cranes?" You say: "We have three. In total, nine machines."

vocab.example: We have six teams on site.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o número ao algarismo
exercises.explanation: Memorize a forma escrita de cada número. Diga em voz alta enquanto liga.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva uma resposta com números
exercises.prompt: Responda à pergunta "How many teams on site?". Escreva 2 frases curtas usando pelo menos 2 números da aula por extenso (ex.: six, three, nine).
exercises.modelAnswer: We have six teams on site. We have three cranes. In total, nine machines.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos números e termos da aula.

exercises.title: 3. Qual número é "nine"?
exercises.prompt: O engenheiro diz "nine machines". Quantas máquinas?

options.whyWrong: 5 é "five". "Nine" é 9.
10 é "ten". "Nine" é 9.

exercises.title: 4. Coloque a frase na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: A ordem natural é: "We have six teams on site." Sujeito + verbo + número + substantivo + lugar.

exercises.title: 5. Conte de zero a dez em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Zero, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
exercises.translation: Zero, um, dois, três, quatro, cinco, seis, sete, oito, nove, dez.
exercises.prompt: Diga os números devagar e com clareza, como se contasse equipes no canteiro do Google.
exercises.explanation: Foque na pronúncia clara de "three", "five" e "nine". Repita até soar natural.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, conte de zero a dez e depois responda "How many teams on site?" com um número. Use "We have ___ on site." e "In total, ___."
takeaways: I can say the numbers from zero to ten.
I can ask "How many?".
I can answer with a number on site.
I can count teams and machines in English.

lessons.title: "How many?" — perguntas curtas com números
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz e responde perguntas curtas com números — "How many days?", "How much time?" — para trocar quantidades com o Google na hora, sem travar.
lessons.overview:
Now you join numbers with a question. How many? asks about count. How many teams? How many days? How much? asks about amount. How much time? These two questions are very useful on site every day.

With Google, time and count are key. The client wants clear answers. "How many days for this floor?" You answer: "About four days." Short and direct. Words like about and around help when you are not 100% sure.

At Racional, you manage contracts and schedules. Fast, clear answers build trust with the client. When the Google team asks a number, you reply right away. This lesson gives you the short questions and the short answers you need.
lessons.intro:
As âncoras desta aula são duas perguntas: "How many days?" e "How much time?".

Para responder sem se comprometer demais, use "about" ou "around" (mais ou menos): "About four days."
lessons.situation: O time do Google quer saber prazos no canteiro. Você troca quantidades em perguntas e respostas rápidas.
lessons.context: A Google manager asks: "How many days for this floor?" You say: "About four days." He asks: "How much time for the whole area?" You say: "Around two weeks. We need more people."

vocab.example: How many days for this floor?
How much time for the area?
We have six teams right now.

exercises.title: 1. O gerente quer saber o prazo. Qual pergunta usar?
exercises.prompt: Você quer perguntar quantos dias para esse andar. O que você diz?

options.text: How many days for this floor?
How much days for this floor?
options.whyWrong: Com "days" (contável, no plural) use "how many", não "how much".

options.text: How are days for this floor?
options.whyWrong: "How are" pergunta como alguém está. Para quantidade de dias, use "how many days".

exercises.title: 2. Ligue a pergunta à resposta
exercises.explanation: "How many" + resposta com número de dias/semanas. "How much time" + resposta com período.

exercises.title: 3. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: How many days for this floor?
exercises.explanation: Pergunta curta de prazo. "How many days" + "for" + lugar.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva uma pergunta e uma resposta
exercises.prompt: Escreva uma pergunta sobre prazo e a sua resposta, como na conversa com o Google. Use pelo menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: how many days, about, around, we need).
exercises.modelAnswer: How many days for this floor? About four days. We need more people.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos da aula.

exercises.title: 5. Leia a troca em voz alta
exercises.targetText: How many days for this floor? About four days.
exercises.translation: Quantos dias para este andar? Cerca de quatro dias.
exercises.prompt: Você responde a um gerente do Google que quer saber o prazo. Faça a pergunta e dê a resposta com voz firme.
exercises.explanation: Use "about" para dar uma estimativa sem se comprometer com um número exato.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, simule a troca com o Google: pergunte um prazo e responda com uma estimativa. Use "How many days?", "about" ou "around" e "We need more people."
takeaways: I can ask "How many days?".
I can ask "How much time?".
I can answer with about or around.
I can talk about time and count with Google.

lessons.title: O que é um data center? — vocabulário introdutório
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica, com vocabulário introdutório, o que é um data center e por que o Google constrói tantos — conectando o seu dia a dia de obra ao negócio do cliente.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a big building full of computers. The computers are called servers. They store and process data. Your photos, your e-mails, your maps — they live in a data center. It is the home of the cloud.

Google builds many data centers around the world. They need a lot of power and a lot of cooling. The servers are hot, so the building must stay cool. The data center runs 24/7 — every day, all the time. It must be safe and never stop.

This is your project with Racional. You build the facility for Google. You know the building, the structure, the systems. Now you learn the words in English. When you say server, rack, power, and cooling, the Google team sees that you understand their business. This builds a strong partnership.
lessons.intro:
Os termos-âncora desta aula são quatro: data center, server, power e cooling.

Use a frase simples "A data center stores data." e "It runs 24/7." (funciona o tempo todo) para explicar o tema em poucas palavras.
lessons.situation: Em uma visita ao canteiro, alguém do Google comenta sobre o prédio. Você mostra que entende o que é um data center.
lessons.context: You walk on site with the Google team. You point to the building and say: "This is the data center. It stores data. The servers run 24/7. They need power and cooling. We keep them safe."

vocab.example: It needs a lot of power.
Your photos live in the cloud.

exercises.title: 1. Coloque a frase na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: A ordem natural é: "A data center stores data." Sujeito + verbo + objeto.

exercises.title: 2. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: The servers need power and ___.
exercises.explanation: Servidores esquentam, por isso precisam de "cooling" (resfriamento) além de "power" (energia).

exercises.title: 3. O que um data center faz?
exercises.prompt: Você explica ao time do Google. Qual frase está certa?

options.whyWrong: Um data center não vende carros. Ele armazena e processa dados (data).
Um data center não cozinha. Ele guarda dados (data) em servidores.

exercises.title: 4. Ligue o termo ao significado
exercises.explanation: Estes são os termos básicos de um data center. Diga cada um em voz alta.

exercises.title: 5. Explique o que é um data center
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 a 3 frases curtas explicando o que é um data center, como você diria ao Google. Use pelo menos 3 termos da aula (ex.: data center, server, store, power, cooling).
exercises.modelAnswer: This is a data center. It stores data. The servers run 24/7. They need power and cooling.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos da aula.

exercises.targetText: This is a data center. It stores data. It runs 24/7.
exercises.translation: Isto é um data center. Ele armazena dados. Funciona o tempo todo.
exercises.prompt: Você mostra o prédio ao time do Google. Explique o que é um data center com voz clara.
exercises.explanation: Frases curtas e diretas. Você mostra que entende o negócio do cliente.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, explique ao time do Google o que é um data center: o que ele faz e do que precisa. Use "It stores data.", "power", "cooling" e "24/7".
takeaways: I can say what a data center is.
I can say it stores and processes data.
I can say it needs power and cooling.
I can use server, rack, and the cloud.
I can explain the project to the Google team.

lessons.title: "How are you?" — respondendo e devolvendo a pergunta
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você responde "How are you?" com naturalidade e devolve a pergunta com "And you?", mantendo os primeiros segundos de conversa com o Google leves e simpáticos.
lessons.overview:
"How are you?" is a small question with a big job. It opens a conversation. It is not really about your health. It is a friendly way to start. People say it every day, before any business talk. With Google, this is the warm first step.

The answer is simple. "I'm fine, thank you." Or "Very well, thanks." Then you give the question back: "And you?" This makes the talk feel equal and friendly. It shows you care. It is good small talk.

At Racional, relationships matter as much as the work. Before a meeting about contracts or the data center, you have a few seconds of small talk. A warm "How are you?" and a kind answer set a good tone. Today you learn to keep these first seconds light and natural.
lessons.intro:
As âncoras desta aula são a pergunta "How are you?", a resposta "I'm fine, thank you." e a devolução "And you?".

Alternativas simples para a resposta: "Very well, thanks." e "Not bad.". Sempre devolva a pergunta para manter a conversa.
lessons.situation: Você cruza com um gerente do Google antes da reunião. Vocês trocam alguns segundos de conversa leve.
lessons.context: Before the meeting, a Google manager says: "Hi, Fabrício. How are you?" You answer: "I'm fine, thank you. And you?" He says: "Very well, thanks. Busy day today!" You smile: "Me too. Let's start."

vocab.example: Have a good day. You too.

exercises.explanation: Resposta padrão a "How are you?": diga que está bem e devolva a pergunta.

exercises.title: 3. Ligue a expressão ao significado
exercises.explanation: Respostas simples para "How are you?" e a devolução da pergunta.

exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos da aula.

exercises.translation: Estou bem, obrigado. E você?
exercises.prompt: Um gerente do Google pergunta como você está antes da reunião. Responda e devolva a pergunta com simpatia.
exercises.explanation: Sorria ao falar. A devolução "And you?" mantém a conversa leve e equilibrada.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, simule o small talk antes da reunião com o Google: responda "How are you?", devolva a pergunta e diga uma palavra sobre o dia. Use "I'm fine, thank you.", "And you?" e "busy".

I can say "I'm fine, thank you.".
I can give the question back with "And you?".

lessons.title: "Nice to meet you" — primeira reunião com o Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você se apresenta e cumprimenta na primeira reunião com o Google usando "Nice to meet you", "I'm Fabrício" e "This is...", com frases curtas e seguras.
lessons.overview:
The first meeting sets the tone for the whole project. When you meet the Google team for the first time, the first words matter. A clear introduction shows respect and confidence. You do not need long sentences. You need short, warm phrases.

At Racional, you meet many clients. Now the client is Google, and the project is a data center. Google is a North American company, so the first meeting will be in English. "Nice to meet you" is the key phrase. It is simple, polite, and it works every time.

In this lesson you learn to say your name, to present the team, and to thank your host. These small phrases open the door. They make the Google team feel welcome and they make you sound professional from the first second.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fixar três frases-âncora para a primeira reunião: "Nice to meet you." (Prazer em conhecê-lo), "I'm Fabrício." (Eu sou o Fabrício) e "This is..." para apresentar alguém do time.

Responda ao cumprimento com "Nice to meet you too." — basta acrescentar "too" (também).

lessons.context: Hello. I'm Fabrício. Nice to meet you. This is my team. Thank you for having us. It is a pleasure.

lessons.title: Números de 10 a 100 — dezenas e centenas
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz e entende números de 10 a 100 — dezenas e centenas — para falar de prazos, equipes e porcentagens com o Google.
lessons.overview:
Numbers are everywhere in your work. You talk about workers on site, deadlines, square meters, and percent. In a meeting with Google, you need to say these numbers clearly and with confidence.

At Racional, the company has more than 50 years and 620 projects. The data center for Google is big. You will say things like "about two hundred workers" or "thirty days". Small mistakes with numbers can cause big problems, so clear numbers are very important.

This lesson trains the tens and the hundreds: twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, and one hundred. Be careful with thirteen and thirty — they sound close but they are very different. Say them slowly and the Google team will understand you well.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fixar a forma de falar números grandes com segurança: "about thirty workers" (cerca de trinta trabalhadores) e "the deadline is sixty days" (o prazo é sessenta dias).

Cuidado com o par que confunde: thirteen (13) tem som no fim; thirty (30) é mais curto.

lessons.context: We have about fifty workers on site. The deadline is thirty days. That is ninety percent.

vocab.example: The meeting is in fifteen minutes.

exercises.explanation: "One hundred percent" = cem por cento.

Three é 3, não 30.

exercises.explanation: Diga "fifty" com clareza para não confundir com "fifteen".

takeaways: I can say numbers from ten to one hundred.
I can say "about fifty workers".

lessons.title: "What time?" — falando horas básicas em voz alta
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz horas básicas em voz alta e marca um horário com o Google usando "at ten", "half past" e "Let's meet at...".
lessons.overview:
Time is part of every business day. You schedule a call, you set the meeting, and you confirm a time. With a North American client like Google, clear time words avoid confusion and show that you are organized.

At Racional, the data center project has many calls every week — with Google, with suppliers, and with your own team. You need to say "at ten o'clock" or "half past two" with no doubt. Time is money on a construction site.

This lesson gives you simple time phrases: o'clock, half past, a quarter past, and a quarter to. You also learn to propose a time and ask "Does that work for you?". These small phrases keep the project moving.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fixar como propor e confirmar horário: "Let's meet at ten." (Vamos nos encontrar às dez) e "Does that work for you?" (Funciona para você?).

Lembre: half past = e meia; a quarter past = e quinze; a quarter to = quinze para.

lessons.title: Google: a empresa e por que ela constrói data centers
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, com frases simples, sobre o que é o Google e por que ele constrói data centers — base para conversar com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Google is a big technology company. It works with the internet, with search, and with many services. Billions of users use Google every day, all around the world.

To run all these services, Google needs many computers. The computers stay in big buildings called data centers. That is why Google builds data centers, and that is why Racional is here. Racional already builds for clients like Microsoft and Amazon, so this project fits the company very well.

When you understand the client, you talk better with the client. Google grows fast and needs more computers all the time. The data center you build will hold these machines. This lesson gives you simple words to explain the why behind the project — useful in any meeting.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fixar a ideia central em frases simples: "Google is a technology company." e "Google needs data centers."

E a frase que liga causa e efeito: "That is why we are here." (É por isso que estamos aqui).

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz de onde é, onde trabalha e qual é o seu cargo, usando "I am from Brazil", "I work at Racional" e "I am a contracts manager".
lessons.overview:
In every first conversation, people want to know two things: where you are from and what you do. With simple phrases like "I am from Brazil" and "I work at Racional", you answer both in seconds. These are the building blocks of any introduction.

At Racional, you are the contracts manager for the Google project. You can say "I am responsible for contracts" or "my role is contracts". Racional is a construction company from Brazil, with headquarters in São Paulo. The Google team will want to know this.

This lesson also gives you the question back: "Where are you from?" and "Where do you work?". A good conversation goes both ways. You answer, and then you ask. This keeps the meeting warm and human.

Vamos fixar três respostas-âncora: "I am from Brazil." (Sou do Brasil), "I work at Racional." (Trabalho na Racional) e "I am the contracts manager." (Sou o gerente/superintendente de contratos).

Devolva a pergunta: "Where are you from?" e "Where do you work?".

lessons.title: "Excuse me / Sorry" — fórmulas de cortesia em reunião
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa fórmulas de cortesia em reunião — "Excuse me", "Sorry", "Could you repeat, please?" — para pedir, interromper e tirar dúvida com educação.
lessons.overview:
Polite words make a meeting smooth. When you do not understand, you say "Could you repeat, please?". When you want to speak, you say "Sorry to interrupt". These small phrases keep the conversation calm and respectful, even when English is hard.

For a non-native speaker, these phrases are gold. In a meeting with Google, you will not understand everything — and that is normal. The key is to ask. "Could you repeat that, please?" or "More slowly, please." are not signs of weakness. They show care and professionalism.

At Racional, clear communication avoids mistakes on site and in contracts. The same is true in English. With these courtesy formulas, you stay in control of the meeting. You ask questions, you check details, and you never lose the thread.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fixar as fórmulas de cortesia mais úteis: "Excuse me." (Com licença), "Sorry." (Desculpe) e "Could you repeat, please?" (Pode repetir, por favor?).

Para entrar na conversa: "Sorry to interrupt." e para pedir calma: "More slowly, please.".
lessons.situation: Durante a reunião com o Google, alguém fala rápido e você precisa pedir, com educação, que repita mais devagar.
lessons.context: Excuse me. Sorry to interrupt. Could you repeat that, please? More slowly, please. Thank you.

lessons.title: Dias da semana — Monday, Tuesday...
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz os sete dias da semana em inglês, em voz alta, e marca uma reunião com o Google dizendo o dia certo.
lessons.overview:
Every week, the team at Racional plans new meetings. We talk to clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. To plan a meeting, we need the days of the week. This is a simple tool, but it is very important for an executive.

For the Google data center project, Fabrício meets the client often. He sets a day for the site visit. He sets a day for the report. A clear day is a clear plan. When you say the right day, the client trusts you.

The seven days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. In English, each day starts with a big letter. We use the small word on before a day: "on Monday", "on Friday". This lesson helps you plan your week with Google in English.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: "Let's meet on Tuesday" (vamos nos encontrar na terça), "Does that work?" (isso funciona para você?) e "See you on Friday" (te vejo na sexta).

Lembre da palavrinha on antes do dia, e que cada dia começa com letra maiúscula.
lessons.situation: O time do Google quer marcar a próxima reunião de obra. Eles perguntam qual dia funciona para você, e você responde na hora, com o dia certo.
lessons.context: Let's meet on Tuesday. Wednesday is busy for me. Friday is free. So, Tuesday morning? Great. See you on Tuesday.

exercises.explanation: Para dias da semana, usamos 'on': on Monday, on Wednesday, on Friday.

exercises.explanation: Curto e claro vale mais que longo e perfeito. O importante é marcar o dia.

takeaways: I can say the seven days of the week.
I can use 'on' before a day, like 'on Tuesday'.

lessons.title: Meses e datas — "May 28th, 2026"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz os meses do ano e fala uma data completa em inglês, no formato americano — por exemplo, "May 28th, 2026" — para confirmar prazos com o Google.
lessons.overview:
In a contract, the deadline is everything. Racional has more than 620 projects in 50 years. Every project has a date to start and a date to finish. The team always knows the dates. For Google, dates are very important too.

The Google data center has many steps. There is a milestone in one month. There is a handover in another month. Fabrício must say these dates in English. The American client says the month first, then the day, then the year. For example: May 28th, 2026.

The months are January, February, March, April, May, and June — and six more. The day is an ordinal number, like twenty-eighth (28th). The year 2026 is "twenty twenty-six". When you say the date well, you confirm the plan with the client.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe duas frases-âncora: "The deadline is on May 28th" (o prazo é 28 de maio) e "Let's confirm the date" (vamos confirmar a data).

Lembre da ordem americana: mês + dia + ano. Use in para o mês (in June) e on para o dia (on May 28th).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com o Google, vocês definem a data de entrega de uma etapa da obra. Você precisa dizer e confirmar a data completa, no formato que o cliente americano entende.

commonErrors.at: 'At' é para horas, não para datas. Use 'on May 28th'.

takeaways: I can say the months of the year.
I can say a full date, like 'May 28th, 2026'.
I can use 'in' for a month and 'on' for a day.

lessons.title: Hyperscale data center — o tipo que o Google constrói
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica, com vocabulário simples, o que é um hyperscale data center — o tipo gigante que o Google constrói — e usa quatro ou cinco palavras técnicas para falar a língua do cliente.
lessons.overview:
Google does not build a small data center. Google builds a hyperscale data center. This is the giant type. It is built to grow big and grow fast. When you know this word, you are already inside the client's world.

A hyperscale data center is very large. It has many buildings on one site. It needs a lot of power — many megawatts. It needs strong infrastructure. Racional builds large projects: more than 10 million square meters in 50 years. So Racional knows scale. Now Fabrício learns to talk about it in English.

The key words today are scale (size), capacity, infrastructure, to expand (to grow), and megawatt (the power unit). You do not need to explain everything. One short, correct sentence — "This is a hyperscale data center" — shows Google that you speak their language.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe duas frases-âncora: "This is a hyperscale data center" (este é um data center de hiperescala) e "We can expand the capacity" (podemos expandir a capacidade).

Não precisa explicar tudo. Uma frase curta e correta já mostra ao Google que você entende a escala.

lessons.title: "This is..." — apresentando outras pessoas em reunião
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta outras pessoas em uma reunião com o Google, usando "This is..." e dizendo o cargo de cada um.
lessons.overview:
In a meeting, the leader makes the team look strong. Fabrício is the Superintendent of Contracts at Racional. He brings his team to the table with Google. He must introduce each person in English. A good introduction builds trust on the first day.

The simple phrase is "This is...". You say the name and the role: "This is Ana. She is our project manager." Or: "This is Carlos. He is our safety engineer." For two or more people, you say "These are...". It is short and very clear.

Racional works with big clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. In every meeting, the team has many roles: a project manager, a safety engineer, and more. When you introduce your colleague with a clear role, the client knows who does what. This makes the work easy from the start.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: "This is Ana" (esta é a Ana), "She is our project manager" (ela é nossa gerente de projeto) e "He is responsible for safety" (ele é responsável pela segurança).

Lembre: This is para uma pessoa, These are para duas ou mais.

lessons.title: "Could you repeat?" — pedindo para repetir sem se constranger
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pede para o cliente repetir ou falar devagar, em inglês, com calma e sem se constranger.
lessons.overview:
In a real meeting, you do not understand every word. This is normal. Every executive has this moment. The strong move is simple: you ask the person to repeat. You say "Could you repeat?" or "Could you speak slowly?". This is not weak. It is professional.

The team at Google speaks fast and uses many terms. When Fabrício does not catch a word, he asks again. A good question keeps the meeting clear. "Sorry, could you repeat?" saves time. It is better to ask now than to make a mistake in a contract later.

Today you learn calm, polite phrases: "I didn't catch that", "could you speak slowly?", and "could you write it down?". With these words, you stay in control of the conversation. You show Google that you care about every detail of the data center project.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: "Could you repeat?" (pode repetir?), "Could you speak slowly?" (pode falar devagar?) e "Now I understand" (agora eu entendi).

Pedir para repetir é sinal de profissionalismo, não de fraqueza. Diga com calma e um "please".
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com o Google, o cliente fala rápido e você não entende uma parte. Você precisa pedir para repetir, de forma educada, sem perder a postura.
lessons.context: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you repeat, please? Could you speak slowly? Thank you. Now I understand.

lessons.title: Verbo TO BE — am / is / are no dia a dia
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa o verbo TO BE (am / is / are) para falar de você, da sua equipe e do andamento da obra com o Google.
lessons.overview:
The verb to be is the most important verb in English. You use it all the time. You say "I am", "he is", "she is", "we are", and "they are". With this one verb, you can say who you are and how the project is going.

For Fabrício, the verb to be opens many doors. "I am the Superintendent of Contracts." "We are ready." "The project is on schedule." These are strong, clear sentences for a meeting with Google. The client wants to hear that the work is on track.

In daily talk, you often use the short form: "I'm", "we're", "it's". You can say "I am available" or "We are on schedule." When you control the verb to be, you can answer almost any simple question at the table with Racional's biggest clients.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: "I am responsible for contracts" (sou responsável pelos contratos), "We are on schedule" (estamos no prazo) e "The team is ready" (a equipe está pronta).

Lembre: I am, he/she/it is, we/you/they are.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com o Google, o cliente pergunta como está a obra e qual é o seu papel. Você responde com frases curtas usando am / is / are.

lessons.title: Frases curtas com TO BE — "I am the contract executive"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz, em frases curtas com o verbo TO BE, quem você é e qual é o seu cargo, como em "I am the contract executive at Racional".
lessons.overview:
In a real meeting, the first words matter a lot. You say your name. You say your company. You say your role. At Racional, this is normal every day. Racional is a Brazilian company. It is more than fifty years old. It builds big projects in Brazil.

Your role is important. You are the contract executive. You work on the data center project for Google. A good start with the client is a good start for the project. You are the face of Racional in the room.

For now, the goal is simple. You say one short sentence with confidence. "I am the contract executive." "I am at Racional." Short and clear is enough. The client understands you, and you feel safe to talk.
lessons.intro:
Você já viu am, is, are. Hoje vamos transformar isso em frases curtas e firmes para se posicionar diante do Google.

Três âncoras desta aula: "I am the contract executive" (quem você é), "at Racional" (a empresa, sempre com at) e "I am responsible for the contracts" (seu papel). Diga cada uma de cabeça erguida.

lessons.title: A obra do data center — site, building, structure
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você nomeia, em inglês simples, as partes principais da obra do data center — site, building e structure — e aponta cada uma numa visita.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a big project. It has many parts. The site is the land, the place of the work. The building is the structure that goes up. The structure is the frame of concrete and steel that holds everything.

Racional builds big projects like this. It builds for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and now Google. On a site visit, the client walks and looks. The client wants to know the name of each part. You are there with the answer.

For now, you do not need long sentences. You point with your hand and you say the name. "This is the site." "This is the building." Simple words make a strong visit. The client sees the work and understands you.
lessons.intro:
Você é o homem dos contratos da obra do data center. Numa visita, o cliente aponta para o terreno, o prédio e a estrutura — e você diz o nome de cada parte.

Frase-âncora que resolve quase tudo: "This is the site. This is the building. This is the structure." Aponte com a mão e fale. Use também "over there" (ali) para o que está mais longe.
lessons.situation: Visita de obra com o time do Google. Você caminha pelo canteiro do data center e apresenta as partes principais para um engenheiro americano que vê a obra pela primeira vez.
lessons.context: Welcome to the site. This is the main building. The structure is almost ready. The walls are concrete and steel. We work here every day.

exercises.prompt: Você aponta para o prédio principal e diz:

exercises.explanation: This is the + adjetivo + substantivo. 'This is the main building.'

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em inglês, receba o time do Google numa visita: aponte e nomeie o site, o building e a structure em frases bem curtas.
takeaways: I can say 'Welcome to the site'.
I can name the building and the structure.
I can use 'almost ready' on a site visit.
I can point and say the name of each part.

lessons.title: Despedidas: "have a nice day / see you on Monday"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fecha uma reunião com o Google com despedidas simples e calorosas, como "have a nice day" e "see you on Monday".
lessons.overview:
The end of a meeting is important too. The last words stay in the mind of the client. A warm goodbye builds a good relationship. "Thank you all." "It was a great meeting." "See you on Monday." These small words make the client feel good.

Racional wants a strong relationship with Google. The data center project is long. You will meet the Google team many times. A nice goodbye today opens the door for the next meeting tomorrow.

For now, you only need short phrases. "Have a nice day." "See you soon." "Take care." You do not need long sentences. One warm phrase at the door is enough. It shows respect and it is easy to say.
lessons.intro:
Abrir bem uma reunião é importante; fechar bem também. As últimas palavras ficam na memória do cliente.

Três âncoras desta aula: "It was a great meeting" (fechamento), "see you on Monday" (próximo encontro) e "have a nice day" (despedida calorosa). Diga uma delas na porta, com um sorriso.

lessons.context: Thank you all. It was a great meeting. See you on Monday. Have a nice day. Take care.

lessons.title: "I don't understand" — ganhando tempo com naturalidade
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pede repetição e ganha tempo com naturalidade, usando frases como "sorry?", "can you repeat, please?" e "I don't understand".
lessons.overview:
In English, you do not understand everything. This is normal. The good news is simple: you can ask. "Sorry?" "Can you repeat, please?" These small phrases give you time. They are not a problem. They show that you want to understand well.

In a meeting with Google, this is very useful. The Google team speaks fast. They use new words. When you ask them to repeat, you control the conversation. You do not lose the message. A good contract executive asks before there is a mistake.

For now, you only need a few phrases. "One moment, please." "Can you speak slowly?" "I don't understand." Say them with a calm voice. The client will help you. To ask is not weak. To ask is smart.
lessons.intro:
Não entender tudo em inglês é normal. O segredo é pedir com naturalidade e ganhar tempo, sem travar.

Três âncoras desta aula: "Sorry?" (pedir repetição rápida), "Can you repeat, please?" e "Can you speak slowly?". Para ganhar tempo, use "One moment, please" e "Let me think".
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com o Google, o time fala rápido e usa palavras novas. Você pede para repetir e ganha tempo, com calma e segurança.
lessons.context: Sorry? Can you repeat, please? Can you speak slowly? Let me think. One moment, please. Now it is clear. Thank you.

vocab.example: Now it is clear. Thank you.
I am not sure. Let me think.

lessons.title: Valores em milhões: "five million dollars"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz valores grandes em inglês, em frases curtas, como "five million dollars" e "more than ten million".
lessons.overview:
Numbers tell the story of a big project. A data center is worth a lot of money. Millions of dollars. Many square meters. When you say a number in English, you must be clear and calm. A wrong number is a big problem.

Racional builds big projects. More than six hundred projects. More than ten million square meters. These numbers show that Racional is a strong and serious company. Google wants a partner with this experience. The numbers are your proof.

For now, learn the key words: thousand, million, billion. Say the number, then the word "dollars." "Five million dollars." Use "more than" and "about" when you are not exact. Short, clear, and confident.
lessons.intro:
Em negociação, dizer o número certo com clareza é tudo. Um número errado vira problema.

Três âncoras desta aula: "five million dollars" (número + dollars), "more than ten million" (acima de) e "about five million" (aproximadamente). Diga o número devagar e firme.
lessons.situation: Numa conversa com o Google, você fala do valor do contrato e do tamanho da obra do data center, em milhões de dólares e metros quadrados.
lessons.context: The contract is worth five million dollars. The data center has more than ten thousand square meters. Racional is a big company.

lessons.title: "How much?" — perguntas sobre preço e custo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pergunta sobre preço e custo em inglês, com frases simples como "how much?" e "how much does it cost?".
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, you ask about money. "How much?" "How much does it cost?" These questions are short and very useful. Price and cost are at the center of every contract. A good executive asks clear questions about money.

With Google, the data center has many costs. The structure, the steel, the energy, the cooling. Sometimes the price is high. Sometimes it is fair. You ask, you listen, and you answer with calm. "It depends." "The price is fair." "It is good value."

For now, learn the simple questions and answers. "How much does it cost?" "It is about five million." "It depends on the project." Racional gives a fair price and good value. You can say this in English with short, clear words.
lessons.intro:
Em negociação, perguntar sobre dinheiro com clareza é essencial. As perguntas são curtas e diretas.

Três âncoras desta aula: "How much?" (pergunta rápida), "How much does it cost?" (preço de algo) e a resposta "It depends" (depende). Use também "good value" (bom custo-benefício).

lessons.title: Energia: power, electricity, generator — vocabulário básico
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa as palavras básicas de energia em inglês — power, electricity, generator, backup — para explicar ao Google, em frases curtas, como a obra garante energia o tempo todo.
lessons.overview:
Energy is the heart of a data center. The servers run all day and all night. They cannot stop. So the building needs a lot of power. This is the first thing Google wants to know. Racional builds for big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. For these clients, energy is the number one topic.

The main source of power is electricity from the grid. But the grid can fail. So the project also has generators. A generator makes power when the grid is down. This is the backup. The generators use fuel. With this plan, the data center has power non-stop.

For Racional, this is normal work. In 50 years and 620+ projects, the company learned to plan safe power. When you explain this to Google, you build trust. You show that the power supply is safe and the servers never stop. Simple words are enough.
lessons.intro:
Lembre destas frases-âncora que você vai usar na prática: "The data center needs a lot of power." (precisa de muita energia) e "We have generators for backup." (temos geradores de reserva).

Feche sempre com a ideia de segurança: "The servers never stop." É a frase que tranquiliza o cliente.
lessons.situation: Visita técnica com engenheiros do Google. Eles querem saber como o data center garante energia sem nunca parar, e você explica o básico: força, eletricidade e geradores de reserva.
lessons.context: The data center needs a lot of power. The main source is electricity from the grid. We also have generators for backup. So the servers never stop. The power supply is safe.

lessons.title: Yes / No / Maybe — respostas curtas e seguras
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você responde com segurança em inglês usando respostas curtas — Yes, No e Maybe — e suaviza um 'não' de forma educada para manter a conversa com o Google fluindo.
lessons.overview:
You do not need long sentences to answer well. In a meeting, a short answer is often the best answer. Yes, no, and maybe are small words, but they are very strong. They keep the conversation easy and clear.

In business, a hard "no" can sound cold. So you can soften it. You can say "not yet" or "let me check". When you are not sure, you say "I'm not sure" or "I will check and tell you". This keeps the door open with the client.

For Fabrício at Racional, this is a daily tool. Google asks many quick questions about the data center, the team, and the price. With these short answers, he can reply fast, stay calm, and look confident — even with simple English. A clear short answer is better than a long answer full of doubt.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as âncoras desta aula: "Yes, of course." (sim, claro), "No, not yet." (ainda não) e "Maybe. Let me check." (talvez, deixa eu verificar).

Quando não souber, nunca trave: diga "I will check and tell you." — mantém a porta aberta.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google. Eles fazem perguntas rápidas sobre prazo, equipe e possíveis mudanças. Você responde de forma curta, clara e educada, sem travar.

lessons.title: "Please" e "Thank you" — pedido educado em reunião
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz pedidos educados em inglês usando please, thank you e could you...? para pedir algo ao Google em reunião de forma simples e cortês.
lessons.overview:
Polite words are small, but they make a big difference. Please and thank you show respect. With North American clients like Google, they are very important in every meeting. They make the conversation warm and easy.

When you ask for something, use "could you" or "can you". For example: "Could you send the file, please?" or "Can you repeat that, please?". These are soft, polite questions. After the answer, you say "thank you very much" or "I appreciate it".

For Fabrício at Racional, this builds a good relationship from the first meeting. He often needs to ask Google to share a document, to send a plan, or to repeat an answer. With these simple polite phrases, he sounds professional and friendly — and the client feels respected.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as âncoras: "Could you send the file, please?" (pode enviar o arquivo, por favor?) e "Thank you very much." (muito obrigado).

Para responder a um agradecimento, use "You're welcome." (de nada). Pedir com 'please' e fechar com 'thank you' deixa qualquer reunião mais leve.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google. Você precisa pedir um documento, pedir para repetirem uma informação e agradecer — tudo de forma educada e profissional.

lessons.title: Prazos curtos: days, weeks, months
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala de prazos curtos em inglês usando days, weeks e months, e diz quanto tempo uma etapa leva para tranquilizar o Google sobre o cronograma.
lessons.overview:
Time is money in construction. Google wants to know one thing very early: how long does it take? So you need simple time words: days, weeks, and months. With these three words, you can talk about any part of the project.

The key phrase is "it takes". For example: "It takes two weeks." or "It takes three months." You also talk about the deadline and you promise to deliver the work on time. These words show that you control the timeline.

For Racional, the timeline is a strong point. In 50+ years and 620+ projects, the company learned to finish on time. When Fabrício talks about days, weeks, and months with calm and clear English, Google sees a partner that respects the deadline and delivers the data center on time.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as âncoras: "It takes two weeks." (leva duas semanas) e "We deliver on time." (entregamos no prazo).

Use as três medidas de tempo conforme a etapa: days (dias), weeks (semanas), months (meses). 'It takes...' é a estrutura-chave da aula.
lessons.situation: Reunião de cronograma com o Google. Eles perguntam quanto tempo cada etapa do data center leva, e você responde com prazos curtos e claros, mostrando que a obra entrega no prazo.
lessons.context: How long does it take? It takes two weeks. The next stage takes three months. The deadline is short, but we deliver on time.

vocab.example: It is ready in two weeks.

exercises.explanation: Diga a duração com 'it takes' e feche com 'on time'. Passa controle do cronograma.

takeaways: I can talk about days, weeks, and months.
I can say 'it takes two weeks'.
I can talk about the deadline.

lessons.title: "When will it be ready?" — falando de prazos
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pergunta e responde sobre prazos em inglês usando 'When will it be ready?' e respostas como 'by Friday' e 'next month' para alinhar entregas com o Google.
lessons.overview:
In every project, the client asks one big question: "When will it be ready?". Google asks this about the data center many times. So you need to ask it and answer it with confidence. This is the most important time question in a meeting.

To answer, you use simple time markers. You can say "by Friday", "next month", or "by the end of July". If it is close, you say "soon" or "almost ready". If it is not done, you say "not yet". A good promise is "ahead of schedule" — early — and you avoid "behind schedule".

For Racional, hitting the delivery date is a matter of trust. With 620+ projects done, the company knows how to plan and expect the right date. When Fabrício answers "When will it be ready?" with a clear date, Google sees control and reliability — the base of a strong relationship.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as âncoras: a pergunta "When will it be ready?" (quando vai estar pronto?) e a resposta com data, como "It will be ready by Friday." ou "next month".

Para etapas perto do fim, use "almost ready" (quase pronto) ou "soon" (em breve). Sempre dê uma referência de tempo.
lessons.situation: Reunião de acompanhamento com o Google. Eles perguntam quando cada parte do data center estará pronta, e você responde com datas claras: por sexta, próximo mês, em breve.
lessons.context: When will it be ready? It will be ready by Friday. The next stage will be ready next month. It is almost ready. We are on time.

lessons.title: Resfriamento: cooling, temperature — vocabulário básico
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa as palavras básicas de resfriamento em inglês — cooling, temperature, cool air — para explicar ao Google como o data center se mantém frio e seguro.
lessons.overview:
A data center has thousands of servers. They run non-stop, and they make a lot of heat. If the building gets too hot, the servers can stop. So cooling is as important as power. This is a top question for Google.

The job of the cooling system is simple to explain: it makes cool air and keeps the temperature low. It uses water and good airflow. The goal is to keep low the temperature, so it does not rise. When the room stays cold and safe, the servers never stop.

For Racional, building a strong cooling system is part of delivering a safe data center for clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. When Fabrício explains cooling and temperature in simple English, he shows that the company understands what really matters: keeping the machines cool and the operation safe, every degree, every day.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as âncoras: "The cooling system keeps the temperature low." (o sistema de resfriamento mantém a temperatura baixa) e "The room stays cool and safe."

Ligue cada palavra à ideia de 'não deixar esquentar': cool air (ar frio), to keep low (manter baixo), safe (seguro).
lessons.situation: Visita técnica com o Google. Eles perguntam como o data center evita o superaquecimento dos servidores, e você explica o básico: sistema de resfriamento, ar frio e temperatura sob controle.
lessons.context: The servers make a lot of heat. The cooling system makes cool air. It keeps the temperature low. So the room stays cold and safe. The servers never stop.

vocab.example: The servers make a lot of heat.

lessons.title: "Can you help me?" — pedindo ajuda em inglês
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pede ajuda em inglês com frases curtas e seguras — "Can you help me?", "Can you repeat that?" e "I don't understand" — para nunca travar numa reunião com o Google.
lessons.overview:
In every meeting, you do not need to understand everything. Sometimes the other person speaks fast. Sometimes you do not know one word. This is normal. The best executives ask for help. They do not stay silent. At Racional, a company with more than fifty years and over 620 projects, communication is part of the job. With a big client like Google, a simple question keeps the meeting clear and safe.

Today the key sentence is very short: "Can you help me?" You can also say "Can you repeat that?" or "Can you speak slowly?". When you do not understand, you say "I don't understand." These small sentences are strong tools. They show respect, and they keep the conversation open.

For the Superintendent of Contracts at Racional, this is the first step with the Google data center team. You build trust when you ask, not when you guess. A good question is professional. So practice these words today. They are short, they are easy, and they work in any meeting.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você fixa três frases-âncora para pedir ajuda: "Can you help me?" (você pode me ajudar?), "Can you repeat that?" (pode repetir?) e "I don't understand." (eu não entendi).

Decore cada uma como um bloco único. Quando travar na reunião, use uma delas com calma — pedir ajuda é profissionalismo, não fraqueza.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com o Google, alguém fala rápido demais ou usa uma palavra nova. Em vez de ficar calado, você pede ajuda com tranquilidade.
lessons.context: Sorry, can you help me? Can you repeat that, please? I don't understand the last word. Can you speak slowly? Thank you.

exercises.explanation: 'Can you help me?' é a frase mestra. Curta, educada, e resolve.

exercises.title: 3. Peça para repetir

exercises.explanation: 'Repeat' = repetir. 'Can you repeat that?' te salva quando não pegou algo.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva um pedido de ajuda

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, imagine que o Google falou rápido demais. Peça ajuda: comece com 'Sorry, can you help me?' e peça para repetir devagar.
takeaways: I can ask for help with 'Can you help me?'.
I can say 'Can you repeat that?'.

lessons.title: Conversa antes da reunião — weather, weekend
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz small talk antes da reunião falando do tempo e do fim de semana — "How was your weekend?", "It was great" — para quebrar o gelo com o Google de forma natural.
lessons.overview:
A meeting does not start with the contract. It starts with a few warm words. People talk about the weather and the weekend. This is called small talk. It is short, it is friendly, and it builds trust. In Brazil we do this too. With a North American client like Google, this small talk is very common before business.

The sentences are easy. You ask "How was your weekend?" and you answer "It was great. And you?" You can say the day is hot, cold, sunny, or rainy. You can say "I relax with my family." These words are simple, but they open the door.

For the Superintendent of Contracts at Racional, this is the human side of the project. The Google data center is a big and serious job. But first, you say hello like a person, not only like a company. A warm start makes the whole meeting easier. Today you practice these small, friendly sentences.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você fixa as frases de quebra-gelo: "How was your weekend?" (como foi seu fim de semana?), "It was great. And you?" (foi ótimo. E você?) e uma frase sobre o tempo, como "It's sunny today."

Use a pergunta, ouça a resposta e devolva com "And you?". Esse ritmo de pingue-pongue é o coração do small talk.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião com o Google começar, há um minuto de conversa leve. Você aproveita para falar do tempo e do fim de semana.
lessons.context: Good morning! How was your weekend? It was great. I relax with my family. And you? The weather is nice today. It's sunny and warm. Let's start.

lessons.title: Comparação simples: more / less / the same
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz comparações simples com "more", "less" e "the same" — "more experience", "the same quality" — para começar a posicionar a Racional diante do Google.
lessons.overview:
In business, you often compare. You say one option has more, one has less, and two things are the same. These three words are very simple, but they are powerful. With them, you can show the value of Racional next to the market. You do not need long sentences. You need clear words.

Think about the numbers of Racional: more than fifty years, more than 620 projects, more than ten million square meters. This is a lot of experience. When you talk to Google, you can say: "We have more experience." Or you can say: "We have the same high quality, every time." Simple words, strong message.

For the Superintendent of Contracts, this is the start of negotiation language. You are not talking about price yet. You are talking about value. More experience. The same high quality. Less risk for the client. Today you learn to use these three small words with confidence, ready for the Google data center project.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você usa três palavras de comparação: more (mais), less (menos) e the same (o mesmo / igual). E a ponte than (do que) e the same as (igual a).

Frases-âncora: "We have more experience." e "We offer the same quality." São curtas e diretas — use-as para mostrar valor.
lessons.situation: Na preparação do primeiro encontro com o Google, você quer comparar a Racional com o mercado de forma simples, antes de falar em preço.
lessons.context: We have more experience than the market. We offer the same high quality, every time. This option has less risk for you. More years, more projects. The quality is the same as always.

exercises.explanation: Compare com palavras simples: more, less, the same. Mostre valor, não ataque.

takeaways: I can compare with 'more', 'less' and 'the same'.

lessons.title: "It is cheaper / more expensive" — comparando preços
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você compara preços com "cheaper" e "more expensive" — "It is cheaper", "a better price" — para falar de valor com o Google de forma simples e segura.
lessons.overview:
Now you talk about money. In negotiation, you compare prices. One thing is cheaper, one thing is more expensive. This is a key part of any business talk. The words are short, and you use them a lot with a client like Google. A clear price is a strong price.

But price is not only the number. A smart executive talks about value, not only cost. You can say: "It is more expensive, but it is better." Or: "This is a better price for the full project." At Racional, with fifty years of work and over 620 projects, you sell quality and safety, not only a low number.

For the Superintendent of Contracts on the Google data center, this is the heart of the deal. You need to compare a proposal, talk about a better price, and explain value. Today you practice the simple words for this: cheaper, more expensive, price, cost, value. Short words, clear and professional.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você fixa as palavras de preço: cheaper (mais barato), more expensive (mais caro), price (preço) e value (valor).

Frases-âncora: "It is cheaper.", "It is more expensive, but it is better." e "This is a better price." Use-as para falar de números com tranquilidade.
lessons.situation: Numa conversa de proposta com o Google, você compara opções e preços, mostrando que valor e qualidade pesam tanto quanto o número.
lessons.context: This proposal is cheaper. That option is more expensive, but it is better. The price is competitive. We offer good value, not only a low cost. This is a better price for you.

exercises.explanation: Palavra curta ganha '-er': cheap → cheaper. Palavra longa ganha 'more': more expensive.

exercises.explanation: Compare o número, mas sempre fale de valor. Valor vende mais que preço baixo.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, defenda uma proposta da Racional ao Google em 15 segundos. Compare duas opções usando 'cheaper', 'more expensive' e 'better value'.
takeaways: I can say 'It is cheaper' and 'It is more expensive'.
I can talk about price, cost and value.
I can say 'This is a better price'.
I can compare two options with simple words.

lessons.title: Servidores e racks — equipment vocabulary
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa o vocabulário básico de equipamentos do data center — server room, rack, cooling unit, generator — para falar do que a obra da Racional vai abrigar para o Google.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a special building. Inside, there is a server room with many racks. A rack is a tall metal frame. It holds the servers. The servers run all day, every day. They make heat. So the building needs a cooling unit to keep the temperature low. Power must never stop, so there is a backup and a generator.

For Racional, this is the technical heart of the Google project. Racional builds the structure, the raised floor, the power supply, and the space for all this equipment. With over 620 projects and ten million square meters, Racional knows how to build big and complex sites. A data center is one of the most demanding.

For the Superintendent of Contracts, you do not need to be an engineer in English. But you need the key words. When you say rack, cooling unit, or generator, the Google team sees that you understand the project. Today you learn these words in simple sentences, ready for a technical talk.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você fixa o vocabulário de equipamentos: server room (sala de servidores), rack (estante de servidores), cooling unit (unidade de resfriamento) e generator (gerador).

Frase-âncora: "The server room has many racks." e "The cooling unit keeps the temperature low." Use os termos com frases simples.
lessons.situation: Numa visita técnica com o Google, você fala dos equipamentos que o data center vai abrigar e como a obra da Racional os comporta.
lessons.context: The server room has many racks. Each rack holds many servers. The cooling unit keeps the temperature low. The power supply never stops. We have a backup and a generator. The raised floor holds the cables.

lessons.title: Apresentando a Racional em 2 frases simples
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta a Racional ao Google em duas frases simples e seguras — "We are a construction company from Brazil. We build large projects." — abrindo o primeiro contato com confiança.
lessons.overview:
The first contact is the most important. In a few seconds, you say who you are. You do not need a long speech. You need two clear sentences. "We are a construction company from Brazil. We build large projects." Simple, strong, and true. This is the start of trust with Google.

Behind these two sentences, there is a great story. Racional is a Brazilian construction company. It was founded in 1971, so it has more than fifty years of work. It has built over 620 projects and more than ten million square meters. The company is reliable. It wants to be a good partner for the Google data center.

For the Superintendent of Contracts, this is the goal of Module 2: to introduce Racional with confidence. You do not need many words. You need the right two sentences, said with calm and pride. Today you build your short company pitch. This is the door to the whole project.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você monta o seu pitch de duas frases: "We are a construction company from Brazil." (Somos uma construtora do Brasil.) e "We build large projects." (Construímos grandes obras.)

Depois você pode somar uma terceira: "We have over fifty years of experience." Decore as frases como blocos seguros — esse é o seu cartão de visita ao Google.

lessons.context: Hello. We are a construction company from Brazil. We build large projects. We have over fifty years of experience. We are a reliable partner. We want to work with Google.

lessons.title: "We have built..." — falando obras já entregues
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará das obras que a Racional já entregou usando 'We have built...', mostrando experiência para construir confiança com o Google.
lessons.overview:
Racional is a Brazilian construction company. It is more than fifty years old. In all these years, the company has built many big projects. It has built hospitals, shopping malls, and large industrial plants. This is a strong story, and it is a story about trust.

For an executive, this story is very useful. When you meet a new client, the client wants proof. The client wants to know: can this company deliver? A simple answer is the best answer: "We have built more than six hundred projects." A clear number shows experience. It builds confidence in a few words.

The client is Google. Google wants a data center in Brazil, and this is a big and important project. Before you talk about the future, you talk about the past. You show what Racional has done. Companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google look for a partner with a real track record. Racional has one.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura-âncora desta aula é "We have built..." (nós já construímos). Ela mostra tudo o que a Racional entregou ao longo dos anos.

Junte sempre a estrutura a um número forte: "We have built more than six hundred projects." E feche com prova de cumprimento de prazo: "We have delivered them on time."
lessons.situation: Primeira reunião com o Google. É a hora de mostrar a bagagem da Racional: as obras já entregues provam que a empresa é capaz de entregar o data center.
lessons.context: Racional is more than fifty years old. We have built more than six hundred projects. We have built hospitals, shopping malls, and industrial plants. We have delivered them on time.

vocab.example: We have built many big projects.
We have delivered every project on time.
We have worked on big sites.
We have built more than six hundred projects.
We delivered the project on time.
We have a strong track record.

lessons.title: "Is it possible?" — abrindo uma negociação
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você abrirá uma negociação de forma educada usando 'Is it possible...?', pedindo prazos, condições ou ajustes ao Google sem soar agressivo.
lessons.overview:
To negotiate is a big part of every executive's job. In a project, the client and the company do not always agree at first. They talk. They ask. They look for a good answer for both sides. A good negotiation is calm and polite. It is not a fight.

The first words are very important. When you ask, you must be polite. A great opening is "Is it possible to...?" This question is soft and respectful. It opens the door. It does not push. "Would it be possible to...?" is even more polite. With these words, the other side feels respected.

For Racional, this matters a lot with Google. The data center is a big project with a hard deadline. Sometimes you need a little more time, or you need to change the scope. You do not demand. You ask. The goal is always a win-win: good for Google and good for Racional.
lessons.intro:
A frase-âncora desta aula é "Is it possible to...?" (É possível...?) — a porta de entrada educada de qualquer negociação.

Guarde também "Would it be possible to...?" (Seria possível...?), ainda mais educada, e "Can we talk about...?" (Podemos falar sobre...?). Em negociação, abra com pergunta, não com exigência.
lessons.situation: Negociação do data center com o Google. Você precisa pedir um ajuste — no prazo, no escopo ou nas condições — sem parecer que está impondo. Você abre com uma pergunta educada.
lessons.context: Thank you for the proposal. Is it possible to talk about the deadline? We need a little more time. Would it be possible to meet again next week?

vocab.example: Is it possible to change the date?
Would it be possible to start later?
Can we talk about the price?
Is it possible to move the deadline?
Let us look at the terms.
Is it possible to adjust the scope?

exercises.explanation: 'Is it possible to...?' transforma uma exigência em um pedido educado. É a porta de entrada da negociação.

takeaways: I can open a negotiation with 'Is it possible to...?'.
