lessons.title: "I agree / I don't agree" — concordando e discordando
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você concordará e discordará de forma educada usando 'I agree' e 'I don't agree', mantendo a conversa com o Google leve e respeitosa.
lessons.overview:
In every meeting, people say yes and people say no. To agree is to say yes. To disagree is to say no. Both are normal and both are important. A good executive can do both in a calm and polite way. The other side must always feel respected.

When you do not agree, the words you choose matter a lot. "I don't agree" is direct, so you make it soft: "I see your point, but...". This shows that you listened first. You hear the other side, and then you say your idea. This keeps the talk friendly, even when you say no.

For Racional, this is key in the Google project. In the data center talks, you will not agree on everything. That is fine. The goal is to find a middle ground — a fair answer for both sides. When you are close to a deal, a calm "I agree" can close it.
lessons.intro:
As frases-âncora são "I agree" (concordo) e "I don't agree" (não concordo).

Para discordar com educação, use sempre a ponte "I see your point, but..." (entendo seu ponto, mas...). Primeiro mostre que ouviu; depois diga sua ideia. Termine buscando o meio-termo: "Let us find a fair middle ground."
lessons.situation: Reunião do data center com o Google. Há pontos em que você concorda e pontos em que precisa dizer não — sempre com respeito, buscando um acordo justo para os dois lados.
lessons.context: I see your point. On the deadline, I agree. On the price, I don't agree. Let us find a fair middle ground. I think we are close.

vocab.example: I don't agree on the price.
I completely agree with this plan.
I see your point, but I am not sure.
I agree, but we need more time.
I'm not sure about the date.
Let us find a middle ground.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo ao seu significado
exercises.explanation: Concordar, discordar e buscar o meio-termo justo: estes são os pilares de uma reunião respeitosa.

exercises.title: 2. Concorde e discorde com educação
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases para uma reunião com o Google: em uma você concorda, em outra você discorda com educação. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula (ex.: I agree, I don't agree, I see your point, fair). A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
keywords: I agree|I completely agree|I don't agree
exercises.modelAnswer: On the deadline, I agree. On the price, I see your point, but I don't agree. Let us find a fair middle ground.
exercises.explanation: Concordar é fácil. Discordar com educação é a marca de um bom negociador.

exercises.title: 3. Diga não com respeito
exercises.prompt: Você não concorda com o preço, mas quer manter a conversa boa com o Google. A melhor frase é:

options.text: I see your point, but I don't agree on the price.

options.whyWrong: Isso diz que você concorda — o oposto do que você quer.

exercises.explanation: 'I see your point, but...' mostra que você ouviu antes de discordar. Mantém a conversa respeitosa.

lessons.title: Tier I, II, III, IV — classificação de data center
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explicará a classificação de data center por Tiers (I, II, III, IV) ao Google usando frases simples sobre confiabilidade e redundância.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a building full of computers. It must work all day and all night. It can almost never stop. To measure this, the industry uses tiers: Tier I, Tier II, Tier III, and Tier IV. The tier shows how safe and how strong the data center is.

The idea is simple. Tier I is the most basic level. Tier IV is the highest level, with the most backup systems. A higher tier means more redundancy and more uptime. It means the data center almost never has downtime. For a client like Google, this is the heart of the project.

For Racional, this language is very useful. When you talk with Google, you must show that you understand the requirements. You can ask: "Which tier do you need?" Google may aim for Tier III or Tier IV. With a few simple words, you show that Racional speaks the same language as its client.
lessons.intro:
As frases-âncora desta aula são "Tier IV is the highest level" e "Tier I is the most basic".

Guarde também a pergunta-chave para o Google: "Which tier do you need?" (De qual Tier você precisa?) e a ideia central: tier mais alto = mais redundância = mais uptime.
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com o Google sobre o data center. Você precisa mostrar que entende a classificação por Tiers e perguntar qual nível o Google exige para o projeto.
lessons.context: A data center has tiers. Tier I is the most basic. Tier IV is the highest. A higher tier means more backup systems and more uptime. Which tier do you need?

vocab.example: The data center has a high tier.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, explique ao Google a diferença entre Tier I e Tier IV. Diga 'Tier IV is the highest level', cite mais 'redundancy' e 'uptime', e pergunte 'Which tier do you need?'.
takeaways: I can say that Tier IV is the highest level.

I can talk about uptime, downtime, and redundancy.

lessons.title: Falando da equipe da Racional ao cliente Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresentará a equipe da Racional ao Google usando 'This is...' e 'He is in charge of...', mostrando quem cuida de cada parte do projeto.
lessons.overview:
A big project needs a strong team. The data center for Google is a big project, so the team is very important. In the first meeting, the client wants to know the people. Who leads the work? Who is on the site every day? A clear team gives the client confidence.

To present your team, you need only a few simple words. "This is..." introduces a person. "He is the site manager" gives the role. "She is in charge of safety" says what the person does. With three short lines, you can present any colleague in a clear and professional way.

For Racional, this builds trust with Google. The project director leads the project. The site manager runs the site. The safety lead takes care of safety. When you introduce each person with calm and pride, Google sees a real, strong team behind Racional.
lessons.intro:
As frases-âncora são "This is..." (este é...) e "He/She is in charge of..." (ele/ela é responsável por...).

Para cada pessoa, use três passos: nome, cargo e responsabilidade. Ex.: "This is Ana. She is the site manager. She is in charge of the site."
lessons.situation: Primeira reunião com o Google. Você apresenta a equipe da Racional — diretor de projeto, gerente de obra e líder de segurança — para mostrar que há gente forte cuidando de cada parte.

vocab.example: He is in charge of the site.

lessons.title: "How long have you...?" — perguntas curtas sobre carreira
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fará perguntas curtas sobre carreira usando 'How long have you...?', criando uma conversa próxima com o time do Google.
lessons.overview:
People like to talk about their work. To ask about someone's career is a warm and easy way to start a relationship. A simple question like "How long have you worked here?" shows interest. It opens a friendly talk before the business begins.

The key words are small but powerful. "How long...?" asks about time. "For" goes with a period (for ten years). "Since" goes with a start point (since 2015). With these few words, you can ask and answer questions about anyone's background and role.

For Racional, this is great with the Google team. Before a hard meeting about the data center, a little small talk builds trust. You can ask the Google engineer: "How long have you worked in this field?" And you can answer too: "I have worked at Racional for many years." Good relationships start with simple questions.
lessons.intro:
A pergunta-âncora é "How long have you worked...?" (Há quanto tempo você trabalha...?).

Guarde a dupla mais importante para responder: "for" + período (for ten years) e "since" + ponto de início (since 2015). Pergunta curta, conversa próxima.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião técnica, você puxa conversa com o time do Google. Pergunta sobre a carreira deles e fala um pouco da sua, criando relação antes do negócio.
lessons.context: How long have you worked at Google? I have worked at Racional for many years. I joined the company a long time ago. How long have you been in this field?

lessons.title: Pedindo desconto: "Can you give us a discount?"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você responde com calma quando o Google pede desconto, usando frases curtas como "Let me check", "It depends" e "I will get back to you", sem se comprometer na hora.
lessons.overview:
In a business meeting, the client often asks for a discount. This is normal. Google is a big client, and big clients always ask. So Fabrício must be ready for one simple question: Can you give us a discount? The answer is not yes. The answer is not no. The best answer is calm.

The secret is to buy time. You say let me check the numbers. You say it depends on the scope and the timeline. You say I will get back to you tomorrow. With these short phrases, you stay calm and you stay in control. You do not give a price under pressure.

For Racional, the price is built on 50 years of work and 620+ projects. The value is real. So Fabrício does not need to drop the price fast. He needs to sound professional in English while he thinks. A fair question gets a fair, calm answer.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as frases-âncora que você vai usar na prática: "Let me check the numbers." (deixe-me ver os números) e "It depends on the scope and the timeline." (depende do escopo e do prazo).

Feche sempre adiando com elegância: "I will get back to you tomorrow." (eu te retorno amanhã). Nunca diga um preço sob pressão.
lessons.situation: Reunião comercial sobre o data center. O comprador do Google sorri e pergunta se a Racional pode dar um desconto. Você responde com calma, sem fechar nada.
lessons.context: Can you give us a discount? That is a fair question. Let me check the numbers first. It depends on the scope and the timeline. I will get back to you tomorrow.

lessons.title: Defendendo preço: "Our price is fair because..."
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você defende o preço da Racional com frases curtas e firmes, dizendo por que o valor é justo — "Our price is fair because..." — apoiado em qualidade, experiência e segurança.
lessons.overview:
After the client asks for a discount, the next moment comes: you must defend your price. You do not drop it. You explain the value. The key sentence is short and strong: Our price is fair because... Then you give one clear reason.

The reasons are easy. Because we deliver on time. Because we have 50 years of experience. Because safety comes first. You do not talk about the number. You talk about the quality and the track record. Google pays for a partner that is reliable.

For Racional, this is true and easy to show. 620+ projects. 10 million square meters built. Clients like Microsoft and Amazon. So when Fabrício says our price is fair, he has the facts behind him. The price includes safety, quality, and time. That is worth it.
lessons.intro:
Relembre a estrutura-âncora da prática: "Our price is fair because..." (nosso preço é justo porque...) seguida de uma razão simples: because we deliver on time / because safety comes first.

Use também: "I understand the concern." (entendo a preocupação) antes de defender. Você reconhece, mas não baixa o preço.
lessons.situation: O Google acha o preço alto. Em vez de baixar, você explica, com firmeza e gentileza, por que o valor da Racional é justo.
lessons.context: I understand the concern. Our price is fair because we deliver on time and with high quality. We have fifty years of experience. With us, safety always comes first.

vocab.example: It is fair because we deliver on time.
We have a strong track record.
We have fifty years of experience.
I understand the concern about cost.

exercises.explanation: Esta é a frase-mãe da aula: preço justo + uma razão clara. Ouça e escreva.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a defesa do preço
exercises.explanation: 'Our price is fair because...' + razão. Estrutura curta e forte para qualquer negociação.

exercises.title: 3. Reconheça antes de defender
exercises.prompt: I understand the ___. Our price is fair because we work with high quality.
exercises.explanation: 'I understand the concern' reconhece o cliente sem baixar o preço. Depois você defende.

exercises.title: 4. A melhor defesa do preço
exercises.prompt: O Google diz que o preço está alto. A melhor resposta é:

options.text: Yes, it is too expensive. Sorry.
options.whyWrong: Você concorda que é caro e enfraquece a Racional. Defenda o valor.

options.text: I understand the concern. Our price is fair because safety comes first.
The price is the price. No talk.
options.whyWrong: Fechar a conversa soa rude. Reconheça e explique o valor.

exercises.explanation: Reconheça ('I understand the concern') e defenda ('Our price is fair because...').

exercises.title: 5. Defenda o preço em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Our price is fair because we deliver on time and safety comes first.
exercises.translation: Nosso preço é justo porque entregamos no prazo e a segurança vem primeiro.

exercises.explanation: Fale com calma e convicção. Você não discute o número; você mostra o valor.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, imagine que o Google disse que o preço está alto. Defenda o valor da Racional usando 'Our price is fair because...' e uma razão.
takeaways: I can say 'Our price is fair because...' with a clear reason.
I can say 'I understand the concern' before I defend the price.
I can talk about quality, experience, and safety.
I can show that the price is worth it.

lessons.title: Redundância: N+1, 2N — por que importa para o Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica, em frases simples, o que é redundância (N+1, 2N) e por que ela importa para o Google — garantindo que o data center nunca pare.
lessons.overview:
For Google, a data center can never stop. The servers run all day and all night. So the design needs redundancy: extra equipment, ready as a backup. If one part fails, another part keeps the site running. This is the number one topic in every technical meeting.

Two terms are simple and very important. N plus one means "what you need, plus one spare". If you need four generators, N plus one is five. Two N means "double": two full systems. If one full system fails, the other one takes over. Google wants maximum uptime and zero downtime.

For Racional, this is daily work. In 620+ projects, the company learned to design safe and reliable systems. When Fabrício explains redundancy to Google with simple words, he builds trust. He shows that the power never stops and the critical systems are always protected.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as frases-âncora da prática: "We use N plus one for the generators." (usamos N+1 nos geradores) e "If one fails, the backup keeps it running." (se um falha, a reserva mantém ligado).

Feche com a ideia central: "The data center never stops." É a promessa que o Google quer ouvir.
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com os engenheiros do Google. Eles perguntam como a Racional garante que o data center nunca fique sem energia. Você explica redundância com frases simples.
lessons.context: The data center can never stop. So we design for redundancy. We use N plus one for the generators. We always have one backup. For critical systems, we use two N: two full systems. If one fails, the other keeps it running.

vocab.example: If one part fails, the backup starts.
We have five generators on site.
The system can switch over fast.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo técnico ao significado

pairs.right: Reserva que assume se algo falha.
Tempo em que tudo fica ligado.

exercises.explanation: Esses quatro termos são o núcleo de qualquer conversa de redundância com o Google.

exercises.title: 2. Explique a redundância ao Google
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 frases explicando ao Google como a obra nunca para. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula (por exemplo: redundancy, backup, N plus one, two N, never stops). A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: We design for redundancy. We use N plus one for the generators. We always have a backup. If one fails, the other keeps it running. The data center never stops.
exercises.explanation: Palavras simples bastam: reserva + N+1/2N + nunca para. É o que tranquiliza o Google.

exercises.title: 3. O que significa N+1?
exercises.prompt: Você precisa de quatro geradores. Com N plus one, quantos você tem?

options.text: Five generators: four plus one backup.

options.whyWrong: O dobro é 2N. N plus one é só um a mais.
N plus one nunca é menos. É sempre uma reserva a mais.

exercises.explanation: N plus one = o que você precisa + 1 reserva. Aqui, 4 + 1 = 5 geradores.

exercises.title: 4. Monte a promessa de continuidade
exercises.explanation: 'If one fails, the other keeps it running.' Frase-chave da redundância.

exercises.title: 5. Explique em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We design for redundancy. If one part fails, the backup keeps it running.
exercises.translation: Projetamos com redundância. Se uma parte falha, a reserva mantém funcionando.
exercises.prompt: Os engenheiros do Google perguntaram como a obra nunca para. Explique em voz alta.
exercises.explanation: Fale devagar e claro. Termos técnicos simples passam segurança.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, imagine que o Google perguntou como o data center nunca para. Explique redundância usando 'backup' e 'N plus one' ou 'two N'.
takeaways: I can explain redundancy with simple words.
I can say what N plus one and two N mean.
I can say 'If one fails, the backup keeps it running'.
I can tell Google the data center never stops.

lessons.title: Convidando o cliente Google para visitar a obra
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você convida o cliente do Google para visitar a obra em inglês, usando frases simples como "Would you like to visit the site?" e "How about next week?".
lessons.overview:
A site visit is a powerful tool. When the client sees the work in person, words become real. For Racional, this is a strong card: 620+ projects and a real site that Google can walk through. So Fabrício must learn to give the invitation in simple English.

The phrases are short and friendly. Would you like to visit the site? How about next week? Are you free on Tuesday? You offer, you do not push. You also stay flexible: Whatever works for you. Then you close: I will send you the details.

For Google, a visit builds trust fast. They see the team, the safety, and the quality with their own eyes. When Fabrício says It would be a pleasure to show you around, he sounds warm and professional. A good invitation opens the door to a good relationship.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as frases-âncora da prática: "Would you like to visit the site?" (você gostaria de visitar a obra?) e "How about next week?" (que tal semana que vem?).

Seja flexível e gentil: "Whatever works for you." (o que funcionar para você) e feche com "I will send you the details." (eu te envio os detalhes).
lessons.situation: Depois de apresentar a Racional, você quer que o time do Google conheça a obra de perto. Você faz o convite com simpatia e propõe uma data.
lessons.context: Would you like to visit the site? It would be a pleasure to show you around. How about next week? Are you free on Tuesday? Whatever works for you. I will send you the details.

vocab.example: Would you like to visit the site?
Let us plan a site visit.

exercises.prompt: Escreva um convite curto (2 ou 3 frases) para o Google visitar a obra. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula (por exemplo: would you like to, site visit, how about, whatever works for you). A correção olha só o uso dos termos.

exercises.modelAnswer: Would you like to visit the site? It would be a pleasure to show you around. How about next week? Whatever works for you. I will send you the details.
exercises.explanation: Convite simpático e flexível. É assim que você abre a porta para uma boa visita.

lessons.title: Recebendo o time do Google em São Paulo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você recebe o time do Google em São Paulo com frases curtas e calorosas, como "Welcome to Racional" e "How was your trip?".
lessons.overview:
The day arrives: the Google team lands in São Paulo and comes to Racional. The first minutes are very important. A warm welcome sets the tone for the whole visit. Fabrício is the host, and a good host makes the guest feel at home.

The phrases are simple and friendly. Welcome to Racional. It is great to have you here. How was your trip? Would you like water or coffee? Then you guide them: This way, please. Please follow me. Have a seat. Small phrases, big effect.

For Google, the welcome shows respect and care. A long flight is tiring, so a kind word matters. When Fabrício says We are glad you came and offers a coffee, he builds a warm, human relationship. This is the start of trust between Racional and a global client.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as frases-âncora da prática: "Welcome to Racional. How was your trip?" (bem-vindo à Racional. Como foi a viagem?) e "Would you like water or coffee?" (você gostaria de água ou café?).

Para guiar o visitante, use: "This way, please." (por aqui, por favor) e "Please have a seat." (por favor, sente-se).
lessons.situation: O time do Google chegou a São Paulo depois de um voo longo. Você os recebe na Racional como anfitrião, com simpatia e cuidado.

exercises.modelAnswer: Welcome to Racional. It is great to have you here. How was your trip? Please have a seat. Would you like water or coffee? We are glad you came.
exercises.explanation: Caloroso e simples. É assim que você abre a visita com o pé direito.

lessons.title: Falando cronograma: "We will finish by December"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre cronograma com confiança, usando frases simples como "We will finish by December" e "We deliver on time".
lessons.overview:
For Google, time is as important as price. They need the data center ready on a clear date. So Fabrício must talk about the schedule with confidence. The key sentence is short and strong: We will finish by December.

The words are simple but precise. By a date means "not later than that date". In a month means "inside that period". A deadline is the final date. A milestone is an important point on the way. You say: We will deliver on time. We are confident.

For Racional, this is a real strength. 620+ projects delivered, 50 years of work. The company knows how to plan a timeline and reach each milestone. When Fabrício says We will finish by December, he speaks with facts behind him. A clear schedule builds trust with Google.
lessons.intro:
Relembre as frases-âncora da prática: "We will finish by December." (vamos terminar até dezembro) e "We will deliver on time." (vamos entregar no prazo).

Mostre segurança: "We are confident." (estamos confiantes) e fale de marcos com "next month" e "by the end of...".
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google sobre prazos do data center. Eles querem saber quando a obra fica pronta. Você fala o cronograma com clareza e confiança.
lessons.context: We have a clear schedule. We will finish by December. The next milestone is ready next month. We will deliver on time and on budget. We are confident.

vocab.example: The next milestone is ready soon.
We finish phase one next month.
It is ready by the end of the year.
The site will be ready in December.
We plan the timeline with care.

exercises.explanation: 'We will finish by December' + 'We are confident' passa clareza e segurança.

exercises.title: 3. Ligue o termo de prazo ao significado
exercises.explanation: Esses quatro termos são o núcleo de qualquer conversa de cronograma com o Google.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva o cronograma ao Google
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 frases dizendo ao Google quando a obra fica pronta. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula (por exemplo: we will finish, by December, deadline, on time, milestone). A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
keywords: by the end of|by December|deadline|next month
exercises.modelAnswer: We have a clear schedule. We will finish by December. The next milestone is ready next month. We will deliver on time. We are confident.
exercises.explanation: Clareza + confiança. É assim que a Racional mostra controle do prazo.

exercises.title: 5. Fale o prazo em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We will finish by December. We will deliver on time. We are confident.
exercises.translation: Vamos terminar até dezembro. Vamos entregar no prazo. Estamos confiantes.
exercises.prompt: O Google perguntou quando a obra fica pronta. Responda com clareza e confiança.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, imagine que o Google perguntou quando o data center fica pronto. Responda usando 'We will finish by...' e mostre confiança.
takeaways: I can say 'We will finish by December'.
I can use 'deadline', 'milestone', and 'on time'.

lessons.title: Atraso e ajuste de prazo: "We need two more weeks"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você avisa o Google sobre um pequeno atraso e pede mais tempo de forma calma e profissional, usando "We need two more weeks".
lessons.overview:
In every big project, a small delay can happen. The weather changes, a truck is late, the ground is hard. This is normal. At Racional Engenharia, with more than 620 projects and over 50 years of work, the team knows how to handle this. The skill is not to avoid every delay. The skill is to communicate well when you need more time.

For a client like Google, trust is the most important thing. When you say "We need two more weeks", you stay calm and you bring a plan. You give a short reason, like the rain. You give a new date. You show that you control the work. This builds confidence, and confidence keeps the partnership strong.

In this lesson you learn simple words to give an update. You learn how to ask for a little more time without sounding nervous. These small phrases protect a big project. For a contracts director at Racional, this is daily work: clear, short, and honest English with the client.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: I have an update. (Tenho uma atualização.), We need two more weeks. (Precisamos de mais duas semanas.) e We have a plan to catch up. (Temos um plano para recuperar.)

A estrutura é sempre a mesma: aviso curto + motivo curto + novo prazo + solução. Calmo, no controle.
lessons.situation: A chuva forte atrasou a concretagem da fundação. Você precisa avisar o time do Google que vai precisar de duas semanas a mais — e mostrar que já tem um plano.
lessons.context: Hi, I have an update. Because of the rain, we need two more weeks. I'm sorry for the delay. But we have a plan to catch up. The final date will not change.

vocab.example: Because of the rain, we lost two days.
We have a plan to catch up.
We will make up the time.
The final date is still on track.
We need a few more days.
The final date is in June.

options.whyWrong: Excesso de desculpa passa nervosismo. O Google quer ver controle, não pânico.

options.text: I have an update. We need two more weeks. We have a plan.
It will be late. I don't know when.
options.whyWrong: "I don't know when" tira sua credibilidade. Sempre dê um novo prazo.

exercises.explanation: Aviso curto + novo prazo + plano. Calmo e no controle: é assim que se comunica um atraso.

exercises.modelAnswer: Hi, I have an update. Because of the rain, we need two more weeks. We have a plan to catch up.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos: aviso, motivo, novo prazo e solução.

exercises.title: 5. Diga o aviso em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I have an update. We need two more weeks.
exercises.translation: Tenho uma atualização. Precisamos de mais duas semanas.
exercises.prompt: Imagine que você está ao telefone com o Google. Avise o atraso com calma e voz firme.
exercises.explanation: Tom calmo e pausado. Você está no controle, não pedindo desculpa o tempo todo.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, avise o Google sobre um atraso de duas semanas: comece com "I have an update", dê o motivo (rain), diga o novo prazo e termine com "We have a plan to catch up".
takeaways: I can say "I have an update."
I can ask for two more weeks.
I can give a short reason with "because of."
I can say "We have a plan to catch up."

lessons.title: Site visit — andando pela obra do data center
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma visita de obra pelo data center, apontando áreas, dando instruções de segurança e mostrando o andamento com frases curtas.
lessons.overview:
A site visit is a special moment. The client walks on the real construction site and sees the project grow. For Racional Engenharia, the site is the best showroom. The cranes, the structure, the new floors — they show the size and the quality of the work. With more than 10 million square meters built, Racional knows how to receive a client with pride.

When Google visits the data center, two things matter: safety first, and a clear tour. You give a helmet and a safety vest at the gate. You say "Follow me" and "Watch your step". Google takes safety very seriously, so a strong start with safety shows that Racional is professional.

In this lesson you learn short phrases to point and to guide. You point with "over there" and "this is". You show progress with "this area is ready" and "under construction". You do not need long sentences. You need a clear hand and a few simple words to lead the client through the project.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: Follow me. (Venham comigo.), This is the entrance. (Esta é a entrada.) e This area is ready. (Esta área está pronta.)

Para apontar use over there (ali). Para segurança, comece sempre por Please wear your helmet.
lessons.situation: O time do Google chega ao canteiro do data center. Você os recebe no portão, entrega capacetes e coletes e guia o grupo pelas áreas principais.
lessons.context: Welcome to the site. Please wear your helmet and your safety vest. Follow me, and watch your step. This is the entrance. Over there is the crane. This area is ready. That part is under construction.

vocab.example: This is a big construction site.

lessons.title: Small talk sobre viagem e voo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz um pequeno bate-papo (small talk) sobre a viagem e o voo do cliente antes de uma reunião com o Google.
lessons.overview:
Before a meeting, people talk for a few minutes about simple things. This is small talk. It is not about the project. It is about the person. For American clients like Google, small talk is very important. It is warm. It shows that you care about the person, not only the contract.

The team from Google often travels far to visit the data center. They take a long flight to Brazil. They feel tired. They have jet lag. A kind question like "How was your flight?" opens the door. It makes the client feel welcome at Racional Engenharia, a company with more than 50 years of experience receiving big clients.

In this lesson you learn short, friendly questions for the first minutes of a meeting. You ask about the trip, the flight, and the hotel. You offer a coffee. These small words build a real connection. With a good start, the meeting goes better. For Fabrício, this is the human side of leading a project with Google.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: How was your flight? (Como foi seu voo?), Can I get you a coffee? (Posso te trazer um café?) e Please have a seat. (Sente-se, por favor.)

O segredo do small talk é ser breve e caloroso. Pergunta curta, sorriso, e siga para a reunião.
lessons.situation: O time do Google chega ao escritório da Racional depois de um voo longo dos Estados Unidos. Antes de começar a reunião, você conversa um pouco sobre a viagem.
lessons.context: Hello! Welcome to Brazil. How was your flight? It was a long trip. You must be tired. Please have a seat. Can I get you a coffee? How was the hotel?

lessons.title: Conversa rápida sobre família e filhos
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa de forma simples sobre família e filhos com o cliente do Google, criando vínculo antes da reunião.
lessons.overview:
Family is a warm topic. In small talk before a meeting, many people ask about kids and home. For American clients like Google, this is normal and friendly. A simple question like "Do you have kids?" shows that you see the person, not only the project. It builds a real human connection.

At Racional Engenharia, relationships matter as much as the work. The company has worked with big clients for more than 50 years, and trust often grows in these small, human moments. A short talk about family can make a long data center project feel more personal and more friendly.

In this lesson you learn easy questions and answers about family. You ask "How old are they?" and you answer "I have two kids". You return the question with "How about you?". These few words are safe and kind. For Fabrício, they open the door to a strong, warm relationship with the Google team.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: Do you have kids? (Você tem filhos?), How old are they? (Que idade eles têm?) e How about you? (E você?)

"How about you?" devolve a pergunta e mantém a conversa fluindo. Use sempre depois de responder.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião com o Google, a conversa caminha para temas pessoais. O cliente pergunta sobre sua família e você responde e devolve a pergunta.
lessons.context: Do you have kids? I have two kids, a boy and a girl. They keep me busy! How about you? How old are they? That's lovely. My family is back home in Brazil.

lessons.title: "We are on schedule / We are behind schedule"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você informa ao Google se o projeto está no prazo, atrasado ou adiantado, usando "on schedule" e "behind schedule".
lessons.overview:
In every meeting with a client, there is one big question: is the project on time? The answer uses three simple words: on schedule, behind schedule, and ahead of schedule. On schedule means on time. Behind means late. Ahead means faster than the plan. These three phrases are the heart of a status update.

For Google and the data center, time is money and trust. The client wants a clear, honest answer. At Racional Engenharia, with more than 620 projects delivered, this honesty is part of the culture. When you say "We are on schedule", the client relaxes. When there is a small delay, you say it with a plan to get "back on track".

In this lesson you learn to give a quick status in simple English. You answer "How is it going?". You say the project is going well, with "no major issues". You sound calm and in control. For Fabrício, this is the language of trust in every meeting with the Google team.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: We are on schedule. (Estamos no prazo.), We are a bit behind. (Estamos um pouco atrasados.) e We are back on track. (Voltamos ao plano.)

"Schedule" (cronograma) é a palavra-chave. "On / behind / ahead of schedule" cobre as três situações.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião com o Google, o cliente pergunta como vai o projeto. Você dá um status geral curto e tranquilo do data center.
lessons.context: How is it going? Overall, we are on schedule. The work is going well. We had a bit of rain, but we are back on track. There are no major issues. Good news!

vocab.example: We are a bit behind schedule.
Good news! We are on time.

exercises.title: 1. Monte o status positivo
exercises.explanation: "We are on schedule" = estamos no prazo. É a frase mais importante do status.

exercises.title: 2. Complete o status

exercises.explanation: "Back on track" = de volta ao plano. Mostra que houve um problema, mas já foi resolvido.

commonErrors.again: Use "back on track", não "again on track".

exercises.title: 3. Responda "How is it going?"
exercises.prompt: O Google pergunta: "How is it going?" O projeto está no prazo. A melhor resposta é:

options.text: Overall, we are on schedule. No major issues.

options.whyWrong: Resposta vaga passa insegurança. Dê um status claro.
A ordem está quebrada. O certo é "We are on schedule."

lessons.title: Status do projeto — falando percentuais de progresso
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você informa o progresso do projeto ao Google usando percentuais simples, como "about fifty percent complete".
lessons.overview:
Numbers make a status clear. When you say a project is "fifty percent complete", the client sees the picture at once. Percent, complete, and done are the key words. With a simple number, you turn a long report into one short, strong sentence.

For Google and the data center, the project moves through phases: the foundation, then the structure, then the systems. At Racional Engenharia, with more than 10 million square meters built, each phase has a clear measure of progress. A percent number for each phase shows the client exactly where the work is.

In this lesson you learn to give the numbers in simple English. You say "about half", "almost done", or "on target". You use "about" and "around" for an estimate. These small words let Fabrício report real progress to the Google team in a clear and confident way.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora: It is about fifty percent complete. (Está cerca de 50% concluído.), The foundation is done. (A fundação está pronta.) e We are on target. (Estamos na meta.)

"About" e "around" suavizam o número (cerca de). "Complete / done" indicam o que já está pronto.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião de acompanhamento, o Google pede os números do data center. Você relata o progresso de cada fase em percentuais simples.
lessons.context: Let me give you the numbers. Overall, the project is about fifty percent complete. The foundation is done. The structure is around forty percent. We are on target.

vocab.example: Let me give you the numbers.
The structure is at forty percent.

lessons.title: MEP — Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing (introdução)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você nomeia as três grandes disciplinas de instalações de um data center — MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) — e diz uma frase simples sobre cada uma numa reunião com o Google.
lessons.overview:
In a data center, three big areas keep everything working. We call them MEP: Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing. Mechanical is the cooling. Electrical is the power. Plumbing is the water and the pipes. The Google data center needs all three.

Racional builds these systems every day. We install ducts, wiring, and pipes. Each one is a different discipline. A good team works on all three at the same time, on schedule.

Why is this important for you? In a meeting with Google, you must name these systems in English. You do not need long words. You can say: "The electrical system is ready." Simple and clear. This is how Racional talks to a big client like Google.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende a nomear os três sistemas em inglês: mechanical, electrical, plumbing. Decore a sigla MEP — é o jeito americano de falar disso.

Frases-âncora para usar com o Google: "The system is ready." / "It is on schedule." / "We install the pipes."
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com o time do Google. Eles perguntam sobre as instalações do data center. Você precisa nomear os três sistemas e dizer, em uma frase, como cada um está.
lessons.context: We have three systems. Mechanical is the cooling. Electrical is the power. Plumbing is the water. We install the pipes and the ducts. The electrical system is ready for testing. Everything is on schedule.

vocab.example: The mechanical system is the cooling.
Plumbing is the water and the pipes.

The system is ready for testing.

exercises.explanation: MEP = Mechanical (mecânica/cooling), Electrical (elétrica/power), Plumbing (hidráulica/water).

options.whyWrong: Electrical é energia, não água. Água é plumbing.
Forma errada. O certo seria 'We do not install' ou, aqui, 'is ready'.

exercises.explanation: MEP = Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing. Plumbing é a hidráulica (água e tubos).

exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas sobre o data center usando ao menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: system, electrical, plumbing, on schedule).

exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos em inglês.

exercises.translation: Temos três sistemas. O sistema elétrico está pronto.

exercises.explanation: Frases curtas e claras. Não corra; pause depois de 'systems'.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, nomeie os três sistemas (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) e diga uma frase simples sobre cada um, como numa reunião com o Google.
takeaways: I can say MEP means three systems.
I can name mechanical, electrical, and plumbing.
I can say 'The system is ready.'
I can say 'We are on schedule.'

lessons.title: Conversa sobre comida e restaurante em SP
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você puxa uma conversa simples sobre comida e restaurantes em São Paulo com o cliente do Google — uma forma fácil e calorosa de criar vínculo antes da reunião.
lessons.overview:
Before a meeting, people talk a little. We call this small talk. Food is a great topic. It is easy and warm. Everyone likes to talk about a good restaurant.

São Paulo has great food. We have barbecue, fresh juice, and good coffee. You can say: "Do you like barbecue?" or "You should try this dish." These small questions help you build a good relationship with the Google team.

At Racional, the client comes from far away. Sometimes from the United States. A friendly talk about lunch or a tasty dish makes the visit better. Good food and a warm welcome show our culture. This is part of doing business well.
lessons.intro:
Hoje o foco é o small talk sobre comida — leve e amigável. Use perguntas curtas para abrir a conversa.

Frases-âncora: "Do you like...?" / "You should try..." / "It is very tasty."
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião, você caminha com o cliente do Google até a sala. Para quebrar o gelo, você fala sobre comida e sugere um bom restaurante perto do escritório.

lessons.title: Convidando o cliente Google para um almoço
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você convida o cliente do Google para um almoço de forma educada e calorosa, propõe um horário e confirma o convite — um gesto simples que fortalece o relacionamento.
lessons.overview:
An invitation is a warm gesture. When you invite a client to lunch, you show care. The Google team feels welcome. This makes the relationship strong.

The words are simple. You can say: "Would you like to have lunch?" or "How about tomorrow at noon?" Then you confirm: "See you then." Short and polite. This is all you need.

At Racional, we host clients from Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. A good lunch is part of the business. We say: "It would be a pleasure." We book a table near the office. A small invitation can open a big door.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende a convidar com elegância. O segredo é a fórmula educada "Would you like to...?".

Frases-âncora: "Would you like to have lunch?" / "How about tomorrow at noon?" / "See you then."
lessons.situation: No fim da reunião, você quer fortalecer o relacionamento com o time do Google. Você os convida para um almoço, propõe o horário e confirma.
lessons.context: Would you like to have lunch with us? It would be a pleasure. How about tomorrow at noon? There is a good restaurant near the office. It's my treat. Perfect. See you then.

lessons.title: Falando custos por etapa do data center
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, com frases simples, o custo de cada etapa do data center numa reunião com o Google — nomeando a fase e dizendo se está dentro do orçamento.
lessons.overview:
A big project has many phases. First the foundation. Then the structure. Last the finishing. Each phase has a cost. The total cost is the budget.

Google wants to know one thing: is the project on budget? You can say: "The foundation is on budget." Or: "We are slightly over budget." Short and clear. This builds trust.

At Racional, we control the cost in every phase. We track the budget every week. The numbers are under control. When we say "on budget" to a client like Google, it shows we are a strong and serious partner.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você fala de custo por etapa, sem números difíceis. O importante é nomear a fase e dizer se está dentro do orçamento.

Frases-âncora: "The foundation is on budget." / "We are slightly over budget." / "Everything is under control."
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google sobre o andamento financeiro. Eles perguntam sobre o custo de cada etapa. Você responde, fase por fase, se está dentro do orçamento.
lessons.context: The project has three phases. The foundation is on budget. The structure is under control. So far, the cost is good. We are slightly under budget overall. Everything is under control.

lessons.title: "It is included / It is not included" no escopo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz, com clareza, o que está e o que não está dentro do escopo do contrato com o Google — usando 'It is included' e 'It is not included' para evitar mal-entendidos.
lessons.overview:
Every contract has a scope. The scope is the list of work. Some items are included. Some items are not included. This must be very clear.

With a client like Google, clear words stop problems. You can say: "This is included." Or: "This is out of scope. We can quote it separately." Simple and honest. No surprise later.

At Racional, we work with big contracts every day. We always confirm the scope. We clarify what is included and what is not. This is how a serious partner protects the client and the project.
lessons.intro:
Hoje o foco é a clareza de escopo: o que entra e o que não entra. Duas frases resolvem quase tudo.

Frases-âncora: "It is included." / "It is not included." / "We can quote it separately."
lessons.situation: Reunião de contrato com o Google. Eles perguntam se um item específico está no preço. Você responde com clareza se está incluído ou não, evitando mal-entendidos.
lessons.context: Let me clarify the scope. The structure is included. The finishing is included. The extra cooling is not included. It is out of scope. We can quote it separately. I will confirm everything in the contract.

vocab.example: This is part of the scope.
The extra work is out of scope.
It is included, no extra cost.

exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos em inglês.

Civil works are the base of the building. We use concrete and steel. We build the foundation, the columns, and the slabs. This is the strong skeleton of the data center.

The words are simple but important. You can say: "We pour the concrete." Or: "The foundation is ready." Google wants to see the building go up. Clear words show clear progress.

Racional has more than 50 years in civil works. We build big and strong structures. When we say "the foundation is ready" to Google, it shows our experience. This is the heart of what Racional does.

Hoje você aprende as palavras das obras civis: concrete, steel, foundation. Use frases curtas de andamento.

lessons.title: Hobbies e interesses pessoais — vocabulário básico
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala dos seus hobbies com frases curtas como "I like soccer" e pergunta o do cliente do Google com "What do you like to do?", criando vínculo no small talk antes da reunião.
lessons.overview:
Before every meeting, there is small talk. People talk about life. They talk about hobbies. A hobby is a thing you like to do in your free time. For your American client at Google, this small talk is very important. It builds trust. It makes the meeting warm.

You do not need many words. You need one simple idea: "I like..." and "I enjoy...". You can talk about soccer, music, cooking, reading, or fishing. Then you ask the client: "What do you like to do?". This shows you care about the person, not only the project.

At Racional, you work with big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and now Google. The data center is a long project. You meet the same people many times. Good relationships make the work easier. A short talk about a hobby is a small thing, but it opens the door.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura-âncora de hoje é uma só: "I like + atividade" (Eu gosto de...). Ex.: "I like soccer." ou "I like to travel." Um irmão dela é "I enjoy + atividade" (Eu curto...).

Para devolver a pergunta e ouvir o cliente, use "What do you like to do?" (O que você gosta de fazer?). E reaja com simpatia: "Me too!" ou "That sounds fun!".
lessons.situation: Faltam cinco minutos para a reunião com o Google e o clima está parado. Você puxa um assunto pessoal: conta um hobby seu e pergunta o do cliente.
lessons.context: I like soccer. On the weekend, I play with my friends. I also enjoy cooking. What do you like to do?

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você puxa um papo leve sobre esportes com o pessoal do Google usando frases curtas como "Do you like soccer?" e "My team is...", quebrando o gelo com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
In the United States, people love sports. They talk about the game, the team, and the weekend. For your client at Google, sports is an easy and friendly topic. It is a safe way to start a talk. You do not talk about work first. You talk about the game.

You need one simple question: "Do you like...?" and one simple answer: "I like..." or "My team is...". Here in Brazil, soccer is huge. In the US, people watch basketball and American football. Remember: their football is not our soccer!

At Racional, the data center project is long. You will see the Google team many times. A short talk about the game on Monday makes the room warm. It shows you are a person, not only an engineer. This small habit builds a strong relationship.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura de hoje é a pergunta "Do you like + esporte?" (Você gosta de...?) e a resposta "My team is..." (Meu time é...). Verbos-âncora: to watch (assistir) e to play (jogar).

Cuidado cultural: nos EUA, football é futebol americano; o nosso é soccer. Não troque isso com o Google.
lessons.situation: Cinco minutos antes da reunião com o Google. O engenheiro americano comenta que assistiu a um jogo no fim de semana. Você aproveita para puxar conversa.

lessons.title: Aumento de custo: "There is an extra cost because..."
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você comunica ao Google um aumento de custo com frases curtas e claras como "There is an extra cost because...", explicando o motivo de forma simples e profissional.
lessons.overview:
In a big project, the price can change. Sometimes there is an extra cost. This is normal in construction. But you must explain it well. You must be clear and calm. For your client at Google, a clear reason builds trust. A bad explanation breaks trust.

The key word is because. You say: "There is an extra cost because...". Then you give one simple reason. Maybe the scope is bigger. Maybe there is a change in the plan. You show the numbers. You explain the total. Keep it short and simple.

At Racional, you manage contracts for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. Money talks are part of your job. The data center is large, and changes happen. When you explain an extra cost in clear English, the client respects you. They see Racional as a fair and honest partner.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura-âncora é "There is an extra cost because..." (Há um custo extra porque...). O conector-chave é because (porque) — ele liga o custo ao motivo.

Apoie com "The reason is..." (O motivo é...) e feche com the total (o total). Frases curtas, números claros.
lessons.situation: O escopo da obra do data center mudou e o custo subiu. Na reunião com o Google, você precisa comunicar o custo extra e dar o motivo de forma simples.
lessons.context: There is an extra cost. The reason is a change in the scope. Google asked for more. I can explain the numbers.

lessons.title: Justificando aumento — materials, labor, schedule
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você justifica um aumento de custo ao Google apontando o motivo certo — materials, labor ou schedule — com frases simples como "The price is higher because of materials".
lessons.overview:
An extra cost has a reason. In construction, there are three big reasons: materials, labor, and schedule. Sometimes the price of materials goes up. Sometimes you need more labor. Sometimes the schedule is very tight. You must name the right reason for your client.

The structure is simple: "The price is higher because of...". Then you say the reason: materials, labor, or schedule. You can also say "We need more...". Short and clear. For Google, a clear reason is a fair reason. They want to understand, not to fight.

At Racional, with 50 years and 620+ projects, cost talks happen every week. On a data center, materials are special and the deadline is hard. When you explain the cost with one simple reason, Google sees a strong and honest partner. This is good for the long project.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura-âncora é "The price is higher because of..." (O preço está mais alto por causa de...). Os três motivos-chave: materials (materiais), labor (mão de obra) e schedule (cronograma).

Apoie com "We need more..." (Precisamos de mais...) e "to go up" (subir, para preço). Nomeie um motivo por vez.

lessons.title: Procurement & lead time — chegada de equipamento Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre compra e prazo de entrega de equipamentos do Google com frases simples como "The lead time is six weeks" e "We can place the order now".
lessons.overview:
A data center needs special equipment. One example is a transformer. This equipment is not in the store. You must order it early. The time from the order to the delivery is called lead time. Procurement is the work of buying. For a big project, lead time is very important.

The structure is simple: "The lead time is six weeks" and "We can place the order now". You talk with the supplier. You ask them to confirm the date. You watch for a delay. You want the equipment to arrive on time. A short, clear update keeps Google calm.

At Racional, on the Google data center, some equipment comes from far away. If the order is late, the whole project is late. So you plan the procurement early. When you give Google a clear update on lead time and delivery, they trust the plan. This is part of being a strong contract partner.
lessons.intro:
As estruturas-âncora são "The lead time is + tempo" (O prazo de entrega é...) e "We can place the order now" (Podemos fazer o pedido agora). Termos-chave: lead time, delivery (entrega), supplier (fornecedor).

Para tranquilizar o Google, use "on time" (no prazo) e "to confirm" (confirmar). Cuidado com delay (atraso).
lessons.situation: Um transformador do data center precisa ser comprado com antecedência. Na reunião com o Google, você atualiza o prazo de entrega e pede confirmação ao fornecedor.
lessons.context: We can place the order now. The lead time is six weeks. The supplier can confirm the delivery date.

lessons.title: Felicitando o cliente — promotion, anniversary, holiday
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você parabeniza o cliente do Google por uma boa notícia — promotion, anniversary ou holiday — com frases simples como "Congratulations!" e "Well done!".
lessons.overview:
Good relationships are not only about work. They are about people. When your client has good news, you say something nice. Maybe a promotion. Maybe a company anniversary. Maybe a holiday. A short, warm message shows you care. For Google, this is a normal and friendly habit.

The words are very simple: "Congratulations!", "Well done!", and "Happy holidays!". You can say "I am happy for you" or "You deserve it". You do not need long sentences. One kind line is enough. It makes the person smile.

At Racional, the data center is a long project with many people. Over many months, your Google contact may get a new role, or the project may reach a big milestone. A small "Congratulations" at the right time builds a strong, human relationship. This is how a 50-year company keeps clients for many years.
lessons.intro:
A palavra-âncora de hoje é "Congratulations!" (Parabéns!). Combine com "Well done!" (Mandou bem!) e "Happy holidays!" (Boas festas!).

Para tornar pessoal, use "I am happy for you" (Fico feliz por você) e "You deserve it" (Você merece). Frases curtas e calorosas.
lessons.situation: Seu contato no Google foi promovido a um novo cargo. Você abre a reunião com uma felicitação calorosa antes de tratar do projeto.

lessons.title: "I am sorry for..." — desculpas simples no dia a dia
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pede desculpas de forma simples no dia a dia com o Google, usando "I am sorry for...", assumindo um pequeno erro com naturalidade e dizendo o próximo passo.
lessons.overview:
In any project, small problems happen. A report is late. An email is forgotten. A document has a mistake. With the Google team on the data center project, the Racional team must answer in a simple and honest way. A short apology is a sign of respect. It shows that you care about the client.

In English, the safe phrase is "I am sorry for...". You do not need long words. You say sorry, you say why, and you say the next step. For example: "I am sorry for the delay. I will send it today." This is clear and calm. A good apology is short, not dramatic.

Racional has more than fifty years of work and many big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and now Google. Trust is the base of every project. When you say sorry in a simple way and then fix the problem, you protect this trust. Today you learn to apologize with confidence and move on.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar a fórmula segura desta aula: "I am sorry for the delay." e "My apologies."

Lembre também do fechamento que dá tranquilidade ao cliente: "It won't happen again." e "I will fix it today." Pedir desculpa, dizer o motivo e indicar o próximo passo.
lessons.situation: Você atrasou o envio de um documento que o time do Google pediu na reunião do data center. Agora você precisa pedir desculpas de forma curta e dizer quando resolve.
lessons.context: I am sorry for the delay. I had a problem on site. Here is the document now. My apologies for the late reply. Thank you for your patience. I will fix it today. It won't happen again.

lessons.title: "What if we...?" — começando proposta condicional
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você abre uma proposta condicional com o Google usando "What if we...?", sugerindo uma alternativa de forma leve e aberta, sem impor.
lessons.overview:
In a meeting, you do not always agree at once. Sometimes the price is high. Sometimes the date is hard. In these moments, you need a soft way to suggest a new idea. The phrase "What if we...?" opens the door. It invites the other person to think with you.

"What if we...?" is not an order. It is a question. It says: "Here is an idea. What do you think?" This is good with the Google team, because they like clear and open talk. You suggest an option, and then you wait. The client feels free to agree or to bring a new idea.

For Racional, every big project needs good solutions. With clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, the team must suggest and decide together. "What if we split the cost?" or "How about a new date?" are simple keys. Today you learn to open a proposal in a light and friendly way.
lessons.intro:
Hoje a estrutura-âncora é "What if we + verbo?" — por exemplo, "What if we split the cost?"

Tenha também à mão a variação "How about...?" e o fechamento aberto "What do you think?" / "Let me know." Você propõe sem impor e deixa a decisão com o cliente.
lessons.situation: Na negociação do data center há um impasse de custo extra. Você quer propor dividir esse custo com o Google, de forma leve e aberta.
lessons.context: I have an idea. What if we split the extra cost? Or, what if we change the date by two weeks? How about a meeting on Friday to decide? Please let me know what you think.

lessons.title: Trocando prazo por preço — "if you give us more time..."
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você troca prazo por preço com o Google usando "If you give us more time, we can lower the price", fazendo uma oferta condicional simples e clara.
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, you give and you take. This is normal. One classic trade is time for price. If the client gives you more days, you can do a better cost. If the date is very tight, the price goes up. This is a simple and fair rule in any project.

The English structure is easy: "If you give us more time, we can lower the price." You name the condition first, and then the offer. With the Google team on the data center, this trade is useful. The Racional team can plan the work better with more time, and the budget stays under control.

Racional has built more than six hundred projects in fifty years. The team knows that a tight schedule costs more, and more time can save money. When you say "If you give us more time..." in a clear way, you show that you think about the project and the client. Today you learn to make this trade in simple English.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura central de hoje é "If you give us more time, we can lower the price."

Memorize o par condição → oferta e o fechamento que pede o aceite: "Does that work for you?" e "in exchange" (em troca). Você liga uma coisa à outra de forma clara.
lessons.situation: O prazo do data center está apertado e encarece o custo. Você quer oferecer ao Google um preço melhor em troca de duas semanas a mais.
lessons.context: The schedule is very tight. If you give us more time, we can lower the price. Two extra weeks help a lot. We can reduce the cost in exchange. Does that work for you?

lessons.title: HSE — Health, Safety & Environment na obra
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre segurança na obra em inglês básico — usando HSE, PPE e "safety comes first" — ao tratar de saúde e segurança com o Google.
lessons.overview:
On any construction site, safety comes first. This is the number one rule. HSE means Health, Safety and Environment. It is the plan to keep people safe and to protect nature. Before any work starts, the team checks the rules and the gear.

Every person on site must wear the right gear. This gear is called PPE (Personal Protective Equipment). A hard hat for the head. Safety boots for the feet. Gloves for the hands. Goggles for the eyes. These items are required. They are not a choice. They protect the team every day.

For the Google data center, HSE is a top topic. Google asks for a safe and clean site. Racional has more than fifty years of work and a strong safety culture. When you say "Safety comes first" in English, you speak the same language as the client. Today you learn the basic words to talk about safety on site.
lessons.intro:
As âncoras de hoje são "Safety comes first." e "You must wear your PPE."

Tenha em mente os quatro itens-chave do PPE: hard hat, safety boots, gloves e goggles. E lembre: o que é obrigatório é required.
lessons.situation: Você acompanha um gerente do Google em uma visita à obra do data center. Você precisa explicar, em inglês simples, as regras de segurança e o PPE obrigatório.
lessons.context: Safety comes first on our site. You must wear your hard hat. Safety boots and gloves are required. Please wear your goggles too. This PPE keeps you safe. We report every accident.

lessons.title: Abrindo a reunião mensal — agenda em inglês
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você abre a reunião mensal com o Google apresentando a agenda em inglês, usando "first", "second", "third" e "let's begin".
lessons.overview:
Every month, the Racional team meets the Google team to talk about the data center. A good meeting has a clear agenda. The agenda is the list of topics. It tells everyone what you will cover today. With a clear agenda, the meeting is short and useful.

To open the monthly meeting, you name the points in order: first, second, and third. For example: "First, the schedule. Second, the budget. Third, safety." Simple words like next and finally help the group follow you. The client always knows where you are.

Racional works with big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These clients like order and clear talk. A good leader opens the meeting with calm and structure. When you say "Let's begin. First on the agenda is the schedule.", you show control. Today you learn to present the agenda in simple English.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você ancora a abertura em "Let's begin." e na ordem "First... Second... Third..."

Tenha à mão os conectores que guiam o grupo: next (a seguir) e finally (por fim). E a frase de moldura: "On the agenda today we have..."
lessons.situation: É a reunião mensal do data center com o Google. Você abre o encontro e apresenta a agenda com os três pontos do dia: prazo, orçamento e segurança.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone. Let's begin. On the agenda today we have three points. First, the schedule. Second, the budget. Finally, safety on site. Let's start with the schedule.

vocab.example: Here is the agenda for today.

lessons.title: "Let's start" — comandos básicos do anfitrião
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz a reunião como anfitrião usando comandos básicos — "Let's start", "Go ahead", "Let's move on" e "That's all for today".
lessons.overview:
The host leads the meeting. The host opens it, gives the word, and closes it. With a few simple commands, you keep the meeting on track. You do not need long phrases. Short words like "Let's start" and "Let's move on" are enough.

When you want someone to speak, you say "Go ahead" or "Over to you". When a topic is done, you say "Let's move on to the next point." At the end, you say "That's all for today. Thank you, everyone." These commands are clear and friendly. They work well with the Google team.

For Racional, the monthly meeting with the client is important. A calm host shows control and respect. With big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, a clear meeting builds trust. When you host in simple English, the client feels safe with the team. Today you learn the basic commands to lead from start to end.
lessons.intro:
Os comandos-âncora de hoje moldam toda a reunião: "Let's start" (abrir), "Go ahead" / "Over to you" (passar a palavra), "Let's move on" (avançar) e "That's all for today" (fechar).

Lembre também de "Any questions?" antes de encerrar e de "Thank you, everyone."
lessons.situation: Você é o anfitrião da reunião mensal do data center com o Google. Precisa abrir, passar a palavra para um colega, avançar de tópico e encerrar — tudo em inglês simples.
lessons.context: Good morning. Let's start. First, the schedule update. Maria, go ahead. Thank you. Let's move on to the next point. Any questions? That's all for today. Thank you, everyone.

lessons.title: Apresentando uma proposta em 3 partes
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta uma proposta ao Google em três partes claras — o quê, em quanto tempo e sob qual condição — usando uma estrutura simples e fácil de seguir.
lessons.overview:
A good proposal is easy to understand. The best way is to present it in three parts: what you do, when you deliver, and the condition. Three short parts. The client follows you with no problem. Google is a North American client, and clear English helps a lot.

At Racional, every big project starts with a clear proposal. The company has more than 620 works and 50 years of experience. For the Google data center, the proposal says what Racional can build, when Racional can deliver, and the price condition. This is the same idea for clients like Microsoft and Amazon.

In a meeting, you open with one line: here is our proposal. Then you say part one, part two, part three. You use simple words: then and finally. This makes the proposal strong and professional. Short sentences are better than one long sentence.
lessons.intro:
Uma boa proposta é fácil de entender. O segredo é dividir em três partes, sempre na mesma ordem.

Parte 1 — o quê: We can build the data center. Parte 2 — quando: In eighteen months. Parte 3 — condição: If you confirm this week. Ligue as partes com then e finally.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google sobre o data center. Eles esperam a sua proposta. Em vez de falar tudo de uma vez, você apresenta em três partes organizadas.
lessons.context: Here is our proposal in three parts. First, we can build the data center. Then, we deliver it in eighteen months. And finally, the price is fixed if you confirm this week.

vocab.example: Our proposal is in three parts.
We can build the data center.
We deliver it in eighteen months.

The scope is the full data center.
The proposal includes design and build.
Here is our proposal in three parts.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue cada parte ao seu conteúdo

exercises.explanation: O quê, quando e a condição: a estrutura de três partes que o Google segue com facilidade.

exercises.title: 2. Qual é a parte 1 da proposta?
exercises.prompt: Você vai apresentar a proposta em três partes. Qual frase é a PARTE 1 (o quê)?

options.whyWrong: Isso é a condição — a parte 3, não a parte 1.

options.text: We can build the data center.

options.whyWrong: Isso é o prazo — a parte 2 (quando), não o quê.

exercises.explanation: Parte 1 = o quê (build the data center). Parte 2 = quando. Parte 3 = condição.

exercises.title: 3. Ligue a segunda parte
exercises.prompt: First, we can build the data center. ___, we deliver it in eighteen months.
exercises.explanation: 'Then' liga a primeira parte (o quê) à segunda (quando).

commonErrors.After: 'After' precisa de complemento. Para ligar as partes, 'Then' é mais simples e natural.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua proposta em três partes
exercises.prompt: Escreva uma proposta ao Google em três partes (o quê, quando, a condição). Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês da aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: Here is our proposal in three parts. First, we can build the data center. Then, we deliver it in eighteen months. And finally, the price is fixed if you confirm this week.
exercises.explanation: Três partes, três frases curtas: o quê, quando e a condição.

exercises.title: 5. Apresente a proposta em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Here is our proposal in three parts. First, we can build the data center. Then, we deliver it in eighteen months. And finally, the price is fixed if you confirm this week.
exercises.translation: Aqui está a nossa proposta em três partes. Primeiro, podemos construir o data center. Depois, entregamos em dezoito meses. E, por fim, o preço fica fixo se você confirmar esta semana.
exercises.prompt: Apresente a sua proposta ao Google em três partes, com calma e ordem. Repita 3 vezes.
exercises.explanation: Anuncie 'three parts', depois first / then / finally. Cada parte em uma frase curta.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, apresente uma proposta sua ao Google em três partes: 'Here is our proposal in three parts. First... Then... And finally...'.
takeaways: I can open with 'Here is our proposal in three parts.'
I can give the 'what' first: 'We can build the data center.'
I can link the parts with then and finally.
I can end with a clear condition.

lessons.title: "Our proposal is..." — estrutura simples para o Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta a proposta ao Google com a estrutura simples "Our proposal is..." — dizendo o valor, o prazo e a validade numa frase clara e segura.
lessons.overview:
There is one strong way to open an offer in English: our proposal is. It is a simple frame. You only add your content. For example: our proposal is to build the data center. Or: our proposal is a fixed price. This line sounds clear and simple, and it sounds professional.

At Racional, the offer to a client like Google must show the value and the total price. Google is a North American client, so you use dollars. You say the number: ten million, fifteen million. Racional has 50 years and more than 620 works, so the price covers real experience and real quality.

A good proposal is also valid for a time, normally thirty days. You say what the price covers, and you say it is worth it. With the frame our proposal is, every executive at Racional can offer the data center to Google with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Use a frase de ouro Our proposal is... para abrir a oferta com firmeza.

Our proposal is a fixed price of fifteen million dollars. / The proposal is valid for thirty days. Lembre: million (milhão), dollars (o Google é americano), valid (válida).
lessons.situation: Momento da oferta na reunião com o Google sobre o data center. Todos esperam você dizer a proposta oficial. Você abre com 'Our proposal is...' e completa com clareza.
lessons.context: Our proposal is simple. We build the full data center for a fixed price. The total is fifteen million dollars. The proposal is valid for thirty days.

vocab.example: We build the full data center.
The proposal is valid for thirty days.
It is valid for thirty days.
The price covers design and build.
The payment is in three steps.
Our proposal is clear and simple.

exercises.explanation: 'Valid' = válida. A proposta vale por um tempo: 'valid for thirty days'.

commonErrors.value: 'Value' é substantivo (valor). Aqui você precisa do adjetivo 'valid' (válida).

exercises.title: 4. Qual moeda usar com o Google?
exercises.prompt: O Google é um cliente americano. Qual frase está certa para o valor?

The total is fifteen dollars million.

Falta a moeda. Diga 'dollars' para o cliente americano.

exercises.explanation: Com o Google, diga o número + 'million dollars': 'fifteen million dollars'.

exercises.title: 5. Diga a proposta em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Our proposal is simple. The total is fifteen million dollars. It is valid for thirty days.
exercises.translation: A nossa proposta é simples. O total é quinze milhões de dólares. Ela é válida por trinta dias.

exercises.explanation: Comece com 'Our proposal is...', diga o total em dollars e a validade.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, apresente a sua proposta ao Google: 'Our proposal is simple. The total is... million dollars. It is valid for thirty days.'.
takeaways: I can open an offer with 'Our proposal is...'
I can say the total in million dollars.
I can say the proposal is valid for thirty days.
I can keep the offer clear and simple.

lessons.title: Critical path — o cronograma que não pode atrasar
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica o critical path do data center em inglês e diz se o projeto está on track ou behind schedule numa reunião com o Google.
lessons.overview:
In a project, some tasks can wait. Some tasks cannot wait. The line of tasks that cannot wait is the critical path. If one task on the critical path is late, the full project is late. This is why the schedule is so important for a client like Google.

At Racional, the team controls the schedule every day. With more than 620 works in 50 years, Racional knows the data center has key tasks: power and cooling. These tasks are on the critical path. The team checks every milestone and every deadline to stay on track.

In a status meeting with Google, you use short status words: on track, on time, behind schedule. Google wants the truth about the schedule first. Then you give the details and the next step. Clear status builds trust.
lessons.intro:
Há tarefas que podem esperar e tarefas que não podem atrasar. A sequência dessas tarefas críticas é o critical path.

Status em frases curtas: We are on track. (no prazo) / We are behind schedule. (atrasados) / This task is on the critical path.
lessons.situation: Reunião de status com o Google sobre o data center. Eles querem saber do cronograma. Você explica o que está no critical path e se o projeto está no prazo.
lessons.context: Let me update the schedule. We are on track. The power system is on the critical path. It is on time. No delays this month.

vocab.example: Power is on the critical path.
Cooling is on the critical path.
The next step is the power test.

exercises.explanation: Diga o status primeiro (on track), depois a tarefa crítica e o próximo passo.

Isso fala de atraso. Para 'no prazo', use 'on track'.

exercises.explanation: 'We are on track' = estamos no prazo. Diga o status primeiro, sempre.

exercises.explanation: Diga qual tarefa é crítica: 'Power is on the critical path.'

exercises.translation: Estamos no prazo. A energia está no caminho crítico. Está em dia. Sem atrasos este mês.
exercises.prompt: Dê o status do data center ao Google: comece pelo status, depois a tarefa crítica. Repita 3 vezes.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, dê um status do data center ao Google: 'We are on track. ... is on the critical path. It is on time. No delays this month.'.
takeaways: I can say if we are on track or behind schedule.
I can name a task on the critical path.
I can say a task is on time.
I can say there are no delays this month.

lessons.title: Conduzindo a reunião — pedindo a palavra
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pede a palavra de forma educada numa reunião com o Google, usando frases curtas como "Can I add something?" e "May I say a word?".
lessons.overview:
In a meeting, you sometimes want to speak. You need to jump in at the right moment, but in a polite way. With a North American client like Google, you ask first. You use a short, kind question: can I add something? or may I say a word? This shows respect.

At Racional, the executives often join meetings with the client and the team. To lead well, you need to add a point at the right time. On the Google data center, you may want to talk about power, safety, or the schedule. A short polite question opens the door for you.

The key is to be soft and clear. You can say sorry to interrupt or if I may. Then you add your point in one short sentence. This makes you a calm and professional voice in the room, the kind of partner Google wants.
lessons.intro:
Para falar numa reunião, peça a palavra com educação.

Frases-âncora: Can I add something? (Posso acrescentar algo?) / May I say a word? (Posso dizer uma palavra?) / Sorry to interrupt. (Desculpe interromper.) Depois, diga o ponto em uma frase curta.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google sobre o data center. A conversa flui e você precisa acrescentar um ponto importante. Você pede a palavra de forma educada antes de falar.
lessons.context: Sorry to interrupt. Can I add something? I have a quick point about the power system. May I say a word before we move on?

vocab.example: I want to add a point.

I want to raise a point.

takeaways: I can ask for the floor with 'Can I add something?'
