lessons.title: Passando a palavra para outra pessoa
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você passa a palavra para outra pessoa numa reunião com o Google, usando frases curtas como "Over to you" e "What do you think?".
lessons.overview:
A good meeting is not only about you. You also hand over the floor to other people. You ask the client or the team to speak. With Google, this is very important. You say over to you or what do you think? This makes the meeting open and fair.

At Racional, the executive often leads the meeting with the team and the client. You may speak first, and then you pass to the engineer or to the client. On the Google data center, you may ask the safety team or the power team for their thoughts. You bring the right voice into the room at the right time.

The words are short and kind: over to you, go ahead, feel free to add. You can also ask any comments? When you pass the floor with respect, the client feels heard. This builds a strong, mature relationship with Google.
lessons.intro:
Numa reunião, você também passa a palavra para outras pessoas.

Frases-âncora: Over to you. (A palavra é sua.) / What do you think? (O que você acha?) / Would you like to add? (Gostaria de acrescentar?) Convide com calma e ouça.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google sobre o data center. Você terminou o seu ponto e quer ouvir o cliente ou o seu time. Você passa a palavra de forma educada.

lessons.title: Recusando educadamente: "I'm afraid we can't..."
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você recusa um pedido do Google de forma educada com "I'm afraid we can't..." e oferece uma alternativa positiva.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the client asks for something you cannot do. You must say no, but in a kind way. The best frame is I'm afraid we can't. It is soft and professional. With a North American client like Google, you never just say no. You say no with respect, and then you offer a way forward.

At Racional, the team negotiates with big clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. With 50 years and more than 620 works, Racional knows its limits. On the data center, Google may ask for a faster date or a lower price. You say I'm afraid we can't do that, but we can offer another plan.

The secret is the second part: but we can. You give an alternative. You ask would that work? This keeps the talk open and positive. A polite no plus a good option is the heart of a strong negotiation with Google.
lessons.intro:
Às vezes você precisa dizer não ao Google — mas com educação.

Frases-âncora: I'm afraid we can't... (Infelizmente não podemos...) / But we can... (Mas podemos...) / Would that work? (Isso funcionaria?) Recuse e ofereça uma alternativa.

lessons.context: I'm afraid we can't deliver in twelve months. That's not possible. But we can deliver in eighteen months. Would that work for you?

vocab.example: But we can offer a new date.
We can speed up the build.
To be honest, it is hard.

takeaways: I can say no in a polite way with 'I'm afraid we can't.'
I can offer an option with 'but we can.'

lessons.title: "I see your point, but..." — discordando com diplomacia
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você discorda do Google com diplomacia, usando "I see your point, but..." — reconhecendo o outro lado antes de apresentar a sua posição.
lessons.overview:
In any meeting with Google, you will not always agree. Sometimes the client has one idea, and Racional has a better idea. This is normal. The goal is not to win the talk. The goal is to find a good answer together.

To disagree in a soft way is a key skill. First, you show respect. You say "I see your point." Then you give your idea. You say "but..." with a calm voice. The American client likes this style. It is clear, but it is also polite.

Racional has more than 50 years and 620 projects. The team knows quality very well. So when you disagree, you protect quality and the client at the same time. A soft "no" keeps the relationship strong and keeps the data center on the right path.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende a discordar sem fechar a porta. A receita é simples: primeiro reconhecer, depois apresentar sua posição.

Três frases-âncora: "I see your point, but..." (entendo seu ponto, mas...), "I understand your concern." (entendo sua preocupação) e "From our side, quality comes first." (do nosso lado, a qualidade vem primeiro). Repita até sair natural.
lessons.situation: Reunião semanal com o Google. O cliente quer acelerar uma etapa. Você acha arriscado para a qualidade. Você precisa discordar com calma.
lessons.context: I see your point. I understand your concern. But from our side, quality comes first. Let me explain. The way I see it, we need more time. I hear you, and I want a good result for everyone.

vocab.example: I see your point. It is a good idea.
I agree, but I have a concern.
It is fast. However, it is risky.
I understand. This is important for you.
From our side, we need more time.
I hear you. Let me explain our view.
I disagree, but I respect your idea.
I have one concern about the date.
To be honest with you, it is too fast.
The way I see it, quality comes first.
Let us look at it differently.
That is a fair point. Thank you.

lessons.title: Quality control — inspections, tests, approvals
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre controle de qualidade no data center do Google — inspeções, testes e aprovações — com vocabulário técnico simples.
lessons.overview:
Quality control is the heart of a data center project. The client, Google, needs a building that works every day, all year. So we check, we test, and we approve every step. Nothing goes to the next stage without a clear approval.

The process is simple to say. First, we make an inspection. Then we run a test. If the work meets the standard, it passes. If not, it fails, and we fix it. After that, we write a short report for the client.

Racional built more than 620 projects and 10 million square meters. The company knows that quality is the name of trust. When Fabrício says "no issues, it passed" to Google, the client feels safe. Good quality control protects the project and the relationship.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você descreve o ciclo de qualidade em frases curtas. A sequência é sempre a mesma: inspect → test → pass/fail → report → next stage.

Frases-âncora: "We inspect the work." (inspecionamos o trabalho), "It passed. No issues." (passou, sem problemas) e "It meets the standard." (atende ao padrão).
lessons.situation: Visita do time do Google à obra. Você apresenta o resultado da inspeção e dos testes de uma etapa do data center.
lessons.context: We run a quality check every week. First, we inspect the work. Then we run a test. The work meets the standard. It passed. No issues. I send the report today. We can go to the next stage.

vocab.example: Quality control is very important here.

I can say "it passed" or "it failed".

I can say "no issues" to the client.

lessons.title: "Thanks for your patience" — relacionamento próximo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fortalece o relacionamento com o Google reconhecendo a paciência e a parceria do cliente com "Thanks for your patience".
lessons.overview:
A big project is a long road. There are good days and hard days. The client, Google, waits, helps, and trusts. So we say thank you. A simple "thanks for your patience" shows respect and care.

This is not only good manners. It is good business. When you value the client, the relationship gets stronger. The American team likes warm and clear words. "Thank you for understanding" and "It is a pleasure to work with you" mean a lot.

Racional has worked with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These are long partnerships, not one job. Fabrício builds trust with every meeting. A small thank you today opens a bigger door going forward.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende a agradecer de forma calorosa e profissional. Pequenas frases criam vínculo de longo prazo.

Frases-âncora: "Thanks for your patience." (obrigado pela paciência), "It is a pleasure to work with you." (é um prazer trabalhar com vocês) e "We really value this partnership." (valorizamos muito esta parceria).
lessons.situation: Fim de uma fase difícil do data center. O Google esperou por uma solução. Você quer agradecer e reforçar a parceria.
lessons.context: Thanks for your patience. We really appreciate your support. It is a pleasure to work with you. We value this partnership a lot. Thank you for understanding. Your trust means a lot to us, going forward.

lessons.title: Reconhecendo o esforço do time do Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reconhece o esforço do time do Google de forma específica e calorosa, elogiando o trabalho com frases simples.
lessons.overview:
People work better when they feel seen. The team from Google works hard on the data center. So we say "great work" and "well done". A clear and warm thank you gives energy to the whole team.

It is good to be specific. You can say the team was fast, or they delivered on time, or they went the extra mile. The American client values this kind of feedback. It is direct, positive, and honest.

Racional leads many teams across 620 projects. Fabrício knows that good teamwork makes a strong result. When you recognize the effort of the client's team, you also build a better partnership for the next stage of the project.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende a elogiar com calor e foco. Elogio bom é específico: diga o que a pessoa fez bem.

Frases-âncora: "Great work, team!" (ótimo trabalho, equipe), "You did a great job." (vocês fizeram um ótimo trabalho) e "You delivered on time." (vocês entregaram no prazo).
lessons.situation: O time do Google entregou uma etapa difícil dentro do prazo. Você quer reconhecer o esforço na reunião.
lessons.context: Great work, team. You did a great job. You were fast, and you delivered on time. This is impressive. We are proud of this teamwork. Well done. We couldn't have done it without you.

lessons.title: Escopo (scope) — what is in / what is out for Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz, em frases simples, o que está dentro (in scope) e o que está fora (out of scope) do contrato com o Google.
lessons.overview:
Every project needs a clear scope. The scope says what we will do and what we will not do. With Google, this is very important. A clear scope stops problems before they start.

Some work is in scope. It is in the contract, and we cover it. Some work is out of scope. It is not in the contract. When something is out of scope, we say it with calm and respect. We do not say a hard "no". We clarify the boundary.

Racional builds complex projects like the data hall of a data center. Fabrício must show, with simple words, what is part of the deal and what is not. A clear scope protects the contract, the budget, and the relationship with the client.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende a desenhar a linha do escopo: o que está incluído e o que não está. Isso protege o contrato.

Frases-âncora: "This is in scope." (isto está no escopo), "That is out of scope." (aquilo está fora do escopo) e "Let me clarify what is included." (deixe-me esclarecer o que está incluído).
lessons.situation: Reunião de alinhamento com o Google. O cliente pergunta se um item entra no contrato. Você explica o que está dentro e o que está fora do escopo.
lessons.context: Let me clarify the scope. The data hall is in scope. It is part of the contract. We cover it. But this new item is out of scope. It is not included. Let us agree on the boundary. This is our responsibility, and that is not.

lessons.title: Mudança de escopo (change order) — "this is a new request"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reconhece um pedido novo do Google e responde, com calma, que ele exige uma mudança de escopo (change order).
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the client wants something new. This is normal in a big project. With Google, a new request is not a problem. But a new request is not in the original scope. So it needs a change order.

A change order is a simple idea. The client asks for something extra. We say "no problem", and then we explain. Extra work means an additional cost and a new schedule. We prepare the numbers and ask the client to approve and confirm.

Racional manages cost and time on 620 projects. Fabrício must protect the contract and stay friendly at the same time. A clear change order keeps the project fair for Racional and for Google. It turns a new request into a calm, simple agreement.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende a transformar um pedido novo em um processo claro. Você não diz "não"; você diz "sim, com uma mudança de escopo".

Frases-âncora: "I understand. This is a new request." (entendo, isto é um pedido novo), "This is out of the original scope." (isto está fora do escopo original) e "No problem. This needs a change order." (sem problema, isto precisa de uma change order).
lessons.situation: O Google pede um item novo, fora do contrato original. Você precisa acolher o pedido e explicar que ele gera custo e prazo adicionais.
lessons.context: I understand. This is a new request. No problem. But this is out of the original scope. It needs a change order. To add this work, we need extra time and an additional cost. I prepare the impact on the schedule. Please approve and confirm.

lessons.title: Commissioning — testando o data center antes da entrega
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, com frases curtas e simples, sobre o commissioning — os testes finais do data center antes da entrega ao Google — dizendo o que está sendo testado e se passou ou falhou.
lessons.overview:
Before Racional hands the data center to Google, the team tests everything. This step is called commissioning. The team turns on the systems, makes a fake problem, and checks the result. A data center is not a normal building. It cannot stop. So every system must work.

The most important test is the power. Google's servers need power all the time. The team tests the backup power. They simulate a power outage. When the main power fails, the UPS takes over in seconds. Then the generator starts. The team also tests the cooling. Each test has a clear result: it passed or it failed.

Racional builds for big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. With 50+ years and 620+ projects, the company knows that commissioning is where trust is built. A clean test report tells Google that the data center is ready for handover. Simple words and clear results are enough.
lessons.intro:
Você vai reportar testes do data center ao Google. Relembre as frases-âncora: "We are testing the backup." (estamos testando o backup) e o resultado: "The test passed." / "The test failed."

Para a queda de energia: "The UPS takes over." (o no-break assume) e "The generator starts." (o gerador liga). Diga sempre o sistema e o resultado.
lessons.situation: Você acompanha o time do Google no commissioning do data center. A cada teste, o cliente quer saber o que foi testado e se passou. Você reporta de forma curta e direta.

lessons.title: Reunião difícil — mantendo o tom calmo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você mantém o tom calmo em uma reunião difícil com o Google — ouvindo, reconhecendo a preocupação e respondendo com frases curtas e profissionais.
lessons.overview:
Every big project has hard meetings. The client is worried. Maybe the client is angry. There is a delay on the data center. In a hard meeting, your best tool is a calm tone. You do not need to speak loud. You need to listen first.

Three simple moves help a lot. First, you listen: "I hear you." Second, you accept the worry: "That is a fair point." Third, you answer slow: "Let me explain." You do not need to agree with everything. You need to show that you listened. Then you say sorry and offer a solution.

Racional works with demanding clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. In 50+ years and 620+ projects, the company learned one thing: a calm voice builds trust. When you stay calm and say "We are committed to this project", Google sees a strong partner, not a problem. Calm words win more than loud words.
lessons.intro:
Você vai responder ao Google em uma reunião tensa. Relembre as frases que baixam a tensão: "I hear you." (eu te ouço) e "That is a fair point." (é uma observação justa).

Depois, conduza para a solução: "Let me explain." (deixe-me explicar) e "We are committed." (estamos comprometidos). Ouça antes de responder.
lessons.situation: O Google está preocupado com um atraso no data center. O clima na sala está tenso. Você precisa ouvir, reconhecer a preocupação e responder com calma.
lessons.context: I hear you. I understand your concern. That is a fair point. The delay is real, and I am sorry. Let me explain. Then we find the solution together. We are committed to this project.

lessons.title: "Let's take a step back" — pausando para alinhar
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa frases simples para pausar uma conversa tensa, resumir o ponto principal e alinhar com o Google, uma coisa de cada vez.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a meeting goes too fast. There are too many topics at once. Everybody talks. Nobody decides. In English, a calm phrase fixes this: "Let's take a step back." It means: stop, breathe, and look at the big picture again.

After this pause, you do three things. You focus on one topic. You summarize the main point. And you check that you and Google are on the same page. You handle one thing at a time. First this, then that. This is how a leader brings order to a hard meeting.

Racional manages huge projects for clients like Google and Microsoft, with 620+ projects and 10M+ m² built. In a complex job, alignment is everything. When you say "Let's take a step back and focus on the main point", you show calm control. Simple words keep the room aligned and moving forward.
lessons.intro:
Você vai pausar e alinhar a conversa com o Google. Relembre as frases-âncora: "Let's take a step back." (vamos dar um passo atrás) e "Let's focus on the main point." (vamos focar no ponto principal).

Para organizar: "One thing at a time." (uma coisa de cada vez) e "Are we on the same page?" (estamos alinhados?).

lessons.title: Reclamação do Google — ouvindo e respondendo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você recebe uma reclamação do Google com calma — ouvindo, reconhecendo o ponto e dizendo que vai analisar e retornar com uma resposta clara.
lessons.overview:
In a big project, the client will raise an issue. Google may send a claim or a complaint. This is normal. A complaint is not an attack. It is information. The way you receive it shows how strong your company is.

The first step is to listen. You do not defend right away. You say: "Let me make sure I understand." Then you accept the point: "That is a valid point." If you do not have the answer now, you say: "I will look into it and get back to you." You promise a clear answer, not a fast excuse. This is fair, and it builds trust.

Racional handles complex contracts for clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. In a data center job, an issue can affect the date or the cost. When you listen well and say "I appreciate that, and I will look into it", Google feels respected. A good response to a complaint protects the relationship and the contract.
lessons.intro:
Você vai receber uma reclamação do Google. Relembre as frases-âncora: "Let me make sure I understand." (deixe-me confirmar que entendi) e "That is a valid point." (é um ponto válido).

Para fechar com calma: "I will look into it." (vou analisar) e "I will get back to you." (eu retorno para você).
lessons.situation: O Google levanta uma reclamação sobre o projeto. Você precisa ouvir, reconhecer o ponto e prometer uma resposta clara — sem se defender na hora.
lessons.context: Thank you for raising this issue. Let me make sure I understand. That is a valid point. This may affect the date. I will look into it, and I will get back to you with a clear answer. I appreciate that.

lessons.title: Compromisso: "We will fix this by Friday"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você assume um compromisso claro com o Google — dizendo o que vai fazer, até quando e que vai manter o cliente informado.
lessons.overview:
After you listen to a problem, you make a commitment. A commitment is a clear promise. You say what you will do and when. The strongest phrase is simple: "We will fix this by Friday." A real date is better than a vague "soon". Google trusts dates, not words.

A good commitment has three parts. You say the action: "We will fix this." You give a deadline: "by Friday." And you promise to follow up: "I will keep you updated." Then you must deliver on time. A promise kept is worth more than any nice speech. "You have my word."

Racional has 50+ years and a name built on delivery. For clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon, a clear commitment is part of the contract relationship. When you say "We will deliver on time, and I will keep you updated", Google sees a partner who is responsible. A clear, kept promise is how trust grows.

Você vai assumir um compromisso com o Google. Relembre as frases-âncora: "We will fix this by Friday." (vamos resolver isso até sexta) e "You have my word." (você tem minha palavra).

Para acompanhar: "I will keep you updated." (vou te manter informado) e "We will deliver on time." (vamos entregar no prazo).

lessons.title: Handover — entregando o data center ao Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma entrega simples do data center ao Google — dizendo que a obra está completa, testada e pronta, e agradecendo a confiança.
lessons.overview:
The big day arrives. The data center is ready. Now Racional makes the handover to Google. The handover is the moment you hand over the building to the client. It is the end of a long project and the start of trust for the next one.

A good handover is calm and organized. You say the work is complete and tested. You walk Google through the checklist and the documentation. You show that every system passed. Then Google can sign off. The data center is fully operational and delivered on time. This is a project milestone.

Racional has delivered 620+ projects in 50+ years for clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. A clean handover is the company's signature: complete, tested, and on time. When you say "The data center is ready, and thank you for your trust", you close one project and open the door to the next front. Delivery is the real promise.
lessons.intro:
Você vai conduzir a entrega do data center ao Google. Relembre as frases-âncora: "The data center is complete and tested." (o data center está completo e testado) e "It is ready." (está pronto).

Para conduzir e fechar: "Let me walk you through the checklist." (deixe-me apresentar a checklist) e "Thank you for your trust." (obrigado pela confiança).

lessons.title: Building rapport over time — long-term Google partnership
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue dizer frases curtas e calorosas que mostram ao Google que a Racional pensa no longo prazo, usando confiança, parceria e a vontade de trabalhar juntos de novo.
lessons.overview:
A long project is not just one meeting. It grows over time. Every meeting, every visit, every message builds the relationship. This is called rapport. Strong rapport makes a big project safe and calm. The Google data center is a long job, so the relationship with Google must be strong and clear.

Racional is more than 50 years old. The company has more than 620 projects and works with big names like Microsoft, Amazon, and now Google. These clients come back because they trust Racional. They know the company is reliable. Trust is the real product. A data center is technical, but the partnership is human.

In this lesson you learn simple words to show this long view. You can say "partnership", "long-term", and "We look forward to working together again". These short phrases tell Google one thing: Racional is here for the next phase, not only for today. A warm sentence builds more than ten promises.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar três frases-âncora que mostram visão de longo prazo: We value this partnership (valorizamos esta parceria), You can count on Racional (você pode contar com a Racional) e We look forward to working together again (esperamos trabalhar juntos de novo).

Atenção à expressão to look forward to: depois dela o verbo vem sempre com -ing (look forward to working, look forward to seeing).

lessons.title: Following up after the meeting — a quick message
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue escrever uma mensagem curta de follow-up depois de uma reunião com o Google, agradecendo, resumindo o combinado e marcando o próximo passo.
lessons.overview:
The meeting ends, but the work is not finished. A short follow-up message keeps things moving. You write "thank you for your time", you summarize the main points, and you confirm the next step. This small message shows that Racional is organized and reliable.

Google is a North American client. Many decisions happen by e-mail and by short notes. After a meeting about the data center, a clear follow-up helps everyone remember what you agreed on. It says when the next action will happen, for example "by Friday". On a big project, this habit saves time and avoids mistakes.

A good follow-up is short and friendly. You do not need long sentences. You say thank you, you list the main points, you set the next step, and you close with "best regards". In this lesson you learn the simple words to write this message in English, the same way Racional works every day with Microsoft and Amazon.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar a estrutura simples do follow-up: Thank you for your time (obrigado pelo seu tempo), As discussed, the next step is... (conforme conversado, o próximo passo é...) e I will confirm by Friday (vou confirmar até sexta).

Termine sempre de forma educada com Best regards (atenciosamente) e Looking forward to the next step.

lessons.title: Discussing contract terms with Google — basics
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar de forma simples sobre os termos básicos de um contrato com o Google — preço, prazo, escopo e responsabilidade — e dizer que prefere tudo por escrito.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a big project, so the contract is very important. The contract has terms: the price, the deadline, the scope, and the responsibility of each side. When the terms are clear, the project is calm. When they are not clear, problems grow. As superintendent of contracts at Racional, this is your daily world.

With a North American client like Google, everything must be fair and in writing. A good partner does not hide things. If something is not clear, you ask to clarify it. If both sides agree, you write it down and you sign. This protects the relationship and the project.

In this lesson you learn the simple English to talk about contract basics. You do not need hard legal words yet. You need short, clear sentences: "This is in the scope", "The price is fixed", "Let us put it in writing". Racional has signed more than 620 projects, and clear terms are always the first step.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar frases-âncora para falar de contrato: What is the scope? (qual é o escopo?), Is this included? (isto está incluído?) e Let us put it in writing (vamos colocar por escrito).

Lembre também de We agree on the terms (concordamos com os termos) e This is fair (isto é justo).
lessons.situation: Primeira conversa sobre o contrato do data center com o Google. Você quer entender o escopo, o preço e o prazo, e deixar tudo por escrito.

lessons.title: "We need to review the contract" — common phrases
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue usar frases simples para pedir tempo e revisar uma proposta do Google com calma, dizendo que vai checar os detalhes e retornar com um retorno.
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, you do not have to answer right away. It is normal and smart to say "we need to review the contract". You take the proposal, you read it carefully, you check the details, and you get back to the client. Asking for time is not weakness. It shows that Racional is serious.

With a big client like Google, the proposal for the data center has many details: price, scope, deadlines, conditions. You want to make sure everything is right before you say yes. So you say "give us a few days" or "I will get back to you by Wednesday". This protects the project and the margin.

In this lesson you learn the polite phrases to slow down and review. You always thank the client first: "we appreciate the offer". Then you ask for time. This is the daily language of a superintendent of contracts, and it keeps the relationship with Google calm and professional.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar frases-âncora para pedir tempo com educação: We need to review the proposal (precisamos revisar a proposta), Give us a few days (nos dê alguns dias) e I will get back to you by Wednesday (eu retorno até quarta).

Comece sempre agradecendo: We appreciate the offer (agradecemos a oferta).

lessons.title: Data hall layout — racks, rows, cages
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue descrever, com palavras simples, o layout de um data hall — racks, fileiras, corredores e gaiolas — e dizer onde cada parte fica.
lessons.overview:
The heart of a data center is the data hall. This is the big room with the machines. Inside, the servers sit in tall metal frames called racks. The racks stand in rows, with an aisle between them so people can walk and work. The layout is the plan of all this.

For the Google project, Racional builds this room with care. The floor is often a raised floor, with space under it for cables and cool air. Some clients use a cage to separate their area for extra security. Every rack, row, and aisle has a place. Good layout means easy access and safe work.

In this lesson you learn the simple English to describe a data hall. You can say "the racks are in rows", "the aisle is between the rows", and "the cage is next to the main room". These short sentences help you walk a Google engineer through the space, the same way Racional already does for Microsoft and Amazon.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar frases-âncora para descrever o data hall: The racks are in rows (os racks ficam em fileiras), The aisle is between the rows (o corredor fica entre as fileiras) e The cage is next to the main room (a gaiola fica ao lado da sala principal).

Use next to (ao lado de) e between (entre) para dizer onde cada parte fica.

lessons.title: Hosting the Google team at the construction site
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue receber o time do Google na obra com frases simples de boas-vindas e segurança, pedindo que usem os equipamentos de proteção e fiquem juntos durante a visita.
lessons.overview:
When the Google team visits the project, you are the host. A good host makes the visitors feel welcome and, above all, safe. A construction site can be dangerous, so safety first is the rule. You greet the team, you give them the right gear, and you show them around.

Before anyone walks in, everyone must wear a helmet, a vest, and safety glasses. You ask the group to follow you and to stay together at all times. This is normal on every Racional site, and serious clients like Google respect it. Safety shows that the company is professional.

In this lesson you learn warm, simple English to host a client visit. You can say "welcome, glad to have you", "please wear a helmet", and "follow me, please". These short phrases let you host the Google team with confidence and care, the way Racional has done on more than 620 projects.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar frases-âncora para receber a visita: Welcome, glad to have you (bem-vindo, é um prazer recebê-lo), Safety first — please wear a helmet (segurança em primeiro lugar — use um capacete) e Please follow me and stay together (por favor, me siga e fiquem juntos).

Use please para soar educado e at all times (o tempo todo) para reforçar a segurança.

lessons.title: Introducing the Racional technical team to Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta o time técnico da Racional ao Google em frases curtas, dizendo o nome e a função de cada pessoa para o cliente saber com quem falar.
lessons.overview:
When the Google team comes to the site, the first thing they need is simple: they need to know who is who. A clear introduction of your technical team opens the door for everything else. The client wants to put a name and a face to each role. This is the first step of trust.

At Racional, the team on a data center project is large. There is a project manager, a safety lead, and a site engineer. Each person is responsible for one part of the work. When you say who handles what, the client knows where to go. This saves time on every meeting and every call.

Racional has built more than 620 projects in 50 years, for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and now Google. A strong team is the reason. Today you learn to present that team in English, one person at a time, so Google always has a clear point of contact.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura é simples e muito repetível: "This is [nome]. He is our [função]." Para mulheres, use She is. Para dizer o que a pessoa faz, use "He is responsible for [área]."

Uma frase por pessoa: aponte, fale o nome, fale a função. Sem pressa.
lessons.situation: Primeira reunião técnica na obra do data center. O time do Google chega e você apresenta os engenheiros e o gestor de segurança da Racional, um por um.
lessons.context: Good morning. Let me introduce our team. This is Carlos. He is our project manager. He is responsible for the schedule. This is Ana. She is our safety lead. Please feel free to reach out to them.

vocab.example: She is in charge of quality.

lessons.title: Talking about budget — "we are within budget"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você confirma ao Google que o projeto está dentro do orçamento, dizendo "we are within budget" e dando um número simples para sustentar a afirmação.
lessons.overview:
In any project, money is a key topic. The Google team wants to know one thing fast: is the data center within budget? When you can say "yes" in clear English, you give the client calm and trust. Good news about cost is good news for everyone.

A project is on track when the work and the money go as planned. To be under budget is even better: it means you spend less than the forecast. At Racional, cost control is part of the culture. The team reports the numbers every phase, so there are no surprises for the client.

Racional has delivered more than 10 million square meters of work in 50 years. Strong budget control is one big reason clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google come back. Today you learn the simple words to report good cost news with confidence.
lessons.intro:
A frase que tranquiliza o cliente é "We are within budget." — estamos dentro do orçamento. Para dar o número, use "We are two percent under budget." (2% abaixo, ótima notícia).

Note: within = dentro de; under = abaixo de. Afirme primeiro, depois dê o número.
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal de acompanhamento com o time financeiro do Google. Eles perguntam como está o custo do data center. Você confirma que está tudo dentro do previsto.
lessons.context: Thank you for the question. I am glad to report good news. We are within budget. In fact, we are two percent under the forecast. Costs are under control. We are on track for this phase.

lessons.title: Over budget conversation — "we are 3% over"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você comunica ao Google, de forma transparente e calma, que o projeto está acima do orçamento, dizendo "we are three percent over" e oferecendo um plano.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the news is not perfect. The project can go over budget. This is normal in big construction. What the Google team values most is honesty. To be transparent early is much better than to hide a problem. A small number shared on time builds trust.

When costs go up, there is always a reason: a change in scope, higher material costs, or a new request. Your job is to explain the reason in simple words and to share a plan to recover. At Racional, the rule is to keep the client informed at every step.

For 50 years, Racional has worked with demanding clients like Microsoft and Amazon. Honest communication is why these partnerships last. Today you learn to give difficult cost news to Google in a calm and clear way.
lessons.intro:
Quando o custo sobe, a chave é a transparência: "To be honest, we are three percent over budget." Diga o número, depois a causa (due to a change in scope) e ofereça um plano.

Use frases curtas: "There is a reason." + "We have a plan." + "I will keep you informed."

lessons.context: I want to be transparent with you. We are three percent over budget. This is due to a change in scope. Material costs went up. We have a plan to recover. I will keep you informed.

lessons.title: UPS — uninterruptible power supply for Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao Google, com vocabulário técnico simples, o que é o UPS de um data center e por que ele garante energia sem interrupção para os servidores.
lessons.overview:
A data center can never stop. The servers must run all day and all night. This is why the UPS, the uninterruptible power supply, is one of the most important systems. For Google, uptime is everything. The UPS protects it.

The idea is simple. If there is a power outage, the UPS uses battery backup and switches over instantly. It keeps the servers running until the generator takes over. The system is redundant and reliable, so the data center never goes dark.

At Racional, power systems are a core part of every data center we build for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. When you can explain the UPS in clear English, you show the client that the team knows the technical work. Today you learn the key words to do exactly that.
lessons.intro:
A ideia central: se a energia da rede cai (a power outage), o UPS entra instantly com energia de bateria (battery backup) até o gerador assumir.

A frase-âncora é simples: "The UPS keeps the servers running." Explique a função primeiro, o detalhe técnico depois.

lessons.context: This is our UPS, the power supply. If there is a power outage, the UPS switches over instantly. It uses battery backup. It keeps the servers running. Then the generator takes over. The system is reliable.

lessons.title: Reading the room — when to speak, when to listen
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você percebe a hora certa de falar e a hora de ouvir numa reunião com o Google, usando frases curtas para mostrar que acompanha e para entrar no momento certo.
lessons.overview:
In a meeting, when you speak is as important as what you say. To read the room means to feel the right moment. Sometimes you talk. Sometimes you listen. The Google team values a partner who knows the difference. This is a quiet skill, but a strong one.

When you listen well, you can use small phrases to show it: "I see.", "That makes sense.", "Please go on." When you want to add a point, you wait for the right moment and then you jump in with care. A short pause is your friend. It shows respect and control.

At Racional, meetings with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google are about trust, not only about facts. A leader who listens first earns the room. Today you learn the simple English to show you are present and to speak at the right time.
lessons.intro:
Para mostrar que você acompanha, use frases curtas: "I see.", "That makes sense.", "Please go on."

Para entrar na conversa na hora certa, use "If I may add..." ou "May I share a thought?". Espere a pausa, depois fale.

lessons.title: Polite interruption — "May I add something?"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você interrompe com educação numa reunião com o Google, pedindo licença para acrescentar um ponto de forma breve e respeitosa.
lessons.overview:
In every meeting, there is a moment when you need to speak before the other person ends. This is an interruption. Done well, it is polite and useful. Done badly, it feels rude. With Google, the right words make all the difference. A short, kind phrase opens the door.

The key is to ask first and to be brief. You can say "May I add something?" or "Sorry to interrupt, just a quick point." You make your point in a few words, and then you let the client continue. "I'll be quick" shows respect for their time.

At Racional, leaders in meetings with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google know that how you interrupt shapes the relationship. A polite point can save time and add value. Today you learn the simple English to interrupt with care and still be heard.
lessons.intro:
A frase-âncora é educada e curta: "May I add something?" ou "Sorry to interrupt — just a quick point."

Peça licença, fale breve, devolva a palavra: "I'll be quick." + "Please continue."

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reporta o progresso do data center ao Google por marcos, dizendo "We hit milestone three" e apontando o próximo passo. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Big projects move forward in milestones. A milestone is a key delivery point. At the Google data center, the Racional team reaches one milestone, and then the next. The client wants to see where the project is today and what comes next.

In a monthly status meeting, you report each milestone. You say what is complete and what is on track. You also say if the work is on schedule or ahead of schedule. Clear reports build trust. Google sees that Racional controls the timeline.

Racional knows this well. In more than fifty years and over 620 projects, the company delivers by milestones. For a global client like Google, simple and honest progress reports are very important. Good English here means good control of the schedule.
lessons.intro:
A frase-âncora é "We hit milestone three." — atingimos o marco 3. Use to hit a milestone = alcançar um marco.

Depois aponte o próximo: "We are on track for milestone four." (no caminho para o marco 4) e diga o ritmo: "on schedule" (no prazo) ou "ahead of schedule" (adiantado).
lessons.situation: Reunião de status mensal com o Google. Eles querem saber o progresso do data center. Você reporta o marco atingido e o que vem a seguir.
lessons.context: Good news on progress. We hit milestone three last week. The main structure is complete, right on schedule. Now we are on track for milestone four. Next up is the data hall, by the end of next month.

lessons.title: Missed milestone conversation with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz com calma a conversa com o Google quando um marco não foi cumprido — reconhece o fato, dá o motivo curto e mostra o plano de recuperação. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a milestone is late. The work slips, and a delivery date is not met. This is hard, but it happens in big projects. With Google, the best way is not to hide it. The best way is to be honest and clear.

The talk has three simple steps. First, you acknowledge the fact: we missed the milestone. Second, you give the reason in one short line. Third, you show the recovery plan: how Racional brings the work back on track. You take responsibility, and then you point to the solution.

For Racional, trust is the base of every client relationship. In over 620 projects, the company learned one thing: a client respects an honest report more than a perfect excuse. With Google, owning the problem and fixing it keeps the partnership strong.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura é em três passos: acknowledge (reconheça), explain (motivo curto) e recover (mostre o plano).

Frases-âncora: "We missed the milestone.", "The reason was a late delivery." e "Here is our recovery plan." Use o passado para o fato e o futuro (will) para a solução.
lessons.situation: Reunião de acompanhamento com o Google. O marco de liberação do data hall não foi atingido na data combinada. Você abre a conversa de frente, com tom firme e calmo.
lessons.context: I want to be straight with you. We missed the data hall milestone. The reason was a late equipment delivery. We take responsibility for this. Here is our recovery plan to bring the schedule back on track next month.

lessons.title: Backup systems — diesel generators, fuel storage
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao Google, de forma simples, como o sistema de backup do data center funciona — geradores a diesel e estoque de combustível que mantêm a energia se a rede falhar. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
A data center must never lose power. Servers run all day and all night. If the grid power fails, the building needs a backup system. This is one of the most important parts of a Google data center.

The backup system uses diesel generators. When grid power fails, the generators switch on automatically. They keep the data center online at full load. To run for many hours, the site has large fuel storage tanks. The system must be reliable every single time.

Racional builds this kind of complex infrastructure. In data center work for clients like Google, power backup is critical. The Racional team installs the generators, the tanks, and the controls. A simple, clear explanation in English helps the client trust the work.
lessons.intro:
O tema é técnico, mas as frases são curtas. Foque em: "The backup system uses diesel generators." e "The generators switch on automatically."

Use também "if grid power fails" (se a rede falhar) e "fuel storage tanks" (tanques de combustível) para explicar a autonomia.
lessons.situation: Visita técnica com a equipe do Google ao data center. Eles perguntam o que acontece se a energia da rede cair. Você explica o sistema de backup em frases simples.
lessons.context: The data center needs power all the time. If grid power fails, our backup system starts. We use diesel generators. They switch on automatically and keep the site at full load. We have large fuel storage tanks for many hours.

lessons.title: Receiving feedback from Google politely
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você recebe feedback do Google de forma educada e profissional — mostra que escutou, concorda quando faz sentido e aponta o próximo passo. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
In every project, the client gives feedback. Google shares points to improve. Some feedback is easy to hear, and some is hard. The way you receive it says a lot about you and about Racional.

Good feedback skills are simple. You listen. You say "That's helpful" or "Good point". You show that you understand: "I see what you mean". Then you point to the next step: "We will look into it." You do not get defensive. You take the feedback on board and you act.

For Racional, listening well is part of strong client work. In over 620 projects, the best teams turn feedback into better results. With a client like Google, a calm and open answer keeps the relationship healthy and shows real professionalism.
lessons.intro:
Receber feedback bem é simples: escute, mostre que entendeu e aponte a ação.

Frases-âncora: "That's helpful.", "I see what you mean.", "Good point." e "We will look into it." Nunca fique na defensiva.
lessons.situation: Reunião de revisão com o Google. Eles dão feedback sobre um ponto do projeto que pode melhorar. Você escuta e responde de forma aberta e educada.

lessons.title: Giving difficult news to the Google team
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você dá uma notícia difícil ao Google de forma profissional — prepara o terreno, dá o fato com calma, mostra o impacto e termina apontando uma saída. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes you must share difficult news with the client. A date moves. A cost goes up. This is never easy, but in big projects it happens. The way you say it makes a big difference for the Google relationship.

The method is calm and clear. First, you soften the start: "I'm afraid I have some difficult news." Then you give the fact in one line. After that, you share the impact: what changes for the project. And you always end with a way forward: "The good news is..." or "What we propose is..."

Racional values being transparent with clients. In over fifty years of work, the company learned that bad news shared early, with a plan, keeps trust strong. With Google, honesty plus a clear next step is always the right path.
lessons.intro:
Dar notícia difícil tem quatro passos: prepare, diga o fato, mostre o impacto e ofereça uma saída.

Frases-âncora: "I'm afraid I have some difficult news.", "Unfortunately, the date will move." e "The good news is we have a plan."
lessons.situation: Reunião com a equipe do Google. Você precisa avisar que uma data vai mudar. Você dá a notícia de frente, com calma, e termina apontando uma saída.
lessons.context: I'm afraid I have some difficult news to share. Unfortunately, the data hall will be ready later than planned. Let me share the impact on the schedule. The good news is we have a plan, and the delay is temporary.

lessons.title: Negotiation language — proposals and counter-proposals
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa linguagem simples de negociação com o Google — faz uma proposta, recebe a contraproposta e busca um meio-termo que funcione para os dois lados. As instruções vêm em português; a prática, em inglês.
lessons.overview:
Negotiation is part of every big contract. With Google, you make a proposal, and the client makes a counter-proposal. Then both sides talk and look for a deal. Good negotiation is calm, clear, and fair.

Simple language helps a lot. You say "How about a new date?" to open an idea. You say "That works for us." to accept, or "Let me come back to you." to think. The goal is to meet halfway and find common ground — a win-win for Racional and Google.

Racional negotiates contracts every day, from scope to schedule. In the data center project, the commercial talks with Google are a core part of the work. Clear, simple English in a negotiation builds trust and protects a strong, long partnership.
lessons.intro:
Negociar tem um ritmo: proposta, contraproposta e meio-termo.

Frases-âncora: "How about...?" (que tal...?), "That works for us." (isso funciona pra nós), "Let me come back to you." (deixe eu retornar) e "Let's meet halfway." (vamos a um meio-termo).
lessons.situation: Reunião comercial com o Google sobre o data center. Você apresenta uma proposta, eles trazem uma contraproposta e vocês buscam um meio-termo que funcione para os dois.
lessons.context: Here is our proposal. How about a new date for the data hall? I understand your point. Instead of that, let's meet halfway. That works for us. It is a win-win for both sides. Let me come back to you tomorrow.

vocab.example: Let me come back to you.
We push for a fair price.

lessons.title: BATNA basics — alternatives in negotiation with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende o conceito de BATNA — a sua melhor alternativa se o acordo com o Google não fechar — e usa frases curtas como "we have other options" para negociar com calma e firmeza.
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, the most important idea is your best alternative. This is your BATNA: what you do if the deal does not happen. When you know your alternative, you are calm. You do not feel fear. You can say "no" with a clear mind.

For Racional, this matters a lot with a client like Google. The data center is a big project. But Racional has 50 years of work, 620 projects, and many clients. So Racional always has a plan B. Another project. Another client. A better time. This is real strength on the table.

A good BATNA does not mean you are aggressive. You still value the partnership. You still want the deal. But you are not desperate. You say: "We want this. But we have other options." This is how a strong company talks to a strong client.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe estas âncoras: "Our best alternative is..." (Nossa melhor alternativa é...) e "We have other options." (Temos outras opções.)

E a frase que mostra firmeza sem ameaça: "We value this partnership, but we are not desperate." (Valorizamos esta parceria, mas não estamos desesperados.)
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião comercial com o Google, você define internamente a melhor alternativa da Racional caso o acordo do data center não feche. Isso muda a sua postura na mesa.
lessons.context: Let me be clear on our plan. If this deal does not work, our best alternative is the new project in the south. So we can stay calm. We value this partnership with Google. But we are not desperate. We have other options.

lessons.title: Cooling deep dive — air, water, free cooling
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao Google, em inglês simples, os três tipos de resfriamento de um data center — air, water e free cooling — dizendo o que cada um faz.
lessons.overview:
Servers make a lot of heat. Too much heat is a big problem in a data center. So cooling is one of the most important systems on the site. For a client like Google, good cooling means safe servers and a low energy bill.

There are three main types. Air cooling uses cold air to cool the servers. It is simple and common. Water cooling uses water to remove the heat. Water is more efficient for a high load. Free cooling uses the cold outside air when the weather is cool. It saves a lot of energy.

For Racional, this is a strong point. The company builds big projects for Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. A clear cooling plan shows the client that Racional knows how to save energy and keep the servers cool. The goal today is to say what each method does, in simple words.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe a estrutura: método + o que faz + vantagem.

Exemplos-âncora: "Air cooling uses cold air." · "Water cooling removes the heat." · "Free cooling uses outside air and saves energy."
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com o time de engenharia do Google sobre eficiência energética. Eles querem entender qual solução de resfriamento a Racional propõe e por quê.
lessons.context: Let me explain the cooling. Air cooling uses cold air to cool the servers. Water cooling uses water to remove the heat. It is good for a high load. Free cooling uses the cold outside air. It saves a lot of energy.

vocab.example: Cooling is very important for the servers.
Servers make a lot of heat.
Free cooling helps us save energy.
We use the cold outside air.

lessons.title: Rebuilding the relationship after a tough meeting
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reconstrói o relacionamento com o Google depois de uma reunião difícil, usando frases curtas e calmas como "I value our partnership" e "let's move forward".
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a meeting is tough. People do not agree. There is some tension. This is normal in business. But the relationship is more important than one hard meeting. A good leader knows how to start fresh after a difficult day.

For Racional, the relationship with Google is for years, not for one meeting. The data center is a long project. So after a tough talk, the goal is simple: clear the air and move forward. You say: "I value our partnership. Let's start fresh." Calm words rebuild trust.

This skill is very important for a leader like you. Racional works with big clients — Google, Microsoft, Amazon. Strong relationships keep these clients for the long term. After a hard meeting, the right words show that you are calm, mature, and ready to find common ground.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe as âncoras de reconciliação: "I value our partnership." (Valorizo nossa parceria.) · "Let's start fresh." (Vamos recomeçar.) · "Let's move forward." (Vamos seguir em frente.)

E a frase que mostra escuta: "I hear you." (Eu te ouço / entendo o seu lado.)
lessons.situation: Depois de uma reunião tensa com o Google sobre preço, você liga ou envia uma mensagem para reduzir a tensão e recuperar a boa relação antes do próximo encontro.
lessons.context: I know the last meeting was tough. I want to clear the air. I value our partnership a lot. There are no hard feelings. Let's start fresh and move forward. I hear you, and I think we can find common ground.

lessons.title: "We need to talk" — preparing the Google client
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você prepara o cliente do Google antes de uma notícia importante, usando frases curtas como "I'd like to share an update" e "it's not all good news".
lessons.overview:
Sometimes you have news that is not easy. A delay. A change. A new cost. A good leader does not surprise the client. First, you give a heads-up. You say: "I'd like to share an update. It is important." This prepares the client before the details.

For Racional and Google, this is about trust. The data center is a big project with big numbers. When you prepare the client ahead of time, you show respect. You say: "It's not all good news, but I have a plan." This is much better than a bad surprise in a meeting.

This skill helps a leader like you in every client relationship. Racional works with Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. These clients value honesty. When you set the stage before hard news, you stay calm and in control. You show that you are honest and ready with a solution.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe as âncoras: "I'd like to share an update." (Gostaria de compartilhar uma atualização.) · "It's important." (É importante.)

E a frase honesta que prepara o cliente: "It's not all good news, but I have a plan." (Não é só boa notícia, mas eu tenho um plano.)
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião formal, você dá um aviso prévio ao contato do Google: há uma notícia importante sobre o cronograma do data center, e você quer prepará-lo com calma.
lessons.context: I'd like to share an update with you. It is important. Before we go into the details, I want to prepare you. It's not all good news. But I have a plan, and I'd like to hear your view too. Let's set the stage first.

lessons.title: Defending margin to Google — why our price is fair
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você defende a margem da Racional ao Google em inglês simples, explicando que o preço é justo e reflete valor, com frases como "the price is fair" e "it includes quality".
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, the client often asks for a lower price. This is normal. But a good price is not just a number. It is value for money. Your job is to show that the price is fair and that it reflects value. You say: "The price is fair. It includes quality and on-time delivery."

For Racional, this is very important with Google. The data center needs high quality and a safe schedule. Racional has 50 years of work and 620 projects. This experience has a real cost, and it is worth it. A low price with low quality is a big risk for the client.

When the client pushes on price, you stay calm. You say: "I understand your concern." Then you explain what is included. If needed, you can adjust the scope, not just lower the price. This protects the margin and the quality at the same time. This is how a strong company defends its value.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe as âncoras: "The price is fair." (O preço é justo.) · "It includes quality and on-time delivery." (Inclui qualidade e entrega no prazo.)

E a frase que acolhe sem ceder: "I understand your concern, but it's worth it." (Entendo sua preocupação, mas vale a pena.)
lessons.situation: O Google pede um desconto no data center. Você defende o preço com calma, explicando que ele reflete qualidade, prazo e o valor da experiência da Racional.
lessons.context: I understand your concern about the price. But the price is fair. It reflects value. It includes high quality and on-time delivery. This is worth it for a project like this. If you want, we can adjust the scope. But I don't want to lower the quality.

exercises.explanation: Acolha, explique o valor e mostre o que está incluído. Assim você defende a margem.

lessons.title: Discussing risk — "if X happens, we will Y"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala de risco com o Google usando a estrutura "if X happens, we will Y", explicando consequências e ações de forma clara e sem surpresas.
lessons.overview:
Every big project has risk. A delay. A change order. A problem with the weather. A good leader talks about risk in a calm, clear way. The best tool is one simple structure: "If this happens, we will do that." This shows the client you are ready for any case.

For Racional and Google, this builds trust. The data center is a long project. When you say "If the schedule changes, we will inform you right away," the client knows there will be no surprises. You take responsibility and you show a plan for each case.

This structure also covers hard cases like force majeure — a big event no one can control, like a storm or a strike. You say: "In that case, we will revise the schedule and inform you." Clear words about risk show that Racional is a strong, honest partner for Google.
lessons.intro:
Antes de praticar, fixe a estrutura-mestra: "If X happens, we will Y." (Se X acontecer, nós faremos Y.)

Exemplos-âncora: "If there is a delay, we will inform you." · "In that case, we will revise the schedule."
lessons.situation: Na negociação do data center com o Google, você fala sobre riscos do projeto — atrasos, mudanças de escopo, force majeure — e explica o que a Racional fará em cada caso.
lessons.context: Let me talk about risk. If there is a delay, we will inform you right away. If you ask for a change, we will send a change order. If there is a force majeure event, we will revise the schedule. In that case, there will be no surprises.

lessons.title: Security — physical and digital, perimeter at Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre segurança no data center do Google em inglês, separando segurança física e digital e descrevendo o controle de perímetro com frases curtas e simples.
lessons.overview:
Security is very important for Google. A data center keeps data from the whole world. So nobody enters without permission. There are two kinds of security. The first is physical security. The second is digital security. Physical security protects the place. Digital security protects the data.

Physical security starts at the perimeter. The perimeter is the line around the site. Racional builds a strong fence there. There are cameras and one main gate. Every worker needs a badge. The badge gives access to the site. Some areas are restricted. Only authorized people can enter.

Racional knows this work well. The company built data centers for Microsoft, Amazon, and now for Google. Security has many layers. You start at the fence and the gate. Then you control every door inside. When you talk about security with Google, always say one word first: physical or digital. This is simple and clear.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai usar duas frases-âncora bem simples: "Security has two layers: physical and digital." (A segurança tem duas camadas: física e digital) e "Every worker needs a badge to enter." (Cada trabalhador precisa de um crachá para entrar).

Lembre também de "Only authorized people can enter." (Só pessoas autorizadas podem entrar). São frases curtas e fáceis de repetir.
lessons.situation: Numa visita técnica, o time de segurança do Google quer entender como a Racional protege o canteiro e o futuro data center. Você apresenta as camadas de segurança.
lessons.context: Security has two layers. The first is physical. The second is digital. Physical security starts at the perimeter. We have a fence, cameras, and one gate. Every worker needs a badge. Only authorized people can enter.

lessons.title: Bridging cultures — Brazilian vs. American style with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reconhece a diferença entre o estilo brasileiro e o americano de comunicação e escolhe frases curtas para ir ao ponto com o Google.
lessons.overview:
Brazilians and Americans talk in different ways. This is not good or bad. It is only a different communication style. The Brazilian style likes small talk first. We build the relationship, and then we talk about business. The American style is more direct. Google likes to get to the point fast.

For Fabrício, this is important every week. He talks with Google about the data center. The Google team wants the next steps and a clear plan. They read short and direct as respect for their time. So Fabrício keeps the small talk short. Then he goes to the point. A simple phrase helps: "Just to be clear, here is the plan."

You do not need to change your culture. You only adjust the rhythm. A little less small talk, a little more clarity. Racional works with American clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. With a small adjustment, both sides find common ground. This makes every meeting more efficient.
lessons.intro:
Suas frases-âncora hoje são bem objetivas: "Let's get to the point." (Vamos ao ponto) e "Just to be clear..." (Só para deixar claro...).

Para fechar, use "What are the next steps?" (Quais são os próximos passos?). São pontes simples para soar direto, do jeito que o Google gosta.
lessons.situation: Você percebe que, nas reuniões, o time do Google fica impaciente quando você dá muitas voltas antes do assunto. Hoje você ajusta o estilo.
lessons.context: We like small talk first. That is our style. But Google is more direct. So let's get to the point. Just to be clear, here is the plan. And what are the next steps?

vocab.example: We have a different communication style.

lessons.title: American directness — adjusting your communication style
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você responde a um feedback direto do Google de forma respeitosa, concordando ou discordando com frases curtas e claras.
lessons.overview:
Americans are very direct. Directness is normal for Google. They give honest feedback. Sometimes the feedback is hard to hear. But it is not personal. So do not take it personally. It is only about the work. This is the American way, and it is a sign of trust.

For Fabrício, this is a daily skill with Google. He needs simple phrases to answer. To agree, he can say "Fair point." To disagree in a soft way, he can say "I see it differently." To start a sentence, "To be honest..." works well. These phrases are short, clear, and straightforward.

Fabrício can also push back in a polite way. He can show a concern and stay respectful. "I see it differently, but let's solve it together." This is good for the data center project. Racional and Google do not always agree. But with clear and honest words, both sides move forward and find a good answer.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você treina respostas curtas a um feedback direto. Frases-âncora: "Fair point." (Boa observação / tem razão) e "I see it differently." (Eu vejo de forma diferente).

Para abrir com honestidade, use "To be honest..." (Para ser honesto...). E lembre: feedback direto não é pessoal.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião, um gerente do Google dá um feedback bem direto sobre um prazo. Você responde com calma, concordando ou discordando de forma respeitosa.
lessons.context: Thank you for the honest feedback. To be honest, I see it differently. But that is a fair point. I have one concern about the deadline. Let's solve it together.

lessons.title: Contract clauses — penalty, bonus, liability
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre cláusulas básicas do contrato com o Google em inglês simples, citando multa, bônus e responsabilidade.
lessons.overview:
A contract has many clauses. A clause is one rule in the contract. Three clauses are very important for Fabrício. The first is the penalty. The penalty is money you pay for a delay. The second is the bonus. The bonus is money you get for early completion. The third is liability. Liability is who pays when there is a problem.

For the Google data center, these clauses protect both sides. Google wants the project on time. So the contract has a penalty for a delay and a bonus for early work. This is fair. Fabrício always wants to cap the penalty. To cap means to set a top limit. A penalty without a cap is a big risk for Racional.

Fabrício is the Superintendent of Contracts at Racional. He reviews every clause with care. He talks about the terms with Google in a calm and clear way. "In return for a bonus, we accept a penalty." Good clauses are good for both sides. They make a strong contract for the data center.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você usa três palavras-chave do contrato: penalty (multa), bonus (bônus) e liability (responsabilidade).

Frases-âncora: "We want to cap the penalty." (Queremos limitar a multa) e "In return, we accept a bonus." (Em troca, aceitamos um bônus). Frases curtas, de negociação.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião jurídica e comercial, você discute com o Google as cláusulas de multa por atraso, bônus por entrega antecipada e responsabilidade.
lessons.context: The contract has three clauses. There is a penalty for a delay. There is a bonus for early completion. And there is liability for problems. We want to cap the penalty. In return, we accept the bonus. This is fair for both sides.

lessons.title: Force majeure — talking about unexpected events
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao Google um atraso causado por força maior em inglês simples, ligando o evento ao impacto no prazo.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a project has a problem. The problem is not your fault. It is an unexpected event. We call this force majeure. It is an event beyond our control. For example, very heavy rain stops the work. Or a supplier is late with a delivery. These events are not the company's fault.

For the Google data center, Fabrício must explain these events fast and in a clear way. First, he informs Google. Then he says the cause and the impact. "Heavy rain stopped the work for one week. This will affect the schedule." When the cause is force majeure, the team can ask to extend the deadline. This is normal in big contracts.

Racional has more than fifty years of experience. The company knows that rain, suppliers, and other circumstances can delay a project. The key is honest and fast communication. Fabrício keeps Google informed. He explains the event, the impact, and the new plan. This builds trust, even when something goes wrong.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você liga um evento ao seu efeito no prazo. Frases-âncora: "This is beyond our control." (Isso está fora do nosso controle) e "This will affect the schedule." (Isso vai afetar o cronograma).

Para pedir mais prazo: "We need to extend the deadline." (Precisamos estender o prazo). Avise o Google sempre rápido.
lessons.situation: Uma chuva muito forte parou a obra do data center por uma semana. Você precisa informar o Google, explicar que foi força maior e pedir mais prazo.
lessons.context: We have an unexpected event. This is beyond our control. Heavy rain stopped the work for one week. This will affect the schedule. We need to extend the deadline. We inform you now, very fast.

vocab.example: This is a force majeure event.

lessons.title: Sustainability — LEED, water use, renewable energy
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre sustentabilidade no data center do Google em inglês simples, citando certificação LEED, uso de água e energia renovável.
lessons.overview:
Sustainability is very important for Google. A data center uses a lot of power and water. So Google wants a green building. One key word is LEED certification. LEED is a global mark for a green building. Google wants to aim for LEED on the new data center. This is a clear goal for the project.

There are three big areas. The first is water use. The team works to reduce the water and to recycle it. The second is renewable energy, like solar power. Clean energy lowers the carbon footprint. The third is waste. On the site, the team must reduce and recycle the waste. All of this makes the building more efficient.

For Fabrício, sustainability is a strong selling point with Google. Racional has more than fifty years and many green projects. The company can build a data center that is fast, safe, and green. "Sustainability is a top priority for us." This is the language Google wants to hear.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você fala de sustentabilidade com três pilares: water use (uso de água), renewable energy (energia renovável) e waste (resíduos).

Frases-âncora: "We aim for LEED certification." (Buscamos a certificação LEED) e "Sustainability is a top priority." (Sustentabilidade é prioridade máxima).

lessons.title: Long-term partnership language with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa frases simples de parceria de longo prazo com o Google — falando de confiança, apoio e projetos futuros — para mostrar que a Racional quer construir junto por muitos anos.
lessons.overview:
A long-term partnership is more than one project. The Racional Engineering team builds the Google data center today. But the goal is bigger. The goal is to work together for many years. Big clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon want partners they can trust. Trust is the base of every long relationship.

In 50 years, Racional built 620+ projects. Why do clients come back? Because the company is reliable. The team supports the client at every stage. The client can count on Racional. This is the message Fabrício gives to Google: "We are here for the long term."

Long-term language is warm and simple. You talk about "we" and "together", not only "I". You say "We value this partnership." You say "You can count on us." These short phrases open the door to future projects. One good data center today can become many projects tomorrow.
lessons.intro:
Estamos no M5: o relacionamento maduro com o Google. A obra vai bem; agora você mostra que a Racional pensa em anos, não em uma obra só.

Guarde três frases-âncora: "We value this partnership." (valorizamos esta parceria), "You can count on us." (podem contar conosco) e "We want to work together for the long term." (queremos trabalhar juntos no longo prazo). Fale sempre de "we" e "together".
lessons.situation: Jantar de relacionamento depois de uma fase importante do data center. O diretor do Google elogia a obra. É o momento de plantar a semente da parceria de longo prazo.
lessons.context: Thank you. We value this partnership. We trust your team. You can count on us. We want to work together for the long term. We are here for you, side by side.

vocab.example: We think about the long term.
We want future projects with you.
We are committed to this project.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo ao sentido
exercises.explanation: Quatro blocos que transformam 'fornecedor de uma obra' em 'parceiro de anos'.

exercises.title: 2. Qual frase abre a parceria de longo prazo?
exercises.prompt: Você quer mostrar ao Google que pensa além desta obra. A melhor frase é:

options.whyWrong: Isso fecha a porta. Você quer abrir o futuro, não encerrá-lo.
Isso limita você a um job. A mensagem de parceria é de continuidade.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase de confiança

exercises.explanation: 'You can count on us' (ou 'rely on us') diz ao cliente que ele pode contar com a Racional.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua mensagem de parceria

exercises.modelAnswer: We value this partnership. You can count on us. We want to work together for the long term, on future projects too.
exercises.explanation: Valorizar + confiança + longo prazo. Esse é o roteiro que abre a porta do próximo contrato.

exercises.title: 5. Fale do relacionamento no jantar

exercises.translation: Valorizamos esta parceria. Vocês podem contar conosco. Queremos trabalhar juntos no longo prazo.
exercises.prompt: Responda ao elogio do diretor do Google plantando a semente da parceria de longo prazo. Tom caloroso.
exercises.explanation: Sorria ao falar. Repita até sair leve. Relacionamento de anos começa numa frase bem dita.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em inglês: agradeça ao Google, diga que valorizam a parceria e que o cliente pode contar com a Racional no longo prazo. Cerca de 15 a 20 segundos.
takeaways: I can say we value this partnership.

I can talk about the long term.

lessons.title: "We have grown together" — narrating the relationship
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conta a história do relacionamento com o Google em frases simples — 'we have grown together' — falando de onde vocês começaram, o que superaram e onde estão hoje.
lessons.overview:
Every strong relationship has a story. The story has a start, a hard part, and a happy end. With Google, the Racional team can tell this story. "When we started, we were new. We faced challenges. We solved them together. Now we are stronger." A good story shows the client that the partnership is real.

People remember stories more than numbers. Racional has 50+ years and 620+ projects. But the best way to win trust is to say: "Look how far we have come together." The data center had hard days. The team and Google solved problems step by step. Every milestone is part of the same journey.

The anchor phrase is simple: "We have grown together." It means we are not the same as before — we learned, we are stronger, and we are proud. This is warm, human language. It turns a construction project into a true partnership.
lessons.intro:
Ainda no M5. Hoje você aprende a contar a história da parceria. Narrar a jornada vale mais que listar números.

Use a linha do tempo em três tempos: passado ("When we started..."), caminho ("We faced challenges together") e presente ("Now we are stronger"). A frase-âncora é "We have grown together." (crescemos juntos). Não esconda os desafios — eles provam que a parceria é forte.
lessons.situation: Evento de aniversário do projeto. O Google pede que você diga algumas palavras sobre o caminho até aqui. Você conta a história da parceria, em inglês.
lessons.context: When we started, we were new. The first months were hard. We faced challenges. But we solved them together, step by step. Now we are stronger. We have grown together. I am very proud.

vocab.example: When we started, we were new.
Look how far we have come.

exercises.explanation: 'We have grown together' é a frase-âncora da aula. Curta e forte.

exercises.explanation: 'When we started, we were new' abre a história. Mostra de onde vocês vieram.

exercises.title: 4. Qual frase fecha bem a história?

options.whyWrong: Isso é negativo e fecha mal. A história é de superação.

options.text: I do not remember the start.
options.whyWrong: Você quer mostrar a jornada, não esquecê-la.

exercises.explanation: Fale devagar e com orgulho. A história em três tempos é fácil de lembrar.

takeaways: I can start the story with 'when we started'.
I can say we faced challenges together.
I can say now we are stronger.
I can say 'we have grown together'.
I can sound proud of the journey.
