lessons.title: Re-negotiation — when conditions change with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa frases simples para re-negociar com o Google quando as condições mudam — falando abertamente, propondo opções e buscando uma solução justa para os dois lados.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes conditions change in a project. Steel costs more. The scope grows. The plan needs new dates. When this happens, the team must talk to Google in an open and calm way. This is re-negotiation. It is normal in big projects, even with a strong partner.

Racional has 50+ years of contracts. The company knows that good re-negotiation is not a fight. It is a talk between partners. You explain the new conditions. You bring the facts. Then you look for a fair solution for both sides. A good deal is a win-win: both sides are happy.

The language is simple and honest. You say "Conditions have changed." You say "Let me explain this openly." You say "One option is to share the cost." These phrases keep the relationship safe. You protect the partnership and the project at the same time, going forward.
lessons.intro:
Continuamos no M5, agora no lado comercial. Re-negociar não é brigar: é conversar entre parceiros quando algo muda.

Guarde três frases-âncora: "Conditions have changed." (as condições mudaram), "One option is to share the cost." (uma opção é dividir o custo) e "Let's find a fair solution." (vamos achar uma solução justa). Fale aberto e calmo.
lessons.situation: O custo do aço subiu muito e o escopo do data center cresceu. Você precisa abrir o assunto com o Google e propor uma saída justa para os dois lados.
lessons.context: Thank you for your time. Conditions have changed. The cost went up. The scope is bigger now. Let me explain this openly. One option is to share the cost. Let's find a fair solution, going forward.

vocab.example: We need to re-negotiate the price.
We need to adjust the plan.
I want to raise one point.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo ao sentido
exercises.explanation: Quatro blocos que mantêm a re-negociação calma e justa.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva a abertura da re-negociação
exercises.prompt: Escreva 1-2 frases para o Google: diga que as condições mudaram e proponha dividir o custo ou achar uma solução justa. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês da aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: Conditions have changed and the cost went up. One option is to share the cost. Let's find a fair solution, going forward.
exercises.explanation: Fato + opção + solução justa. Esse é o roteiro de uma re-negociação madura.

exercises.title: 3. Qual frase abre bem o assunto?
exercises.prompt: Você precisa abrir a re-negociação sem criar atrito. A melhor frase é:

options.text: Conditions have changed. Let me explain this openly.

options.whyWrong: Isso soa como exigência. Re-negociação é conversa, não ordem.

options.text: This is your problem, not ours.
options.whyWrong: Isso quebra a parceria. Você quer uma solução para os dois lados.

exercises.title: 4. Monte a frase da opção
exercises.explanation: 'One option is to share the cost' propõe uma saída sem impor. Mantém o tom de parceria.

exercises.title: 5. Abra a re-negociação em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Conditions have changed. Let me explain this openly. One option is to share the cost. Let's find a fair solution.
exercises.translation: As condições mudaram. Deixe-me explicar isto abertamente. Uma opção é dividir o custo. Vamos achar uma solução justa.
exercises.prompt: Abra com o Google o tema do custo do aço. Tom calmo, aberto e voltado para a solução.
exercises.explanation: Fale devagar. A calma na voz mostra que você quer resolver, não brigar.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em inglês: diga ao Google que as condições mudaram, explique de forma aberta e proponha dividir o custo como uma solução justa. Cerca de 15 a 20 segundos.
takeaways: I can say 'conditions have changed'.
I can explain the new cost openly.
I can say 'one option is to share the cost'.
I can ask for a fair solution.
I can keep the talk calm, going forward.

lessons.title: Talking about claims — calmly, with facts
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta um claim ao Google com calma e fatos — mostrando a evidência, o custo extra e os dias extras, para chegar a um acordo justo.
lessons.overview:
In big projects, a claim is normal. A claim is a formal request. You ask for extra time or extra money for extra work. With Google, the Racional team must present claims in a calm and clear way. The secret is simple: stay calm and use the facts.

A good claim has evidence. You show the record, the dates, and the photos. You show the change order that Google approved. With the facts on the table, the client can see the truth. "Based on this, we are entitled to extra days." There is no fight — only data.

Racional has 50+ years of contracts and knows how to settle a claim well. You walk the client through the facts, step by step. You ask for what is fair: additional cost or extra days. A calm, clear claim protects the project and the relationship at the same time.
lessons.intro:
Ainda no M5 comercial. Apresentar um claim não é reclamar — é mostrar fatos e pedir o que é justo, com calma.

Guarde três frases-âncora: "Let me walk you through the facts." (deixe-me mostrar os fatos), "Based on this, we are entitled to extra days." (com base nisto, temos direito a dias extras) e "As you can see, the change order was approved." (como você vê, a mudança foi aprovada). Calma e fatos.
lessons.situation: Houve trabalho extra no data center por causa de uma mudança aprovada. Você precisa apresentar o claim ao Google com calma, mostrando a evidência.
lessons.context: Thank you. Let me walk you through the facts. Here is the record. The change order was approved. As you can see, we did extra work. Based on this, we are entitled to extra days and additional cost. Let's settle it calmly.

vocab.example: Let me walk you through it.
We are entitled to extra days.
As you can see, it is clear.

options.text: This is not fair to us.
options.whyWrong: Emoção atrapalha. Mostre os fatos e a evidência primeiro.

exercises.explanation: Quatro blocos que sustentam um claim claro e calmo.

exercises.title: 3. Ouça e escreva

exercises.explanation: 'Let me walk you through the facts' é a frase que abre o claim com calma.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva a base do claim
exercises.prompt: Escreva 1-2 frases para o Google: mostre que a mudança foi aprovada e diga que a Racional tem direito a dias extras ou custo adicional. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês da aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: The change order was approved. As you can see, we did extra work. Based on this, we are entitled to extra days and additional cost.
exercises.explanation: Fato + evidência + pedido justo. Esse é o roteiro de um claim maduro.

exercises.title: 5. Apresente o claim em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Let me walk you through the facts. The change order was approved. Based on this, we are entitled to extra days.
exercises.translation: Deixe-me mostrar os fatos. A ordem de mudança foi aprovada. Com base nisto, temos direito a dias extras.
exercises.prompt: Apresente o claim ao Google com calma, mostrando a evidência e pedindo o que é justo.
exercises.explanation: Fale devagar e firme. A calma na voz dá força aos fatos.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em inglês: apresente o claim ao Google — diga que vai mostrar os fatos, que a mudança foi aprovada e que a Racional tem direito a dias extras. Cerca de 15 a 20 segundos.
takeaways: I can say 'let me walk you through the facts'.
I can show the change order and the evidence.
I can say we are entitled to extra days.
I can ask for additional cost calmly.
I can settle a claim with facts.

lessons.title: Permits & licenses — environmental, civil, electrical
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala em frases simples sobre licenças e alvarás do data center — ambiental, civil e elétrica — dizendo o que está aprovado, em andamento e pronto para revisão.
lessons.overview:
No big project starts without permits and licenses. A permit is an official paper. It says the work can begin. For a data center, Google needs many of them: an environmental permit, a civil permit, and an electrical license. Without them, the work cannot move.

Racional has 50+ years and 620+ projects, so the team knows the local authority and the rules well. The team must apply for each permit, wait for the authority to issue it, and keep every paper valid. Compliance means we follow the law at every step. A late permit can stop the whole site.

In a meeting with Google, Fabrício gives the permit status in simple words. He says what is approved, what is in progress, and what is ready for review. He talks about the deadline for each one. Clear permit status gives the client peace of mind and keeps the data center on track.
lessons.intro:
Aula técnica do M5: licenças e alvarás do data center. Você não vai explicar a lei — só dar o status em inglês simples.

Guarde três frases-âncora: "The civil permit is approved." (o alvará civil está aprovado), "The environmental permit is in progress." (a licença ambiental está em andamento) e "The electrical license is ready for review." (a licença elétrica está pronta para revisão).
lessons.situation: Reunião de status com o Google. Eles querem saber a situação das licenças do data center. Você dá o status de cada uma em inglês.
lessons.context: Here is the permit status. The civil permit is approved. The environmental permit is in progress. The electrical license is ready for review. We applied for all of them. We follow full compliance.

vocab.example: The electrical license is in progress.
The authority will issue it soon.
We apply for the permit today.
We renew the license every year.

exercises.title: 1. Monte a frase do status
exercises.explanation: 'The civil permit is approved' dá o status de forma curta e clara.

exercises.title: 2. Complete o status
exercises.prompt: The environmental permit is in ___.
exercises.explanation: 'In progress' significa 'em andamento'. É o status para algo que ainda não terminou.

commonErrors.in progressing: Em inglês é só 'in progress', sem '-ing' extra.

exercises.title: 3. Qual frase diz que falta pouco?
exercises.prompt: A licença elétrica está quase pronta. A autoridade só precisa olhar. A melhor frase é:

options.text: The electrical license is ready for review.

options.whyWrong: Isso diz que não há licença. Você quer dizer que ela está quase pronta.

options.text: The electrical license is not started.
options.whyWrong: Isso diz que nem começou. 'Ready for review' é o contrário: está quase no fim.

exercises.title: 4. Ligue o termo ao sentido
exercises.explanation: Quatro palavras-chave para dar o status de qualquer licença.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva o status das licenças
exercises.prompt: Escreva 1-2 frases para o Google com o status: uma licença aprovada e outra em andamento. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês da aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: The civil permit is approved. The environmental permit is in progress. We applied for the electrical license too.
exercises.explanation: Diga o que está pronto e o que falta. Status claro dá tranquilidade ao cliente.

exercises.title: 6. Dê o status em voz alta
exercises.targetText: The civil permit is approved. The environmental permit is in progress. The electrical license is ready for review.
exercises.translation: O alvará civil está aprovado. A licença ambiental está em andamento. A licença elétrica está pronta para revisão.

lessons.title: Steering committee meetings — executive-level Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você abre e conduz um steering committee com o Google em frases simples — dando o status geral, dizendo que tudo está no prazo e no orçamento e apontando os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
A steering committee is a high-level meeting. The top people from Racional and Google meet here. They do not talk about small details. They look at the big picture: is the data center on track? Is it on budget? Is it on schedule? This meeting guides the whole project.

For an executive like Fabrício, this is a key moment. He gives a short status update. He shows the last milestone. He raises one point of attention, if there is one. Then he talks about the next steps. Every word counts, because every person in the room is a stakeholder.

Racional has run committees like this for 50+ years, with clients like Microsoft and Amazon. The language is clear and calm. "We are on track and on budget." "Here is the big picture." "I will keep you posted." At the end, you align on the decision and thank everyone for coming.
lessons.intro:
Aula interpessoal do M5: o steering committee com o Google. Aqui você abre, dá o status geral e aponta os próximos passos.

Guarde três frases-âncora: "We are on track and on budget." (estamos no prazo e no orçamento), "Here is the big picture." (este é o panorama geral) e "Thank you all for coming." (obrigado a todos por virem). Frases curtas, tom de liderança calma.
lessons.situation: Steering committee trimestral. Na sala, os diretores da Racional e os executivos seniores do Google. Você precisa abrir e dar o status do data center em poucas frases.
lessons.context: Thank you all for coming. Here is the big picture. The data center is on track. We are on budget and on schedule. We reached an important milestone. The next steps are clear. I will keep you posted.

vocab.example: Here is a short status update.

lessons.title: Talking to executives above your usual Google contact
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala com um executivo acima do seu contato habitual no Google — um diretor ou VP — de forma curta, clara e respeitosa, indo direto ao ponto.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes you talk to someone above your usual contact at Google. This person is a director or a VP. They have very little time. They want the result, not all the details. You must be short and clear.

With a senior person, you give the answer first. Say the most important point. Then you stop. You give more detail only if they ask. This is a sign of respect. It shows you know how to talk to a decision-maker.

At Racional, the data center for Google is a big project. A VP may join the call for five minutes. In 50 years and more than 620 projects, Racional learned one thing: leaders want the headline. Today you learn to give it in simple English.
lessons.intro:
Três frases-âncora desta aula: "Thank you for your time." (agradeça o tempo da pessoa), "In short, the project is on track." (vá direto ao ponto) e "I can give more details if you want." (ofereça aprofundar).

Com sênior, a ordem é: resposta primeiro, detalhe só depois — e só se pedirem.
lessons.situation: O VP de infraestrutura do Google entra na call por cinco minutos. Seu contato de sempre não está. É com você. Você precisa ser claro e curto.
lessons.context: Thank you for your time. In short, the project is on track. We are within budget. We deliver the first phase next month. I can give more details if you want.

lessons.title: Strategic negotiation with Google — long-term thinking
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala de uma parceria de longo prazo com o Google em frases curtas, mostrando que a Racional pensa no futuro e quer crescer junto.
lessons.overview:
A good business is not only about today. It is about the long term. With Google, the data center is the first project. But it can be the start of many. When you talk about the future, you build a strong partnership.

The key word is trust. Trust takes time to build. You build it project by project. A good relationship is a win-win: it is good for Google and good for Racional. Both sides grow together.

Racional has worked with Microsoft and Amazon on data centers. These clients came back for more. Why? Because Racional thinks long-term. Today you learn to say this to Google in simple English: we want to invest in the future, not only in one project.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "We think long-term." (pensamos no longo prazo), "This is a win-win." (é bom para os dois lados) e "We want to grow together." (queremos crescer junto).

A ideia central: confiança (trust) se constrói com o tempo, projeto a projeto.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google sobre o futuro. O data center é só o começo. Você quer mostrar que a Racional pensa em uma parceria longa, não em um projeto só.
lessons.context: We think long-term. This is a win-win for both of us. We want to invest in a strong partnership. Trust takes time, and we want to build it. Let's grow together.

lessons.title: "What's important to you?" — discovery in negotiation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você faz perguntas simples para descobrir o que é importante para o Google, ouvindo antes de propor uma solução.
lessons.overview:
Before you sell, you must listen. Good negotiation starts with one question: "What's important to you?" When you ask this, you learn the real priority of the client. This first step is called discovery.

With Google, the priority may be time. Or it may be safety. Or it may be cost. You do not know until you ask. So you ask, and you listen. Then you can offer the right solution. This is much better than a guess.

At Racional, every great project starts the same way: understand the client first. In 50 years, with clients like Microsoft and Amazon, this rule never changed. Today you learn simple questions that help you find out what Google really needs.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "What's important to you?" (o que é importante para você?), "Tell me more." (me conte mais) e "What matters most?" (o que importa mais?).

A ideia central: pergunte e ouça (listen) antes de propor. Descobrir vem primeiro.
lessons.situation: Início da negociação do data center. Antes de falar de preço ou prazo, você quer entender a prioridade do Google. Você faz perguntas e escuta.

lessons.title: BIM — building information modeling, why Google asks
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica em frases curtas o que é o BIM e por que o Google pede esse modelo digital na obra do data center.
lessons.overview:
BIM means building information modeling. It is a 3D model of the building on a computer. It is not only a drawing. It holds a lot of information: walls, pipes, cables, and more. The team can see the whole building before they build it.

Why does Google ask for BIM? Because it helps to plan. In the model, the team can find a clash — when two parts hit the same place. They fix it on the computer, not on the site. This saves time and money. It is safer too.

At Racional, a data center is very complex. There are many systems in a small space. BIM puts them all on a single platform. Everyone — Racional and Google — sees the same model. Today you learn to explain this in simple English.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "BIM is a 3D digital model." (o BIM é um modelo digital em 3D), "It helps us plan." (ele nos ajuda a planejar) e "We find a clash before we build." (achamos um conflito antes de construir).

A ideia central: ver o prédio no computador antes de construir reduz erro.
lessons.situation: O Google pergunta sobre o BIM no projeto do data center. Você explica, de forma simples, o que é e por que ele ajuda os dois lados.
lessons.context: BIM is a 3D digital model of the building. It holds a lot of information. We use it to plan. We find a clash before we build. Google and Racional see the same model.

lessons.title: Phone calls with Google — no visual cues
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma ligação telefônica com o Google em frases curtas — se identifica, pede para repetir e confirma os pontos, mesmo sem ver a outra pessoa.
lessons.overview:
A phone call is harder than a meeting. You do not see the face. You have no visual cues. So you must be very clear with your words. You say your name. You confirm. You ask the person to repeat when you don't hear well.

With Google, a quick call can solve a problem fast. But the line can be bad. The sound can break. Simple phrases save the call: "Could you repeat that?", "Just to confirm...", "I can't hear you well." These keep you in control.

At Racional, the site team and the client talk by phone every day. A clear call avoids mistakes on a big project like the Google data center. Today you learn the simple phrases that make a phone call easy, even with no picture.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "This is Fabrício speaking." (aqui é o Fabrício falando), "Could you repeat that?" (você pode repetir?) e "Just to confirm..." (só para confirmar...).

A ideia central: ao telefone, confirme tudo em voz alta — você não vê o rosto da pessoa.

lessons.context: Hello, this is Fabrício speaking. Sorry, the line is bad. Could you repeat that, please? Just to confirm, the meeting is on Friday. Thanks for the call. Talk soon.

lessons.title: Video meetings with Google — speaking clearly on camera
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa de uma reunião por vídeo com o Google em frases curtas — testa o som, compartilha a tela, fala devagar e claro na câmera.
lessons.overview:
A video meeting is the most common way to talk to Google today. You see the person, but the connection is not always good. The sound can break up. There is sometimes a small lag. So you check the basics first: "Can you hear me?", "Can you see my screen?"

On camera, you must speak slowly and clearly. You wait for your turn. You mute when you don't speak, and you unmute when it's your turn. These small habits make the meeting smooth and professional.

At Racional, teams in Brazil meet clients like Google by video every week. A clear video call saves a trip and keeps the data center project moving. Today you learn the simple phrases to run a video meeting with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "Can you hear me?" (você consegue me ouvir?), "Can you see my screen?" (você consegue ver minha tela?) e "Let me share my screen." (deixa eu compartilhar a tela).

A ideia central: cheque som e tela no começo, fale devagar e dê o turno (go ahead).
lessons.situation: Reunião por vídeo com o Google sobre o data center. Você testa o som, compartilha a tela com um número e fala devagar para todos entenderem.
lessons.context: Hi everyone. Can you hear me? Good. Let me share my screen. Can you see my screen? I will speak slowly. Please go ahead if you have a question. Let's wrap up.

vocab.example: I hear you loud and clear.

lessons.title: Talking numbers fast — confidence with big values
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diz valores grandes em inglês — milhares, milhões, bilhões e percentuais — com confiança e sem travar para falar de orçamento com o Google.
lessons.overview:
Numbers are the heart of any contract. As Executive Superintendent of Contracts at Racional, you talk about money every day. The budget, the estimated cost, the cost per square meter. With a big client like Google, you must say these figures clearly and fast. A small number mistake can create a big problem.

Racional has more than 50 years of work. The company built over 620 projects and more than 10 million square meters. These are huge numbers. The Google data center is also a large project, with a high total cost. You need simple words like thousand, million, and billion to talk about it.

You do not need exact numbers all the time. Words like about, roughly, and ballpark help you give a quick idea. This makes you sound calm and confident. In this lesson, you practice big values so you can talk money with Google without fear.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três âncoras de número: "It is about ten million dollars", "That is roughly fifteen percent" e "The total is...".

A ideia é uma só: dar o valor com calma. Use about e roughly quando não quiser ser exato — isso é normal e profissional.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o time financeiro do Google. Eles perguntam o custo desta fase da obra. Você precisa dar o número com segurança.
lessons.context: The total budget is about ten million dollars. This phase is roughly fifteen percent of the total. The cost is two thousand dollars per square meter. These figures are a ballpark. I can confirm the exact number later.

lessons.title: Defending the timeline under Google's pressure
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você defende o cronograma da obra sob a pressão do Google, explicando que o prazo é realista e propondo opções sem prometer o impossível.
lessons.overview:
The timeline is a promise. As Contracts Superintendent, you protect it. Google wants the data center fast. The client puts you under pressure. But a good deadline must be realistic. Racional has built over 620 projects in 50 years because the company keeps its word.

One phase depends on another. You cannot start the roof before the walls. So you explain this to Google in simple words. You can speed up the work. You can add crews. But you never break one rule: safety stays first. This is the Racional way.

When the client pushes hard, you stay calm. You say "let me check what's possible". You do not say yes to everything. You commit to what you can do. This keeps the project on track and keeps Google's trust. In this lesson, you learn to defend the schedule with respect and confidence.
lessons.intro:
Três frases-âncora para a pressão: "The timeline is realistic", "Let me check what's possible" e "Safety stays first".

A meta é não prometer o impossível. Você mostra opções (speed up, add crews) sem abrir mão da segurança.
lessons.situation: O Google quer a obra mais rápida e pressiona na reunião. Você precisa defender o prazo sem brigar e sem prometer demais.
lessons.context: I understand the pressure. The timeline is realistic. This phase depends on the previous phase. We can speed up. We can add crews. But safety stays first. Let me check what's possible. I want to keep the project on track.

lessons.title: Subcontractor management — local Brazilian crews
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala da gestão de subcontratados e das equipes locais brasileiras para o Google, explicando quem faz o quê na obra e como você coordena tudo.
lessons.overview:
A big project needs many hands. On the Google data center, Racional works with many subcontractors. One crew does the electrical work. Another team does the cooling. As Superintendent, you manage all of them. You coordinate the work so it runs well.

Racional uses local labor. The company hires Brazilian skilled workers near the site. This is good for the project and good for the region. With over 620 projects, Racional knows how to find the right people and how to oversee them.

Google wants to know who is responsible for each part. So you explain the structure in simple words. Each supplier reports to a leader. Each leader reports to you. You know the full workforce and the headcount. This shows control and gives the client peace of mind.
lessons.intro:
Estruturas-âncora: "This crew handles the electrical work", "I manage the subcontractors" e "They report to me".

A ideia é uma só: mostrar quem faz o quê. Use responsible for e report to para deixar a hierarquia clara.
lessons.situation: O Google quer entender quem trabalha na obra. Você explica os subcontratados, as equipes locais e como tudo é coordenado.
lessons.context: We work with many subcontractors on site. This crew handles the electrical work. Another team handles the cooling. We hire local labor. The workers are skilled. They report to me. I manage the full workforce.

vocab.example: This crew does the electrical work.

lessons.title: Storytelling — short stories that win Google's trust
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conta uma história curta e verdadeira sobre a obra para conquistar a confiança do Google, usando uma estrutura simples de começo, meio e fim.
lessons.overview:
A good story builds trust. Numbers tell the client what you do. A story shows how you do it. With Google, a short, true story is powerful. It shows that Racional solves problems. In over 50 years and 620 projects, the company has many strong stories to tell.

The structure is simple. First, the challenge: "Last year, we had a tough deadline." Then, the action: "So we added a night shift." Then, the result: "In the end, it worked. We finished on time." Three steps, no hard words.

This kind of story is honest and human. You can be proud without sounding arrogant. You show that Racional faces a hard moment and learns from it. For Google, this is real proof. In this lesson, you learn to tell a short success story in clear, simple English.
lessons.intro:
A estrutura de três passos: "Last year, we had a problem..." (desafio), "So we decided to..." (ação) e "In the end, it worked" (resultado).

É uma ideia só: começo, meio e fim. Use so para ligar o problema à solução.
lessons.situation: Conversa com o Google. Você quer mostrar, com uma história real, que a Racional resolve problemas difíceis na obra.
lessons.context: Last year, we had a problem. The rain stopped the work. It was a big challenge. So we decided to add a night shift. The team worked hard. In the end, it worked. We finished on time. I am proud of my team.

vocab.example: Last year, we had a problem.

lessons.title: Sharing past success — "we did this for a similar client"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta um sucesso passado ao Google — 'fizemos isto para um cliente parecido' — para mostrar experiência e gerar confiança sem soar arrogante.
lessons.overview:
The best way to win trust is proof. When you talk to Google, you can say: "We did this before." Racional has a strong track record. The company built a similar project for another big client. This is real experience, and experience matters a lot.

Google works with Microsoft and Amazon too. These clients want a partner with a proven history. Racional built data centers and complex projects before. You can say: "We built it. We delivered it on budget and on time." Simple words, strong message.

You do not need to brag. You just share the facts. "We handled a similar client. The project was complex, and it was successful." This shows Google that Racional can handle the data center too. A good reference is worth more than a promise. In this lesson, you learn to share past success with calm confidence.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "We have experience with similar projects", "We built it for another client" e "We delivered on time and on budget".

A meta é mostrar prova, não se gabar. Use similar, track record e proven para soar confiável.

lessons.title: Pricing strategy — talking value, not cost, to Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala de valor, não de custo, ao apresentar preço ao Google — mostrando o que ele recebe em troca antes de chegar ao número.
lessons.overview:
Price is more than a number. As Contracts Superintendent, you know this well. When Google looks at the price, you help them see the value. Cost is what they pay. Value is what they get in return. With Racional, they get quality, safety, and on-time delivery.

A data center is a big investment. Google does not want the cheapest builder. Google wants the right partner. Racional has 50 years of work and a proven method. This protects the project and gives the client peace of mind. That is real value.

So before you say the number, you talk about what Google receives. "You get top quality. We protect the schedule. We control the scope." Then the price feels fair, not high. A high return on investment makes the choice easy. In this lesson, you learn to talk value first, then cost.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "Let me focus on the value", "You get quality and safety" e "It is worth it".

A ordem importa: primeiro o valor, depois o número. Use value, in return e worth it para posicionar o preço.
lessons.situation: O Google acha o preço alto. Antes de discutir o número, você mostra o valor: qualidade, segurança e entrega no prazo.
lessons.context: I understand your concern about the price. Let me focus on the value. You get top quality. You get full safety. You get on-time delivery. The investment is worth it. We protect the project and give you peace of mind.

lessons.title: Closing the deal — final phrases with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fecha um acordo com o Google usando frases curtas e claras — confirma o que foi combinado, marca o próximo passo e encerra com profissionalismo.
lessons.overview:
In business, a deal is only real when both sides say the same thing out loud. To close the deal means to end a talk with a clear yes. For an executive at Racional, this moment is important. After long meetings about the Google data center, the client wants three simple things: what you agree on, the next step, and a clear good-bye.

Good closing language is short. You do not need long words. You confirm, you say what comes next, and you thank the client. Phrases like we agree on, the next step, and thank you for your time make the end of a meeting calm and strong. At Racional, with 50 years and more than 620 projects, clear closings keep big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google happy.

When you wrap up a meeting well, you protect the project. You and the client are on the same page. There is no doubt. The Google team feels safe and ready to move forward. A clear closing is a small habit, but it builds trust on every contract.
lessons.intro:
Vamos fechar uma reunião com calma e clareza. Lembre destas frases-âncora: So, we agree on... (então, concordamos em...) para confirmar, I'll send you... (vou te enviar...) para marcar o próximo passo e Thank you for your time para encerrar.

Uma ideia por frase. Confirme, defina o próximo passo, agradeça. Simples assim.
lessons.situation: Fim de uma reunião de negociação com o Google sobre o cronograma do data center. Tudo foi acordado e agora você precisa encerrar de forma clara e confiante.
lessons.context: So, we agree on the new schedule. Great. I'll send you the document tomorrow. Let's move forward with this plan. Thank you for your time today.

lessons.title: Project lifecycle in English — design to handover
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você nomeia, em inglês simples, as grandes fases de um projeto de construção — do projeto à entrega — para acompanhar o Google quando ele falar do ciclo da obra.
lessons.overview:
Every building project follows a path. It starts on paper and ends with the keys in the client's hand. This path is the project lifecycle. For Racional, with more than 620 projects and 10 million square meters built, this path is the same on every job — from a small office to a big Google data center.

There are a few big phases, in order. First is design, the plan and the drawings. Then comes construction, the real work on site. After that is commissioning, when the team tests all the systems. The last phase is handover, when Racional gives the finished building to the client.

You do not need to explain each phase in detail. You only need to say where the project is now. A simple line like We are in the construction phase keeps the Google team informed. When you know the milestone and the next stage, every status meeting is calm and clear.
lessons.intro:
Vamos situar o projeto numa linha simples: design → construction → commissioning → handover. Lembre da frase-âncora We are in the ___ phase (estamos na fase de...).

Com isso, você responde a qualquer pergunta de status do Google em uma frase curta.
lessons.situation: Reunião de status do data center com o Google. Eles perguntam em que ponto o projeto está. Você responde nomeando a fase e o que vem a seguir.
lessons.context: Right now, we are in the construction phase. The design is complete. Next, we test all the systems. This stage is commissioning. The final step is the handover to your team.

vocab.example: We are in the construction phase.
The handover is the final step.

lessons.title: Difficult conversations — when Google is unhappy
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma conversa difícil com o Google de forma calma — escuta, reconhece a preocupação e mostra que está cuidando do problema.
lessons.overview:
In any long project, the client is not always happy. Sometimes Google has a concern or an issue. This is normal. What matters is how you talk in this moment. A difficult conversation is not a fight. It is a chance to show that Racional listens and cares.

The first job is to listen. You do not defend right away. You say I understand and I hear you. This makes the client feel safe. Then you show action. You say I'll look into it and I'll come back to you. Simple, calm words build trust, even when the news is bad.

For an executive at Racional, with 50 years of work and clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, staying calm is a real skill. When you stay calm and offer a clear plan, a hard talk becomes a strong relationship. The client sees a partner, not a problem.
lessons.intro:
Numa conversa difícil, escutar vem antes de responder. Lembre destas frases-âncora: I understand (eu entendo), I hear you (eu te ouço / entendo sua preocupação) e I'll look into it (vou verificar isso).

Mantenha a calma e termine com um próximo passo claro: I'll come back to you (eu volto a falar com você).
lessons.situation: O Google está insatisfeito com um ponto do projeto e levanta uma preocupação em reunião. Você precisa escutar, acolher e mostrar que vai cuidar do assunto.
lessons.context: I understand your concern. You are right, this is an issue. I hear you. I'll look into it today. Then I'll come back to you with a clear plan.

vocab.example: You're right, this is an issue.
I'll come back to you tomorrow.

I'll come back with a clear plan.
It is important to stay calm.

lessons.title: Apology language — taking responsibility with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você assume a responsabilidade por um erro com o Google de forma clara — pede desculpa, diz o que vai corrigir e mostra que vai recuperar a confiança.
lessons.overview:
Mistakes happen on every big project. The strong move is not to hide a mistake. It is to take ownership of it. To apologize the right way is a real business skill. When Racional makes an error on the Google data center, a clear and honest apology protects the relationship.

A good apology has three parts. First, you say sorry: I'm sorry for the delay. Second, you take responsibility: It was my mistake. Third, you show action: I'll fix it and it won't happen again. You do not give many excuses. You speak short and true.

For an executive at Racional, with 50 years of trust and clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, this language helps rebuild trust after a hard moment. When you take responsibility and make it right, the client sees a serious partner. A clean apology can make the relationship even stronger than before.
lessons.intro:
Pedir desculpa com clareza tem três passos. Lembre das frases-âncora: I'm sorry for... (desculpe por...), It was my mistake (foi meu erro) e I'll fix it (vou corrigir).

Sem desculpas longas. Assuma, conserte e mostre que it won't happen again (não vai acontecer de novo).
lessons.situation: Houve uma falha da Racional num ponto do projeto do data center. Você precisa pedir desculpa ao Google, assumir o erro e mostrar como vai corrigir.
lessons.context: I'm sorry for the delay. It was my mistake. I take full responsibility. I'll fix it this week. It won't happen again. We want to rebuild your trust.

lessons.title: Discussing penalties with Google — calmly, with data
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre multas e ajustes com o Google de forma calma e baseada em dados — apresenta os fatos, pede uma revisão justa e busca um acordo.
lessons.overview:
In a big contract, sometimes there is a penalty. A penalty is money paid for a delay or a problem. This is a hard topic. But you can talk about it in a calm, professional way. The secret is simple: use the data, not emotion. Numbers keep the talk fair and clear.

For an executive at Racional, the best move is to show the figures and the facts. You can say according to the data and the delay was caused by a change request. You do not blame anyone. You review the facts together with the Google team and you ask for a fair and reasonable result.

Racional has 50 years of contracts and clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. A calm, data-based talk about a penalty protects the relationship. When you stay calm and show the numbers, both sides can reach an agreement. The goal is not to win a fight. The goal is a fair solution that keeps the project moving.
lessons.intro:
Falar de multa exige calma e dados. Lembre das frases-âncora: According to the data... (de acordo com os dados...), The delay was caused by... (o atraso foi causado por...) e Let's review the facts (vamos revisar os fatos).

Sem emoção, sem culpa. Mostre os números e busque um resultado fair (justo) e reasonable (razoável).
lessons.situation: O Google quer aplicar uma multa por um atraso no data center. Você precisa discutir o tema com calma, mostrar os dados e buscar um acordo justo.
lessons.context: Let's review the facts. According to the data, the delay was caused by a change request. The figures show the real cause. I think a fair number is reasonable. Let's reach an agreement.

lessons.title: "Let's find a solution together" — collaborative tone
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa um tom colaborativo com o Google — convida o cliente a resolver um problema junto, propõe opções e busca uma saída boa para os dois lados.
lessons.overview:
The best negotiations do not feel like a fight. They feel like teamwork. When there is a problem, you can say let's find a solution together. This small phrase changes the whole tone. The client stops feeling like an enemy and starts feeling like a partner. For Racional, this collaborative tone is gold on a long project like the Google data center.

A challenge is not a wall. It is a shared task. You can offer an option with soft questions like what if we...? and how about...? These words invite the client to think with you. You show that we're on the same team and that you both want a win-win.

Racional has 50 years of work and big clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. A collaborative tone keeps these relationships strong. When you focus on a common goal and say let's move forward together, a hard moment becomes a shared win. You stay flexible: I'm open to new ideas. That is how partners solve problems.
lessons.intro:
O tom colaborativo transforma um problema em tarefa compartilhada. Lembre das frases-âncora: Let's find a solution together (vamos achar uma solução juntos), What if we...? (e se a gente...?) e How about...? (que tal...?).

Mostre flexibilidade e foco no objetivo comum: We're on the same team (estamos no mesmo time).
lessons.situation: Surgiu um desafio no projeto do data center. Em vez de discutir, você convida o Google a resolver o problema em conjunto, propondo opções.
lessons.context: We have a challenge. Let's find a solution together. What if we change the order of the work? How about a new date? We're on the same team. I want a win-win.

lessons.title: Risk management — identifying and mitigating risks
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre gestão de riscos no projeto do data center do Google — nomeando um risco, dizendo o impacto e propondo uma ação para reduzi-lo.
lessons.overview:
Every big project has risks. A risk is a problem that can happen. Rain can stop the work. A truck can be late. A team can be small. Good leaders see these problems early. This is risk management. It means you find the risk, you see the impact, and you make a plan.

For Racional, risk management is not new. The company has 50 years and 620 projects. The teams know the weather, the soil, and the suppliers. On the Google data center, the plan is clear. We monitor the risks every week. We keep a backup plan ready. We act early to prevent delays.

Google wants a calm and clear partner. When you say "The main risk is rain, and we have a backup plan", you show control. Simple words are enough. You name the risk. You give the impact. You give the action. This is how a leader speaks about risk in English.
lessons.intro:
Vamos usar uma estrutura curta e poderosa: The risk is... The impact is... To mitigate it, we will...

Frases-âncora: The main risk is rain. / The impact is a delay. / To mitigate it, we have a backup plan. Uma ideia por frase, sempre com a ação no fim.
lessons.situation: Reunião de planejamento do data center com o Google. Eles perguntam quais são os principais riscos do projeto. Você nomeia um risco, diz o impacto e a ação de mitigação.
lessons.context: The main risk is heavy rain. The impact is a delay of one week. To mitigate it, we have a backup plan. We monitor the risks every week. We are prepared. The project is under control.

lessons.title: Steering the conversation back to business with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe, em inglês simples, trazer a conversa de volta ao tema principal numa reunião com o Google, de forma educada e clara.
lessons.overview:
In a long meeting, people talk about many things. Sometimes the conversation goes off topic. This is normal. But the leader keeps the meeting on the right road. This is to steer the conversation back. You bring the group back to the main topic in a polite way.

For Racional, meetings with Google have a clear agenda. There is a lot to cover: timeline, safety, costs. Time is short. A good host says "That's a great point, but let's come back to the schedule." The other person feels respected, and the meeting stays on plan.

This skill builds trust. When you stay on track, Google sees a partner who values their time. You do not need long words. Short and kind phrases are enough. "Let's circle back to that later" or "In the interest of time, let's move on" keep the meeting strong and calm.
lessons.intro:
Vamos treinar frases curtas e gentis para voltar ao foco.

Frases-âncora: Let's come back to the main topic. / That's a great point. / In the interest of time, let's move on. Primeiro você valida a pessoa, depois traz de volta ao tema.
lessons.situation: Reunião sobre o data center. O time do Google começa a falar de um assunto fora da pauta. Você, com educação, traz a conversa de volta ao tema principal.
lessons.context: That's a great point. But in the interest of time, let's come back to the main topic. We can circle back to that later. Now, let's stay on track. We still have a lot to cover today.

lessons.title: "Let's circle back to..." — Google meeting management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz e encerra uma reunião com o Google em inglês simples, usando frases para retomar pontos, definir próximos passos e fechar com clareza.
lessons.overview:
Good meeting management is a leadership skill. At the end of a meeting, the host makes things clear. What did we decide? Who does what? When is the next step? This is the time to wrap up and list the action items.

For Racional, every meeting with Google needs clear next steps. The project is big, with many teams. If you say "On my end, I will send the schedule by Friday", everyone knows the plan. You recap the main points and you follow up after the meeting.

Some topics are too long for the room. You can say "Let's take that offline" or "Let's circle back to that." This keeps the meeting short and useful. A clear close shows Google that Racional is organized, calm, and always ready for the next steps.
lessons.intro:
Vamos treinar o fechamento de reunião em inglês simples.

Frases-âncora: Let's circle back to that. / The action item is... / Let me recap the next steps. No fim, sempre diga quem faz o quê e quando.

lessons.title: Term sheet review with Google — key contractual items
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você comenta, em inglês simples, os itens principais de um term sheet com o Google — escopo, prazo, pagamento — e faz perguntas sobre cada um.
lessons.overview:
A term sheet is a short document. It lists the key items of a deal. It shows the scope, the timeline, and the payment terms. Both sides read it before the full contract. It is a map of the agreement.

For Racional and Google, the term sheet of the data center is important. It says what Racional will build, when, and how payment works. It also has milestones and deliverables. When you read each clause with care, you protect the project and the partnership.

In the meeting, you go item by item. You say "I agree on the scope" or "I have a question about the timeline." Simple and clear words are enough. This shows Google that Racional is serious, careful, and a strong partner for a big project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos revisar o term sheet item a item, em inglês simples.

Frases-âncora: I agree on the scope. / I have a question about the timeline. / Let's cover the payment terms. Uma frase por item, concordando ou perguntando.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google para revisar o term sheet do data center. Vocês passam pelos itens principais: escopo, prazo e pagamento. Você concorda ou faz perguntas.

lessons.title: Signing language — "we are aligned on..."
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa, em inglês simples, a linguagem de fechamento de acordo com o Google — confirmando alinhamento, avançando e celebrando a parceria.
lessons.overview:
The end of a long talk is a special moment. Both sides are aligned. You read the final terms. You confirm the points. Then you say "We have a deal." This is signing language. It is positive, warm, and clear.

For Racional and Google, this moment closes the data center agreement. It is the start of a real partnership. When you say "We are aligned on the scope and the timeline", everyone feels safe to move forward. The words are simple, but the message is strong.

This is also a human moment. You can say "It's a pleasure to work with you" and "I'm looking forward to the project." A warm close builds trust for the years ahead. Racional has 50 years of partnerships. A good signing day is how each one begins.
lessons.intro:
Vamos treinar a linguagem positiva de fechamento de acordo.

Frases-âncora: We are aligned on the scope. / We have a deal. / It's a pleasure to work with you. Confirme, avance e celebre.

lessons.title: Final inspections — punch list, defects, sign-off
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre a inspeção final do data center — punch list, defeitos a corrigir e a entrega final ao Google.
lessons.overview:
At the end of a project, there is a final inspection. The team walks through the building. They look at every room. They make a punch list. This is a list of small problems, or defects, to fix before the handover.

For Racional, the final inspection of the Google data center is a proud moment. The teams walk through the site with the client. They check each item. They repair the pending points. When everything is good, both sides sign off.

The handover is when Racional gives the building to Google. It must meet the standard. A clean punch list and a calm sign-off show 50 years of quality. This is how a great project ends — and how the next one begins.
lessons.intro:
Vamos treinar a linguagem da inspeção final e da entrega.

Frases-âncora: Let's walk through the site. / This defect is on the punch list. / We will fix it before the handover. Aponte o defeito e diga a ação.
lessons.situation: Inspeção final do data center com o Google. Vocês percorrem a obra, montam a punch list, anotam os defeitos a corrigir e preparam a entrega (handover).
lessons.context: Let's walk through the site. This is the final inspection. We have a short punch list. One defect is pending. We will fix it this week. Then the project meets the standard and we sign off.

lessons.title: Multi-cultural meeting — Google US + India + Brazil at the table
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma reunião multicultural com o Google (EUA, Índia e Brasil na mesma mesa) usando frases simples que confirmam o entendimento e incluem todos os times.
lessons.overview:
A multicultural meeting is a meeting with people from many countries. In the Google data center project, three teams sit at the table: the Google team in the United States, engineers in India, and Racional in Brazil. Each team has a different accent and a different time zone. This is normal in big projects.

Good communication is not about perfect English. It is about being clear. You speak slowly. You confirm the message. You ask people to repeat. When you say "let me make sure I understand," you protect the project from mistakes. A small question now saves a big problem later.

Racional works with global clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These calls always mix cultures. When Fabrício includes every team and keeps the talk simple, the meeting runs well. Respect and clarity build trust across borders.
lessons.intro:
Numa reunião com EUA, Índia e Brasil, a regra é simples: fale devagar, confirme e inclua todos. Não tenha medo de pedir para repetir — isso é respeito, não fraqueza.

Frases-âncora desta aula: "Let me make sure I understand" (deixa eu confirmar), "Could you repeat that, please?" (pode repetir?) e "On our side / on your side" (do nosso lado / do lado de vocês).
lessons.situation: Call do data center com três times ao mesmo tempo: Google nos EUA, engenheiros na Índia e sua equipe no Brasil. Os sotaques são diferentes e você precisa garantir que todos se entendam.
lessons.context: This is a multicultural meeting. Let me make sure I understand. Could you repeat that, please? On our side in Brazil, the plan is ready. What about your side?

lessons.title: Code-switching — formal vs. casual with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você ajusta o tom entre formal e casual com o Google, escolhendo a frase certa para um e-mail oficial ou para uma conversa descontraída de corredor.
lessons.overview:
The same message can change its clothes. In a formal email to Google, you write "I would like to schedule a meeting." In the hallway, you say "Got a minute?" The idea is the same, but the tone is different. This change of style is called code-switching.

Every executive does this every day. A document needs a formal register. A coffee break needs a casual register. When you pick the right tone, you sound natural and you build a good relationship. The wrong tone can feel cold or too relaxed.

At Racional, Fabrício talks to many people: the Google director, the site engineer, his own team. With Google in the data center project, first emails and contracts are formal. Daily talk is casual. A simple rule helps: start formal, then relax when the other person relaxes. This keeps respect and warmth at the same time.
lessons.intro:
O mesmo recado muda de roupa: num e-mail oficial você fala formal; num café com o colega, fala casual. Trocar de registro na hora certa é o code-switching.

Compare: "I would like to" (formal) versus "Let's grab a coffee" (casual); "Thank you" versus "Thanks a lot!". Na dúvida, comece formal.
lessons.situation: Num mesmo dia você escreve um e-mail oficial ao diretor do Google e, mais tarde, encontra o engenheiro do dia a dia no corredor. O recado é parecido, mas o tom muda.
lessons.context: In the email: I would like to schedule a meeting. In the hallway: Hey, got a minute? Let's grab a coffee. Thanks a lot!

vocab.example: I would like to schedule a call.

lessons.title: Win-win framing with Google — language patterns
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa frases simples de ganha-ganha (win-win) com o Google, mostrando que a parceria é boa para os dois lados.
lessons.overview:
A win-win deal is good for both sides. You win, and the client wins too. This is the heart of a strong partnership. When Fabrício talks with Google about the next steps of the data center, the message is simple: "This works for both of us."

Win-win language is calm and positive. You do not fight for one side only. You look for a fair deal that helps everyone. Words like together, both sides, and long-term show that you think about the future, not only about today.

Racional has built 620+ projects over 50+ years. The company grows when its clients grow. With global clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, the best deals are the ones where both companies benefit. When Fabrício says "we are on the same team," he opens the door to renewal and new projects.
lessons.intro:
Negociar não é vencer o outro. A ideia de hoje é win-win: bom para os dois lados. Você mostra que pensa na parceria e no longo prazo.

Frases-âncora: "This works for both of us" (isto é bom para os dois), "We both win" (os dois ganham) e "It's a fair deal" (é um acordo justo).
lessons.situation: Conversa com o Google sobre a próxima frente do data center. Você quer mostrar que a renovação é boa para os dois lados, não só para a Racional.

lessons.title: "If we agree on X, can you agree on Y?" — package deals
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você propõe acordos por pacote ao Google com a estrutura 'If we agree on X, can you agree on Y?', trocando pontos para chegar ao meio-termo.
lessons.overview:
A package deal joins many points into one agreement. You do not fight for each item alone. You trade. The key sentence is simple: "If we agree on X, can you agree on Y?" This is how Fabrício can move a negotiation with Google forward.

In a package, you give and take. Maybe Google wants a shorter timeline. Maybe Racional wants a clear scope and a fair price. You put these points together as a package and you both meet in the middle. Nobody loses everything; both sides win something.

Racional manages large, complex projects with global clients. In the data center renewal, many things are on the table at once: price, timeline, scope, support. The package approach keeps the talk calm and organized. When you say "that works for me," you close one piece and move to the next.
lessons.intro:
Em vez de brigar por cada ponto, junte tudo num pacote. A estrutura-chave: "If we agree on X, can you agree on Y?" (se concordamos em X, vocês topam Y?).

Frases-âncora: "as a package" (como pacote), "in exchange" (em troca) e "meet in the middle" (chegar ao meio-termo).
lessons.situation: Negociação da renovação do data center com o Google. Há vários pontos na mesa — prazo, escopo, preço — e você quer fechá-los juntos, como um pacote.
lessons.context: If we agree on the timeline, can you agree on the price? Let's do it as a package. We give and take. Let's meet in the middle. That works for me.

lessons.title: Operations & maintenance — handing the building over
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz a entrega da obra ao Google (handover) com frases simples sobre operação, manutenção, garantia e checklist.
lessons.overview:
The handover is the moment Racional gives the building to Google. The work is done. Now the client takes over. This is a key step at the end of the data center project. A good handover means Google can use the building with confidence.

At handover, you talk about operations and maintenance. You give the operations manual. You explain the warranty. You run a final inspection and check every item on a checklist. The goal is simple: every system must run smoothly and the building must be ready to use.

Racional has delivered 620+ projects over 50+ years. A clean handover protects the relationship with global clients like Google. When Fabrício says "the building is ready to use" and "we offer full support," he closes one project well and opens the door to the next one.
lessons.intro:
O handover é a entrega da obra ao cliente. A obra acabou; o Google passa a operar. Você fala de operação, manutenção e garantia.

Frases-âncora: "The building is ready to use" (o prédio está pronto para uso), "Here is the operations manual" (aqui está o manual de operação) e "We offer full support" (oferecemos suporte total).

lessons.title: Trust-building with Google — small consistent moves over months
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala de confiança com o Google usando frases simples sobre cumprir a palavra, ser confiável e entregar no prazo, passo a passo.
lessons.overview:
Trust is not built in one day. It grows with small steps over many months. Every time Fabrício keeps his word and delivers on time, Google trusts Racional a little more. This is how a strong, long relationship is born.

The secret is to be consistent. You do the same good thing again and again. You follow up. You are honest when there is a problem. You say "you can count on us," and then you prove it with action. Words are nice, but actions build real trust.

Racional has 50+ years and 620+ projects. That history is pure trust, built one project at a time with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. In the data center project, when Fabrício says "I keep my word" and "we deliver on time," he is opening the door to renewal and to the next front of work.
lessons.intro:
Confiança se constrói passo a passo, com pequenos gestos ao longo dos meses. Cada entrega no prazo soma um pouco mais de trust.

Frases-âncora: "You can count on us" (você pode contar conosco), "I keep my word" (eu cumpro minha palavra) e "We deliver on time" (entregamos no prazo).

lessons.title: Recognizing the Google team — names, contributions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reconhece pessoas do time do Google pelo nome e pela contribuição, com agradecimentos curtos e específicos como 'Thank you, Sarah, for your help with...'.
lessons.overview:
At the end of a big project, words of thanks are very important. People work hard, and they want to feel seen. When you say a name and a real contribution, you build trust. This is part of every strong business relationship.

For Fabrício, the data center for Google is a long project with many people. The Google team helps with the schedule, with safety, and with many decisions. To recognize this work is smart and kind. Racional has more than fifty years and many big clients. Good relationships are one reason for this.

A simple 'thank you' is good. A specific 'thank you' is better. 'Thank you for your help with the plan' shows you saw the great work. This small habit helps you keep clients like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon for the next project.
lessons.intro:
Hoje a estrutura-âncora é "Thank you, [nome], for [contribuição]" — Obrigado, [nome], por [o que a pessoa fez].

Lembre também de duas frases curtas que dão calor: "Great work, everyone" e "I really appreciate it" (eu agradeço de verdade). Seja sempre específico: diga o nome e o que a pessoa fez.

lessons.title: Talking about the next Google contract — pipeline
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala do próximo contrato com o Google usando linguagem simples de pipeline, como 'the next project' e 'what's coming next?'.
lessons.overview:
Every business looks at the future. The word pipeline means the projects that may come next. When one project ends, a good company asks: 'What's coming next?' This is normal and smart business talk.

For Fabrício, the Google data center is almost ready. Now is a good time to talk about the next opportunity. Big clients like Google often build more than one site. Racional wants to be ready for the next project, with the same team and the same quality.

The tone is light. You show interest, not pressure. You say 'We'd love to do more with you' and 'We are ready to plan ahead'. This is how Racional keeps long partners like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon for many years.
lessons.intro:
Hoje as frases-âncora são "What's coming next?" (o que vem depois?), "the next project" e "We'd love to do more with you".

O tom é de interesse, não de cobrança. Você pergunta primeiro e depois oferece a Racional, sem pressa.

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você inicia uma conversa de pré-venda com o Google usando frases simples como 'It's still early' e 'We could explore your needs', sem assumir compromisso.
lessons.overview:
Before a real deal, there is a soft talk. We call it a pre-sales conversation. Both sides explore ideas with no commitment yet. You learn the client's needs and share a rough idea of a solution. It is light and open.

For Fabrício, this is the first step to the next Google project. Google may have a new site in mind. Racional listens first, then shows how it can help. No numbers are final at this early stage. The goal is trust and a clear picture of the need.

Simple, honest words work best here. You say 'It's still early' and 'No commitment yet'. This protects both sides and keeps the talk relaxed. With more than fifty years of work, Racional knows that good solutions start with good questions.
lessons.intro:
Hoje as frases-âncora são "It's still early" (ainda é cedo), "No commitment yet" (sem compromisso ainda) e "We could explore your needs".

O objetivo é abrir a conversa comercial com calma: entender a necessidade do Google e dar uma ideia geral, sem fechar nada.

lessons.title: Modular construction — Google's preference for speed
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala de construção modular em inglês simples, explicando ao Google por que ela é mais rápida, com frases como 'It's faster' e 'We build in a factory'.
lessons.overview:
Modular construction is a modern way to build. Teams build parts in a factory, away from the site. Then they bring the parts and assemble them fast. The result is faster work and high quality.

Google likes speed. A data center needs to be ready on time. With modular work, Racional can build off-site, save time, and repeat the same good design. This is a strong point for a fast client like Google.

Racional has built more than 620 projects and over ten million square meters. Modern methods like modular construction help deliver big sites on time, with less waste and less risk. For Fabrício, these simple words show Google a clear benefit: speed without losing quality.
lessons.intro:
Hoje as frases-âncora são "It's faster" (é mais rápido), "We build in a factory" e "We deliver on time".

A ideia central é uma só: construção modular = velocidade com qualidade. Você explica isso ao Google com frases curtas.
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com o Google sobre o método de obra. Você explica, de forma simples, por que a construção modular é mais rápida.

lessons.title: Defending the Racional team to Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você defende o time da Racional diante do Google com frases simples e firmes como 'My team is experienced' e 'We take responsibility'.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a client has a concern. A good leader listens first, then defends the team with calm words. You say 'I understand your concern' and then show why the team is strong. This is part of every mature relationship.

For Fabrício, the Google project is big and complex. If Google has a worry, Fabrício must back the team. He shows that his people are experienced, reliable, and committed. He also says the team will take responsibility and fix any problem.

Racional has more than fifty years and over 620 projects. This history is proof of a skilled team. With simple, honest English, Fabrício can defend his people and keep Google's trust, even in a hard moment.

Hoje as frases-âncora são "I understand your concern" (entendo sua preocupação), "My team is experienced" e "We take responsibility".

A sequência é clara: primeiro você acolhe a preocupação, depois defende o time com firmeza e calma.

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você defende a posição do Google dentro da Racional com frases simples como 'Let me explain' e 'It makes sense', mostrando o ponto de vista do cliente.
lessons.overview:
A good partner also defends the client inside its own company. When you explain the client's point, your team understands them better. You say 'Let me explain' and show why Google needs something. This helps both sides work as one.

For Fabrício, this is part of a mature relationship. Sometimes Google wants a fast change or a special rule. Inside Racional, Fabrício explains the reason: 'It makes sense, because Google needs speed.' This builds alignment and trust.

When both companies are on the same page, the project runs better. Racional has worked with big clients for decades. To see the client's side is a key skill. It is good for the project and good for the next contract with Google.

Hoje as frases-âncora são "Let me explain" (deixe-me explicar), "It makes sense, because..." e "Let's be on the same page".

A ideia é levar o ponto de vista do Google para dentro da Racional, com calma e clareza, para alinhar os dois lados.

lessons.title: Escalation language — when things need to go up at Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pede, em inglês simples e educado, que um assunto suba de nível na hierarquia do Google — escalando um problema sem soar como reclamação.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a problem is too big for one person. The contact at Google wants to help, but the contact cannot decide. So the topic must go up. In English we call this to escalate. It is normal in big projects. It is not a fight.

For Racional, this skill is very useful. The data center for Google is a large project. Many people work on it. When one point is urgent, you ask for a decision-maker. You move the topic to the next level. This keeps the project on time.

Good escalation is calm and polite. You give the reason. You ask to move up. You say thank you. With this, the contact at Google does not feel attacked. The contact feels you respect the team. A clear request is always better than a complaint.
lessons.intro:
Você vai usar três frases-âncora: dê o motivo — This is urgent.; peça para subir — Can we escalate this? / I'd like to involve your manager.; e mantenha o respeito — I appreciate your help.

Lembre: escalar é firme, nunca agressivo. Motivo + pedido + agradecimento.

lessons.title: De-escalation language — calming a hot situation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa frases simples em inglês para acalmar uma situação tensa com o Google — baixar a temperatura e voltar a buscar uma solução juntos.
lessons.overview:
In a long project, people sometimes get upset. A meeting can become tense. This is normal. The good leader knows how to de-escalate. To de-escalate means to make the situation calm again. You bring the temperature down with simple, kind words.

For Racional and Google, the relationship is long. The data center takes time. Small problems will come. When the contact at Google is unhappy, you do not push back hard. You stay calm. You say I hear you. You show you are on the same side.

De-escalation protects the partnership. After you calm the room, you look for a solution together. You focus on the next step, not the past. A calm leader keeps the trust. This is how Racional keeps good clients for many years.
lessons.intro:
Você vai usar frases curtas para acalmar: I hear you. / I'm sorry to hear that. / Let's take a step back. / We are on the same side.

Depois de acalmar, convide para a solução: Let's find a solution together.

lessons.title: Capacity planning — racks, kilowatts, density
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa vocabulário básico de planejamento de capacidade — racks, quilowatts e densidade — para falar do data center do Google em inglês simples.
lessons.overview:
A data center is full of servers. The servers sit in tall metal frames. We call them racks. Each rack uses power. We measure power in kilowatts (kW). To plan a data center, the team must know how much power each rack needs. This is capacity planning.

For the Google project, this is the heart of the design. More power per rack means more heat. The building must handle the heat and the load. Racional builds the space that supports this demand. The right footprint and good redundancy keep the data center safe.

You do not need to be an engineer to talk about this in English. You need a few clear words: rack, power load, density, to scale up. With these words, you can follow a technical meeting with Google and ask the right questions.
lessons.intro:
Você vai usar termos-âncora do data center: rack (armário de servidores), kilowatt / power load (carga de energia), density (densidade) e to scale up (aumentar a capacidade).

Frase-modelo: Each rack uses ten kilowatts. We can scale up.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião técnica com o Google sobre o data center, a equipe discute quanta energia cada rack vai usar e se o prédio aguenta a demanda.
lessons.context: Each rack uses power. We measure power in kilowatts. This is the power load. High density means more heat. The building must handle the demand. We can scale up later.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, explique ao Google quanta energia cada rack usa, fale do calor e diga que o prédio aguenta a demanda e pode crescer.

I can talk about power load.

lessons.title: The end-of-project conversation with Google — thank-yous
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você agradece e fecha um projeto com o Google em inglês simples — celebrando a parceria e deixando a porta aberta para o próximo.
lessons.overview:
Every project comes to an end. The data center is ready. The team did good work. Now it is time to say thank you. The end-of-project conversation is short, but it is very important. It is the last image the client keeps of you.

For Racional, the end is also a new start. You thank Google for the trust. You say it was a pleasure to work together. You talk about the partnership and what you learned. A warm goodbye opens the door for the next project.

This is how Racional grows. Good clients come back. Microsoft, Amazon, Google — strong relationships last for years. When you end well, you do not really say goodbye. You say let's keep in touch. The door stays open.
lessons.intro:
Você vai usar frases-âncora de agradecimento: Thank you for your trust. / It was a pleasure to work with you. / I hope we work together again.

E deixe a porta aberta: Let's keep in touch. The door is open.
lessons.situation: O projeto do data center do Google está concluído. Na reunião de encerramento, você agradece a confiança, celebra a parceria e abre caminho para a próxima frente.

lessons.title: Reference and referral — asking Google for one
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você pede, em inglês simples e educado, uma referência ou indicação ao Google — pedindo uma boa palavra para abrir portas com novos clientes.
lessons.overview:
A happy client is your best sales tool. When the project goes well, you can ask for a reference or a referral. A reference is a kind word about your work. A referral is an introduction to a new client. Both help Racional win the next project.

You must ask with care. You are proud of the result. The client is satisfied. So you ask in a simple, polite way: Would you mind giving us a reference? A good word from Google means a lot in the market.

This is how a strong track record grows. Racional has 620+ projects and 50+ years. Each happy client can recommend the company to others. A referral from a name like Google opens many doors. Do not be shy — if the work is good, ask.
lessons.intro:
Você vai usar frases-âncora educadas para pedir: Would you mind giving us a reference? / Could you recommend us? / It would mean a lot.

Lembre: você pede com orgulho do resultado e com educação.

lessons.title: ROI conversation — return on investment from Google's view
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, do retorno sobre o investimento (ROI) do ponto de vista do Google — mostrando valor, entrega no prazo e sem surpresas.
lessons.overview:
Every client wants value for the money. They ask one question: was it worth it? The answer is the return on investment, or ROI. ROI is not only money. It is also time, trust, and no problems. From Google's view, good ROI means the project paid off.

For Racional, the message is clear and strong. We deliver on time. We deliver on budget. There are no surprises. This is the value. A data center that opens on time gives Google more savings and a faster start.

When you talk about ROI, keep it simple. Use words like value, efficient, predictable, long-term. A predictable partner is a safe partner. This is why big clients choose Racional again and again. Good ROI brings the next contract.
lessons.intro:
Você vai usar frases-âncora de valor: We deliver on time and on budget. / There are no surprises. / It was worth it.

Conecte sempre ao retorno: This is good ROI for you.
lessons.situation: Na conversa de fechamento com o Google, você mostra o retorno do investimento: entrega no prazo, dentro do orçamento e sem surpresas — valor de verdade para o cliente.

lessons.title: Renewal & expansion — second site, third site with Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você propõe ao Google a continuidade da parceria — um segundo e um terceiro site —, com frases simples de renovação e expansão.
lessons.overview:
Renewal means we continue. Expansion means we do more. A good project does not end. It grows. The Racional team built one data center for Google. Now we can build the second site. This is the next step.

Google is a big client. Google grows fast. Google needs more sites in Brazil. Racional is ready. We have 50 years of work and 620 projects. We can build at scale. We can deliver again and again.

When the first project goes well, we ask for the second one. This is normal in business. We say: "We would love to build your next site." We keep the partnership growing. One good site opens the door to many future projects.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você propõe ao Google continuar e crescer juntos. Use estas âncoras: "We are ready for the next step." (Estamos prontos para o próximo passo.) e "We would love to build your second site." (Adoraríamos construir o seu segundo site.)

Lembre: site = local de obra, a palavra que o Google usa. Proponha o próximo passo enquanto a confiança está alta.
lessons.situation: O primeiro data center foi entregue. Em uma conversa estratégica, você sugere ao Google construir um segundo e até um terceiro site com a Racional.
